# Industrial ATLAS: reusable components and articulation

The canonical model is `fixtures/Canonical/AssemblyInterfaces/IndustrialAtlas/atlas-industrial.firmament`.
Its root now assembles reusable base, upper arm, forearm, and jaw components through
published mounting frames. Joint covers and cover fasteners own their complete
local construction; keyed mounting sites instantiate them. The housing SectionChain
geometry remains unchanged. Materials and appearances are authored in the source.
Assembly GLB export now forwards those occurrence appearances to the existing
serializer, matching USD and the interactive display instead of emitting default grey.

The model retains 60 visible bodies and 24 shared geometry definitions. Five
top-level interfaces replace the former 59 individually seated relationships:
Shoulder, Elbow, WristMount, GripLeft, and GripRight. The wrist is fixed; the other
four interfaces admit motion. Gripper body and jaw components are direct articulated
occurrences, avoiding an unplaced organizational container.

## Corrected construction defects

| Feature | Previous construction | Current construction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cover standoffs | 15 mm shafts extended 3 mm into the cover plates | 12 mm shafts meet the underside; heads meet the outer face |
| Jaw roots | Began at X=13 mm, 17 mm inside the 30 mm body | Begin at the body's X=30 mm front face |
| Grip pads | Extruded upward from the jaws | Rotated inward and seated on the opposing jaw faces |

At zero jaw travel, the modeled pads have a 21 mm gap. Positive GripLeft and
GripRight states open their respective jaws outward. Pose evaluation changes
occurrence frames while reusing the same geometry definitions; the pads retain
their local relationship to the jaws.

`IndustrialAtlasModernizationTests` checks transformed native display bounds for
these contacts and clearances, and checks rigid child frames and jaw-to-body
relationships in two articulated poses. USD and GLB tests also exercise the real
display/export paths. Published frame origins use dimension-checked length
arithmetic, including `H / 2`, rather than duplicated height literals.

## Inspect and export

```powershell
dotnet Aetheris.CLI/bin/Release/net10.0/aetheris.dll asm inspect fixtures/Canonical/AssemblyInterfaces/IndustrialAtlas/atlas-industrial.firmament --json
dotnet Aetheris.CLI/bin/Release/net10.0/aetheris.dll asm export-glb fixtures/Canonical/AssemblyInterfaces/IndustrialAtlas/atlas-industrial.firmament artifacts/local/atlas.glb --state Shoulder=-65 --state Elbow=100 --state GripLeft=4 --state GripRight=4 --json
```

Helios copies these canonical modules with source hashes and generates its ATLAS
SVG from the native placed topology edges at that same presentation pose.

This is a nominal presentation assembly, not a manufacturing or robotics release.
The assertions qualify the specific cover and gripper repairs; they do not establish
global collision freedom. Curved drive/housing internals remain simplified. The
current exact solid-interference checker admits convex planar bodies and cannot
qualify all of this model's curved geometry.

Current native qualification: Release solution build succeeded; the fast core lane
passed 1,058 tests and the full serial solution lane passed 4,391 tests across
21 suites, with zero failures or skips. STEP export/reimport retained 24 definitions,
60 bodies and 36 repeated instances. Blender 5.2.2 imported the posed GLB with
60 mesh objects and 24 shared mesh datablocks, and passed normal/transform checks.
Generated reports, STEP/USD/GLB files and render evidence are under ignored
`artifacts/local/atlas-modernization/`.

The synchronized ten-module Helios example also passed the production Chromium
workflow: intact source, native Worker build, visible geometry, hierarchy selection
and inspector. It reported 24 definitions, 113 occurrences, zero diagnostics and
zero page errors. The measured Worker build was 18.6 seconds in this local run;
this is a workflow sample, not a benchmark.
The complete refreshed browser run passed eight workflows, including all five
examples and gallery/theme behavior; all 37 Helios unit tests also passed.

docs/public/drawing-notes.md.title: Reading engineering drawings with Drawing Notes
docs/public/drawing-notes.md.markdown:
# Reading engineering drawings with Drawing Notes

Aetheris Drawing Notes is scratch paper for an engineer or agent reading a dense PDF. The PDF remains authority. A note records an interpretation, its confidence, and the exact page-space rectangle that led to it; it is not CAD truth and is never silently promoted into geometry.

Drawing Notes is deliberately separate from BRep, STEP, Firmament lowering, OCR, and automatic dimension inference. It works when the reader can see a value and its leaders, highlight that source area, and state the relationship explicitly.

## Start a notebook

```powershell
aetheris drawing inspect drawing.pdf --json
aetheris drawing notes create drawing.pdf --out notes `
  --name "Fixture - Drawing Notes" `
  --title "Aetheris Drawing Notes Synthetic Fixture" `
  --sheets "SHEET 1 OF 1" `
  --json
```

The project contains `drawing-notes.json`, an initial `drawing-notes.md`, and local browser UI assets. It records the source SHA-256, page count and sizes, visible metadata supplied by the reader, and the packaged PDF renderer identity. It does not copy the PDF.

Coordinates are PDF page-space points (`1/72 inch`) with a top-left origin. A rectangle is `x,y,width,height`. This makes annotations independent of monitor resolution and zoom.

## Work locally

Create a named view, its local datum, a dimension, and the relationship between them:

```powershell
$project = "notes/drawing-notes.json"

aetheris drawing notes add-region $project `
  --id DetailD --name "Detail D" --page 1 `
  --bounds "465,60,180,200" --type Detail

aetheris drawing notes add-note $project `
  --id DetailD.Origin --label "Detail D local origin" `
  --category Datum --page 1 --bounds "485,80,25,160" `
  --region DetailD --confidence High

aetheris drawing notes add-dimension $project `
  --id Camera1.CenterX --label "Camera 1 center X" `
  --value "25.00 mm" --type Coordinate --axis X `
  --page 1 --bounds "510,95,80,20" --region DetailD `
  --class ProductGeometry --confidence High

aetheris drawing notes add-relation $project `
  --id Camera1.CenterX.FromDetailD `
  --from Camera1.CenterX --to DetailD.Origin `
  --kind ReferencedFrom
```

Use stable semantic labels such as `ProductBody`, `RearCamera1`, or `DetailD.Origin`. Preserve drawing wording in `--original-text`; put your interpretation in `--note` or `--interpretation`. Use `--aliases "REAR CAMERA 1,Camera 1"` for distinct source labels that name the same notebook feature.

Supported relation kinds are `Targets`, `ReferencedFrom`, `LocatedIn`, `DetailOf`, `SectionOf`, `KeepoutFor`, `CoordinateIn`, and `RelatedTo`. For example, use `KeepoutFor` rather than an open-ended synonym such as `AppliesTo`; the bounded vocabulary keeps graph exports consistent.

Do not force uncertainty into a known type. Use `Unknown`, `Low`, or `Unresolved`, and add a first-class `Question` note. A camera field-of-view cone or material exclusion region should be classified as `SensorKeepout`, `AccessoryKeepout`, or `MaterialRestriction`, not `ProductGeometry`.

## Highlight and crop

The browser UI renders PDF pages, thumbnails and crops with locally bundled PDF.js. It works offline and does not require PDFium, Skia, Poppler or a CDN. Select a note or drag a rectangle, then click **Export crop** to download its PNG and `.crop.json` source metadata (allow multiple downloads if your browser asks).

For headless automation, explicitly select an external Poppler `pdftoppm` executable. Aetheris does not install or bundle it. Omitting the renderer produces `drawing-renderer-required`; inspection, notes and vector drawing generation need no native backend:

```powershell
$renderer = "C:/tools/poppler/bin/pdftoppm.exe" # or /usr/bin/pdftoppm
aetheris drawing render drawing.pdf --page 1 --out page-1.png --dpi 240 --renderer $renderer
aetheris drawing crop drawing.pdf --page 1 `
  --bounds "465,60,180,200" --name DetailD `
  --out notes/crops/p01-detail-d.png --dpi 300 --renderer $renderer
```

Crop coordinates are relative to the top-left of the **rotated, visible CropBox**, in physical PDF points (1/72 inch, including UserUnit). Raster boundaries round outward to whole pixels at the selected DPI; the sidecar keeps the requested page-space bounds. The browser checks the source hash and page dimensions before enabling annotation. Older notebooks retain their renderer provenance; incompatible coordinates require explicit reconciliation.

Every crop receives a `.crop.json` sidecar containing its page, source bounds, document hash, renderer, and DPI. The PNG is a rendering of the real source area, not an OCR redraw.

For interactive work, launch the local browser UI:

```powershell
aetheris drawing notes serve notes/drawing-notes.json `
  --source drawing.pdf --port 4178
```

The UI provides pages and regions on the left, a pan/zoom PDF rendering with overlays in the center, note and relation editing on the right, and a textual relationship tree. Drag a rectangle and press `D` for a dimension, `V` for a view, or `Q` for a question. The server checks the PDF hash on load and save; UI and CLI persist the same model.

## Export and hand off

```powershell
aetheris drawing notes validate notes/drawing-notes.json `
  --source drawing.pdf --json

aetheris drawing notes export notes/drawing-notes.json `
  --format markdown --out notes/drawing-notes.md
```

JSON retains the complete graph. Markdown is the compact LLM handoff. Both are byte-stable for the same project and contain no generated timestamp. Filters keep downstream context bounded:

```powershell
--page 3
--region DetailD
--class ProductGeometry
--unresolved
```

Validation reports likely duplicate source annotations without merging them. Conflicting meanings assigned to the same page rectangle remain explicit review findings. A changed PDF produces `drawing-source-hash-mismatch` rather than silently attaching old notes to a new revision.

The repository-owned qualification fixture is [`synthetic-engineering-drawing.pdf`](../../fixtures/DrawingNotes/synthetic-engineering-drawing.pdf). It includes a front and side view, two global datums, a detail-local datum, dimensions, a section, a functional keepout, and an unresolved question. Regenerate it with `fixtures/DrawingNotes/generate_synthetic.py`.

## Handoff discipline

Give a downstream CAD agent both the original PDF and exported Markdown. Ask it to consume high-confidence `ProductGeometry` notes first, keep local datums distinct, and revisit every low/unresolved item in the source. Do not ask it to model keepout cones as product solids. When a leader or section association is ambiguous, the correct notebook entry is a cited question, not an invented constraint.

docs/public/drawings.md.title: Generate dimensioned engineering drawings
docs/public/drawings.md.markdown:
# Generate dimensioned engineering drawings

A drawing must define the nominal part without requiring its CAD file or measuring
its picture. The compiler distinguishes nominal geometry coverage, specified
limits, material and actual process qualification. Searchable PDF text and a clean
layout are presentation checks, not manufacturing approval.

Helios exposes PDF, SVG and PPTX in **Export** for supported parts, using this same
dimension planner. Selecting several formats downloads a ZIP. The browser projects
the current compiled STEP and checks that authored PMI has not disappeared; it does
not invent material, tolerances or signoffs. Use the authoring workflow below to
supply those requirements. Assembly/Scene automatic drawings are not exposed there.

## Generate a dimensioned plate

```powershell
aetheris drawing generate fixtures/Regression/DrawingGeneration/inspection-plate.firmament --out-dir artifacts/local/drawing/inspection-plate --linear-tolerance 0.1 --angular-tolerance 0.5 --material "6061-T6 aluminium" --drawn-by "Codex (AI)" --date 2026-10-18 --json
```

`generate` also accepts `.step` / `.stp`. The default output directory is
`artifacts/local/drawing/<source-name>`. PDF, SVG, editable PPTX, Drawing IR and a
validation report share the same dimension plan. The compiler preserves source and
body geometry. Generation options are explicit drawing authoring inputs; they do
not rewrite the part or add these requirements to its AP242 PMI.

The current complete-definition family is an axis-aligned rectangular plate/box
with disjoint circular Z-through holes. Recognition accounts for every face,
rectangular stock boundary, full circular opening and cylinder seam. Fillets,
chamfers, blind holes, counterbores, nonrectangular outlines, oblique holes and other
families require an authored complete drawing until their dimension planners are
qualified. They fail automatic generation with `drawing-definition-incomplete`;
a sampled bounding box is never used to claim complete dimensions.

The [code-native bracket rehearsal](code-native-bracket.md) demonstrates the
authored route for a traced L outline with a countersunk through hole. Its final
PDF is independently reconstructed and compared with STEP for two parameter sets.
That bounded authoring helper does not extend the automatic recognition family.

A qualified plate receives:

- Exact controlling width and height dimensions, and thickness on an aligned edge
  view. These values come from stock planes, not sampled display bounds.
- Hole center marks and IDs, a coordinate schedule from the left and bottom
  finished edges, entry-face/orientation information, and explicit THRU extents.
  Visible X0 and Y0 leaders identify those zero edges; `(0,0)` marks their
  intersection on the top face. The table's X and Y headers each state their
  bilateral tolerance, for example `X ±0.1` and `Y ±0.1` (mm).
- Grouped diameter/limit callouts only when size, limits and extent agree.
  Original PMI names, targets and face identities remain in provenance.
- A datum indication on the actual associated plane in a useful view. Coordinate
  edge references do not silently create extra GD&T datums.
- Light internal hole-wall lines in the side view, rather than treating a
  cylinder's parameter seam as an exterior edge.

Coordinates are independent baseline dimensions. No row/column pattern is guessed
from an apparently regular picture. Irregular coordinates remain individual values.
Hole schedules paginate beyond twelve rows; more than four distinct size/limit
groups currently requires authored sheet allocation. Crowded labels or oversized
values reject instead of clipping, shrinking or omitting engineering information.

## Tolerances and manufacturing authority

`--linear-tolerance <mm>` explicitly specifies bilateral stock-size and X/Y
coordinate limits. `--angular-tolerance <degrees>` specifies the general angular
allowance. `--material <name>` supplies the material for the drawing. These are
not defaults and never override existing diameter PMI.

Each table coordinate is measured from its marked zero edge with its own ± limit;
the two limits define independent Cartesian intervals, not a circular GD&T position
zone. X0/Y0 are drawing coordinate references, distinct from authored datum PMI
such as A. They do not silently add B/C datum requirements to the source or AP242.
An unspecified coordinate tolerance prints `TOL?` in each header and remains an
incomplete requirement.

Without these inputs, nominal dimensions are still complete for a recognized part,
but the sheet prominently identifies missing requirements and is not for
manufacture. Missing hole diameter tolerances remain missing as well. JSON reports
`nominalGeometryComplete`, `dimensionalTolerancesComplete`, `materialSpecified`,
`processCapabilityVerified` and `missingRequirements` independently. Authored
Drawing compilation has no automatic coverage assessment; its evidence remains
unassessed rather than implicitly complete.

The planner checks positive stock/diameter intervals and screens remaining hole
webs against Cartesian entry-center limits and cylinder-axis lean on ideal
orthogonal stock. The evidence records that assumption. This bounded interference
screen does not qualify stock form, general angular stacks, surface finish,
inspection uncertainty, a manufacturing process or functional fit. It is not
permission to declare a part manufacture-ready.

For the example, the retained source diameter limits are 3.98-4.05 mm. Those are
source requirements, not a claim that ordinary drilling will meet them, nor an M4
clearance-fit designation. A suitable finishing/inspection process must be agreed.
See the material/process-dependent [Protolabs machining capability table](https://www.protolabs.com/services/cnc-machining/precision-machining-tolerances/).

Conflicting diameter, depth or quantity PMI rejects. Unknown dimension kinds,
unlocated PMI and unqualified AP242 families also reject; semantic requirements
cannot disappear because nominal geometry looks plausible. Automatic PMI readback
currently admits the existing Aetheris millimetre subset, not universal third-party
AP242 PMI. Use multiline fields inside source PMI declarations; some semicolon
forms remain frontend debt.

## Explicit reference visualization

```powershell
aetheris drawing generate model.step --reference-only --out-dir artifacts/local/drawing/reference --json
```

This retains the earlier PMI/wireframe review sheets with approximate `REF`
envelopes. Sheets are marked **REFERENCE ONLY / NOT FOR MANUFACTURE**, and nominal
completeness is false. Manufacturing generation options are rejected in this mode.
Unsupported wireframe geometry also reports a named error. A reference view is not
a substitute for complete dimensions.

## Authored drawings and formats

`aetheris drawing compile <drawing.firmament> --out-dir <directory>` retains explicit
Drawing/Templates, selected views, metadata Records, design tables, Assembly BOMs
and reviews. `generate` delegates a source's explicit Drawing declaration to that
owner. Automatic generation options cannot silently alter an authored drawing.

Within an authored View, `HiddenLines: Wireframe` uses the shared trimmed BRep
wireframe sampler. `VisibleOnly` and `VisibleAndHidden` retain existing bounded
occlusion behavior. Wireframe can show rear geometry but cannot replace dimensions
or supply an unstated hole depth.

PDF uses embedded Inter, searchable text and vector strokes. SVG, React and editable
PPTX consume the same annotation geometry and table data. PPTX requires Inter in the
editor for matching metrics. Text/leader/model and table keepouts are checked;
layout errors reject. DXF and general automatic section/detail/Assembly planning
remain separate work. No general ISO/ASME certification is claimed.

## Title table and traceability

Every sheet has a merged-cell title table for title/identity, material, part number,
revision, scale, units, sheet and status. Separate Drawn / Checked / Approved names
and dates are explicit paired inputs:

- `--drawn-by <name> --date <yyyy-MM-dd>`
- `--checked-by <name> --checked-date <yyyy-MM-dd>`
- `--approved-by <name> --approved-date <yyyy-MM-dd>`

These flags also work with `drawing compile`. The authored metadata Record can
supply `DrawnBy`/`DrawnDate`, `CheckedBy`/`CheckedDate` and
`ApprovedBy`/`ApprovedDate`; legacy `Author`/`Date` remain the Drawn fallback.
Unperformed reviews remain blank. Preparation credit, including AI assistance,
is traceability rather than a digital signature or automatic engineering approval.

## Reconstruction qualification

The regression reader `fixtures/Regression/DrawingGeneration/reconstruct_from_pdf.py`
reads only visible PDF dimensions and tables, writes a fresh Firmament source and
can compile it through the real CLI. It does not read the original source, Drawing
IR or embedded attachments. Compare that frozen reconstruction with the original
only afterward. The witness is bounded to this plate convention, not general OCR
or an automatic engineering reviewer.

The layout follows the completeness and nonredundancy principles in
[MIT's engineering drawing guide](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/2-007-design-and-manufacturing-i-spring-2009/pages/related-resources/drawing_and_sketching/).

docs/public/experimental/garments/armhol.title: Garment armhole experiment
docs/public/experimental/garments/armhol.markdown:
# Garment armhole experiment

> **Experimental.** Garment work is research, not part of the supported product. Its APIs, syntax and results may change or be withdrawn. See [experimental modules](../README.md).

Date: 2026-10-11. This follows [temporary Concept fitting](temporary-fitting.md).
**The final A-pose drape improves from 87.12% to 9.23% peak strain. The complete
dressing sequence remains unqualified because fitting and midpoint checkpoints
still exceed the unchanged 15% strain limit.**

## Controlled inputs

All trials retain the imported GarmentCode cut, raised flat arrangement, 611
vertices, 992 triangles, six seams and zero permanent pins. The control uses
Rest-pose sewing and a collar guide at measured shoulder height plus 45mm,
compliance 1e-8, released after 20 settling frames. Each run has 30 gravity-free
sewing frames, 60 fitting frames, eight substeps and 24 structural iterations.
The transition adds 30 motion frames and 60 wearing frames.

Body SHA-256:
`0a0ad03e86447fc56448940c7aa56b54ea6683e8a874f833e01fd56a65a2d0e5`.
Cloth content key, including arrangement and fabric:
`42C204F0BE495216B6CB3C2C3087EC8C786135D3EE71FE2D465BCFB4D468BA8B`.
Warp/weft compliance remains 1e-8 and diagonal compliance 4e-8. These are
authoring values, not calibrated textile measurements. No pattern dimension,
clearance, acceptance gate or body skin weight was adjusted.

## Contact isolation

`scripts/inspect-garment-strain.cs` recompiles the actual source, checks its hash
against the retained `garment.json`, verifies FigureFit body artifact hashes
and validates snapshot topology/material identity. It reconstructs the authored
final body pose through the existing humanoid solver. It reports semantic edge
membership, material coordinates and body samples for the eight worst links.
It runs five replay frames through `ClothSolver3D` with zero initial velocity
and zero gravity, varying contact and substeps with 24 iterations.

The original final snapshot has 87.119% strain and 0.00872mm sampled penetration.
Its worst link is right-back armhole 336/337, rest length 14.275mm. Its endpoints
are 6.002mm and 7.792mm from the body. Interior triangle samples and connected
constraints also act on them; endpoint distance alone cannot justify disabling
contact.

| Contact | Substeps | Peak strain after five frames | Penetration against original body | Seam gap |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Enabled | 8 | 80.663% | 0.748mm | 1.968mm |
| Enabled | 32 | 85.598% | 0.766mm | 1.734mm |
| Disabled | 8 | 12.490% | 61.136mm | 0.548mm |
| Disabled | 32 | 0.925% | 95.169mm | 0.064mm |

The sewn material can relax when contact is removed, but then enters the body.
More substeps with contact enabled do not repair this control. This implicates
the fitted arrangement and contact/structural conflict; it does not establish
pattern sizing or the discrete contact algorithm as the sole root cause.
Contact-disabled snapshots are diagnostic failures, never accepted fits.

## Declarative fitting and motion

Changing only the fitting pose to TPose reduces final strain to 22.309%, seam
gap to 0.820mm and sampled penetration to 0.000128mm. The guide is released,
with 40 unsupported fitting frames. The worst remaining edge is right-back
armhole 331/332, rest length 10.770mm; the next reported outlier is 9.614%.

Then the same fitted garment follows the existing half-second SmoothStep
transition from TPose to APose, followed by 60 wearing frames:

| Checkpoint | Peak strain | Seam gap | Sampled penetration | Body surface admissible |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Fitting | 22.309% | 0.820mm | 0.000128mm | Yes |
| Midpoint | 22.372% | 1.111mm | 0.000118mm | Yes |
| Wearing | 9.228% | 1.132mm | 0.0000247mm | Yes |

The final garment has no permanent pins or active guides. Final and midpoint
replay checks are exact. Maximum measured body travel per substep is 4.088mm;
this is a diagnostic, not CCD certification. The final wearing snapshot passes
the existing strain/seam/contact gates. **The CLI correctly reports the whole
sequence as failed** because its fitting and midpoint strain still exceeds 15%.
No checkpoint is exempted and no limit is weakened.
The final three wearing samples also satisfy the existing stationary/gate
predicate, with final maximum speed 0.000799m/s. This is bounded settling
evidence, not proof for arbitrary motion.

This isolates the remaining blocker to startup fitting near the right-back
armhole, rather than final A-pose equilibrium or collar retention. A further
startup-arrangement/contact investigation is required before qualifying the
complete sequence. Adding a strain cap that merely transfers the error into
penetration or seam gaps would not resolve it.

The actual front/side/back renders show less armhole bunching than the Rest-pose
control. They still show a coarse, somewhat stiff silhouette and a projecting
neckline; this is a foundation specimen, not a finished textile model. Blender
only presents exported solver meshes, with no fitting, subdivision or cloth sim.

## Reusable source and evidence

`fixtures/Canonical/Garment/garmentcode-dress-guided.firmament` composes existing
Concept measurements, an erased collar plane, named boundary guides, release,
and declarative poses. The original bind skeleton and cut are preserved. A
source regression checks this composition. CLI compilation with the actual
body also confirms the same cloth key, guide command and motion program.

The checked-in specimen SHA-256 is
`6c672fced4ad4a1c210466ed9c5bc8402068ccfbdc13ec812579343bd5f55d9a`.
Experimental source files have different comments; each retained artifact
records its own source hash. Outputs live in
`artifacts/local/garment/armhole-round/`: `strain-inspection.json`,
`wearing-inspection.json`, `tpose-60/`, `transition-60/`, and `specimen/`.
Renders are under `artifacts/local/garment/renders/armhole-round-wearing/wearing/`.

```powershell
dotnet run -c Release scripts/inspect-garment-strain.cs -- `
  artifacts/local/garment/fitting-round/anatolia-guided-high.firmament `
  artifacts/local/humanoid-production/antonia.gameplay-body.json `
  artifacts/local/garment/fitting-round/high-60/garment.json `
  artifacts/local/garment/armhole-round/strain-inspection.json

dotnet Aetheris.CLI/bin/Release/net10.0/aetheris.dll garment drape `
  fixtures/Canonical/Garment/garmentcode-dress-guided.firmament `
  --body artifacts/local/humanoid-production/antonia.gameplay-body.json `
  --ticks 60 --substeps 8 --iterations 24 `
  --out-dir artifacts/local/garment/armhole-round/reproduced --json
```

Use Release for replay probes; Debug is substantially slower. The helper accepts
a retained final snapshot with a FigureFit binding, not an intermediate OBJ.
Guides/body contact remain CPU capabilities. This does not qualify GPU draping,
friction, garment self-contact or continuous collision safety. No new dependency
or third-party solver was adopted. GarmentCode remains MIT-credited to Maria
Korosteleva; see pinned licenses and [import provenance](garmentcode.md).

## Validation

The idle serial Release Aetheris solution build passed with zero errors and
five existing WebAssembly SQLite interop warnings. The complete solution test
lane passed 4,518 tests, including 2,109 Firmament tests and 1,195 kernel tests.
The new source regression composes the known cut, temporary guides and pose
motion without changing cloth identity or the original bind skeleton. The
generated STEP test output was restored after the lane.

The inspection helper ran against both the original Rest snapshot and the
authored final A-pose snapshot; its recomputed metrics match the retained drape.
An equivalent UTF-8 BOM source produced identical compiler identity and replay
results. A mismatched source and attempted input overwrite were rejected, with
no diagnostic report written. Logs and probe reports are retained under
`artifacts/local/garment/armhole-round/`.

The Release Aurelian consumer solution built with zero warnings/errors and its
complete serial test lane passed 1,218 tests, with the installed Naga selected
through `AURELIAN_NAGA`. Copeland logs are
`artifacts/aurelian-beacon3d/garment-armhole-{build,tests}.log`.
This proves consumer regression compatibility, not GPU body-contact support or
native game presentation of this garment. No Copeland source was changed in
this round.

docs/public/experimental/garments/drapin.markdown:
# Garment draping research: improving the known-pattern baseline

> **Experimental.** Garment work is research, not part of the supported product. Its APIs, syntax and results may change or be withdrawn. See [experimental modules](../README.md).

Research date: 2026-10-10. This report compares current source and retained drapes
with primary research. It proposes experiments; it does not qualify a new solver
or a production garment. No runtime, material, source cut or acceptance threshold
was changed during this research turn.

Implementation follow-up (2026-10-11):
[panel meshing and settling experiment](meshing-settling-experiment.md)
implements the mesh and convergence instrumentation, retains the failed drapes,
and isolates the sewing/contact initialization conflict. The measurements below
describe the original research baseline, not the new mesh.

## Findings from the actual artifacts

The [GarmentCode workflow](garmentcode.md) removed uncertainty about the reference
cut and curve interchange. A read-only audit of the two Anatolia controls gives
the following measurements. Both contain the same rest mesh: 1,234 vertices,
2,244 triangles and 3,474 unique triangle edges.

| Measurement | Original arrangement | Arrangement raised 100mm |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Maximum edge tensile strain | 42.351% | 50.823% |
| 95th percentile edge tensile strain | 3.939% | 1.451% |
| Number of edges above 15% | 23 | 11 |
| Maximum triangle principal tensile strain | 46.240% | 51.364% |
| Rest-area fraction above 15% principal tensile strain | 1.407% | 0.145% |

The raised control's worst link is vertices 1210/1214: 1.775mm rest length and
0.902mm extension. The original control's worst link is much longer, 31.646mm,
so short links are not a complete explanation of both failures. The improvement
in the bulk distribution also does not override the failed peak-strain gate.

Rest-mesh quality is poor in more than one location:

- Minimum edge length: 1.409mm; median: 41.434mm; maximum: 56.916mm.
- Minimum triangle angle: 1.790 degrees. 332 triangles (14.8%) have an angle
  below 5 degrees; 554 (24.7%) are below 10 degrees.
- Maximum/minimum area-lumped vertex mass ratio: 110.74.
- Under the current edge classifier: 208 warp links, 336 weft links and
  2,930 diagonal links (84.3%).

`GarmentPanelMesher` already calls the shared `PlanarMeshQuality.Improve` for
Delaunay edge flips. It then bisects overlong edges. That controls maximum edge
length, but does not provide shape refinement, a minimum angle or a controlled
minimum feature size. Merely adding another edge-flip pass is not the proposed fix.

`ClothCompiler3D` assigns warp/weft stiffness only to almost exactly axis-aligned
material edges; all other directions receive diagonal stiffness. These are
authoring compliances, not a calibrated continuum textile model. Improving
triangulation without checking this dependency could change the apparent fabric.

The current drape uses eight substeps and 24 structural iterations per frame,
one contact pass per iteration, 30 gravity-free sewing frames and a fixed number
of settling frames. The retained controls used 30 settling frames: 0.5 seconds
at 60Hz. There is no equilibrium stopping test in this path. Body contacts use
nearest-surface vertex and triangle-sample projections without friction or CCD.
The default bending model is already boundary-corrected vertex bending; it is
not necessary to reintroduce the earlier Better Bending foundation.

## Research that maps to these gaps

**GarmentCodeData, ECCV 2024.** Their pipeline uses a connected box mesh, matched
samples on paired sewing boundaries, constrained Delaunay panel meshing and
gravity-free initialization. It adds semantic body-part handling, temporary
half-space attachments and a static-equilibrium check. Collar guides are released
before the final drape. This supports treating dressing initialization as an
explicit stage rather than expecting unconstrained gravity to find the intended
placement. [Paper, sections 3.4 and appendix C](https://arxiv.org/html/2405.17609v2).
The pinned MIT wrapper also enables body/fabric friction and schedules attachment
release; its parameters are not portable fabric units for Aetheris.

**Quality triangulation.** Shape and size criteria are distinct. Delaunay
refinement inserts vertices to improve triangle shape; flips alone cannot always
repair a bad point distribution. Acute authored boundaries constrain achievable
angles, so a global minimum-angle promise would be incorrect.
[CGAL Mesh_2 documentation](https://doc.cgal.org/latest/Mesh_2/index.html).

**Physics-inspired Estimation of Optimal Cloth Mesh Resolution, SIGGRAPH 2025.**
Uses material properties and boundary conditions to choose spatially varying
resolution, with smooth transitions between fine and coarse regions. Useful
later for collar/seam/contact sizing maps. We first need a sound material model
and a quality mesher; globally shrinking `meshSize` is not an equivalent method.
[Author's project](https://wanghmin.github.io/publication/zhang-2025-pie/).

**Small Steps in Physics Simulation, SCA 2019.** Shows advantages of spending an
XPBD budget on smaller steps rather than many iterations in a larger step. We
already substep, but have not measured the appropriate split for sewn garments.
This is a cheap controlled convergence experiment, not a claimed cure for
invalid initialization. [Author's paper](https://mmacklin.com/smallsteps.pdf).

**Strain Based Dynamics, SCA 2014.** Controls material strain directions
independently of mesh edge directions and separates stretch from shear. It is a
particularly direct match to the present warp/weft/diagonal classification gap.
Adapting its constraints to XPBD still requires area/energy normalization and
verification; the original PBD stiffness parameters are not physical moduli.
[Author's paper](https://matthias-research.github.io/pages/publications/strainBasedDynamics.pdf).

**Automatic Digital Garment Initialization, SIGGRAPH 2024.** Treats panel
arrangement as its own phased selection/placement problem. Its hybrid classifier
and optimizer need not become a dependency: Firmament can supply the panel roles,
body landmarks and target frames explicitly, reducing ambiguity at authoring time.
That is our proposed adaptation, not a reproduction of their method.
[Author's project](https://wanghmin.github.io/publication/liu-2024-adg/).

**OGC, AVBD and C-IPC.** OGC's local contact and movement bounds are attractive
for Vulkan. Aetheris already has an OGC-inspired foundation, but its exhaustive
candidate admission stops at 128 vertices; the 1,234-vertex dress has offset
self-contact disabled. We need a conservative accelerated candidate search and
seam-aware exclusions before garment-scale use. Initial collision recovery is
distinct from preventing new collisions.
[OGC project](https://ankachan.github.io/Projects/OGC/).
AVBD addresses hard constraints and stiffness ratios, but the existing scalar
probe does not demonstrate a garment advantage over XPBD. Keep it as a later
comparison on identical energies and contacts. [AVBD project](https://graphics.cs.utah.edu/research/projects/avbd/).
C-IPC offers coupled strain limits, thickness and friction with strong contact
handling; use it as a reference for validation and possible offline comparison,
rather than adding its global solve to the current small milestone.
[C-IPC project](https://ipc-sim.github.io/C-IPC/).

**Better Bending, SIGGRAPH 2026.** Retain analytic, refinement and rotated-mesh
tests when changing meshing or materials; a convincing dress render cannot
establish convergence. The existing boundary-corrected bending implementation
does not qualify sharp folds, shaped rest states or every irregular mesh.
[Author's project](https://zhenchen-jay.github.io/publication/betterbending/).

## Recommended experiment order

Each experiment starts from the same retained cut, body and explicitly named
arrangement. Change one variable group at a time. Preserve failed runs and the
existing 15% peak strain, 10mm seam-gap and 5mm sampled-penetration limits.

1. **Quality panel meshing in the existing owner.** Keep analytic profiles and
   named spans authoritative. Use bounded shape refinement/interior point
   distribution plus size control. Improve curve sampling with arc-length and
   geometric-error criteria instead of unconditional minimum sample counts.
   Preserve authored endpoints, seam direction and ease. Compare triangle
   angles, area/mass ratios, vertex count, pattern area and actual drape residuals.
   Do not delete a legitimate short authored feature to improve a statistic.
   Target roughly 20-degree angles where the boundary permits, with explicit
   exceptions and failure diagnostics rather than an unconditional guarantee.
2. **Establish settling convergence.** Compare 30, 120 and 600 settling frames
   on the current owner before selecting a new default. Record residual and
   velocity histories. Then compare substep/iteration splits `(8,24)`, `(16,12)`,
   `(32,6)` and `(64,3)`: all have 192 structural passes per frame. Contact work
   and total wall time still need measurement; equal pass counts are not equal
   cost. A bounded equilibrium check should include seam/strain/contact residuals
   and motion, since high damping can make a wrong solution appear stationary.
3. **Explicit temporary fitting guides.** Use existing figure landmarks and
   collar edge identities to author soft half-space guides. Release them during
   the settling phase, then require an unsupported final equilibrium. Avoid
   permanently fixing collar vertices in world space. Retain guide identity,
   active duration, force/residual and release evidence. Drive the existing
   T-to-A pose transition only after the static control qualifies.
4. **Material-space triangle strain.** Compile rest inverses, area weights,
   grain directions and conflict-free rows once. Project warp, weft and shear
   through the existing XPBD schedule. Verify flat-patch stretch/shear, rotation
   of triangulation relative to grain, rigid-motion invariance and mesh refinement.
   Keep edge springs as a named experimental control; do not call their settings
   measured fabric constants. A strain limiter must report residuals and contact
   conflicts rather than silently clamping positions after contact.
5. **Friction and scalable self-contact.** Add controlled tangential response
   with static/sliding tests and moving-body-relative velocities. Do not use high
   friction to hold an incorrectly placed dress. Extend the existing offset
   narrowphase with conservative candidates and seam-aware neighborhoods; compare
   candidate coverage against exhaustive small cases. GPU bounds, reductions and
   projections belong in real `.v.ts`; retain CPU reference agreement and replay.

Shared seam sampling is a useful companion to meshing: derive paired stations
from both analytic lengths, ease and landmarks before triangulation. Keep
weighted constraints for unequal discretizations. Do not naively weld vertices
and replace the flat material charts with their 3D arrangement. If introducing
joined simulation topology, preserve per-triangle rest charts and explicit seam
behavior, including contact exclusions and bending across the join.

The first implementation milestone should cover steps 1-3 on this one dress.
Step 4 is the next material-model milestone; step 5 is needed before layered
outfits and demanding animation. These priorities are engineering inferences
from the measured failures, not demonstrated improvements from new simulations.

## Evidence, reproduction and licensing

Local audit outputs are ignored under `artifacts/local/garment/research/`:
`audit-garment-mesh.py`, `mesh-audit.json` and `mesh-audit.png`. The audit reads
retained `garment.json`; it does not step, remesh, pin or modify either garment.
It computes unique-edge strain, minimum triangle angles, area-lumped masses and
the singular values of each triangle's 3-by-2 deformation gradient. Principal
strain is an additional diagnostic, not a replacement acceptance metric.
The panel plot separates each material chart; chart locations are not drape
placements. Largest edge-strain differences from the runtime reports are below
0.00001 in strain, consistent with serialized float precision.
Analytic checks also passed: translating/rotating the rest mesh produces zero
edge and principal tensile strain within 1e-9; applying uniform scale 1.1 gives
0.1 for both. These validate the audit calculation, not the garment solver.

```powershell
& artifacts/local/garment/research/venv/Scripts/python.exe `
  artifacts/local/garment/research/audit-garment-mesh.py `
  artifacts/local/garment/garmentcode-dress/antonia-reference-sizing/garment.json `
  artifacts/local/garment/garmentcode-dress/anatolia-raised/garment.json `
  --output artifacts/local/garment/research/mesh-audit.json `
  --plot artifacts/local/garment/research/mesh-audit.png
```

The script uses the existing research venv's NumPy/Matplotlib. No packages or
tools were installed this turn. Artifact hashes are retained in `mesh-audit.json`:
original `24f0a427d2cbf270628ad4fdb1e556e8ecb1c0e6d85a81cfd976664039e4de8a`,
raised `55419de373c21bd0e1d2246e459755504a9350ab0b7486e177729dd0cda3dd87`.
GarmentCode source inspected is pinned to
`d449629979028123a5c4dc9e732a2ec19b7fce31`. No new simulator was executed;
the existing drapes remain failed and no new build/test qualification is claimed.

GarmentCode's MIT license does not cover every associated project. The separate
[NvidiaWarp-GarmentCode license](https://github.com/maria-korosteleva/NvidiaWarp-GarmentCode/blob/main/LICENSE.md)
contains a research/evaluation-only use limitation in section 3.3. Do not copy
that fork into the production runtime under the assumption that it is MIT.
This review adopted no fork code or new dependency. Paper-inspired changes
should remain in the existing Aetheris/Aurelian owners with attribution and
independent validation; any future source reuse needs that source's own license
and notices. Existing MIT pattern fixtures and notices remain unchanged.

docs/public/experimental/garments/fit-re.title: Garment fit, resolution and presentation experiments
docs/public/experimental/garments/fit-re.markdown:
# Garment fit, resolution and presentation experiments

> **Experimental.** Garment work is research, not part of the supported product. Its APIs, syntax and results may change or be withdrawn. See [experimental modules](../README.md).

Date: 2026-10-11. This continues the [armhole experiment](armhole-experiment.md)
with the same MIT-credited GarmentCode cut, Anatolia body, fabric and sewing/motion
schedule. These are bounded experiments, not an accepted production garment.
Detailed run data and meshes remain under ignored
`artifacts/local/garment/fit-resolution-round/`.

## Controlled fit and regional trials

All complete runs use 30 sewing frames, 60 fitting frames, a half-second T-to-A
transition, 60 wearing frames, eight substeps and 24 structural iterations.
Temporary supports release after 20 fitting frames. There are no permanent pins.
The acceptance limits remain 15% tensile strain, 10mm seam gap and 5mm sampled
body-clearance violation. Qualified checkpoints do not certify every intervening
surface or motion.

| Trial | Fitting strain | Midpoint strain | Wearing strain | Complete sequence |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Retained control, 60mm mesh request | 22.309% | 22.372% | 9.228% | Fails |
| Collar plane lowered from shoulder +45mm to +15mm | 64.887% | 77.871% | 53.519% | Fails |
| Support sewn shoulder edges at the original height | 21.789% | 22.511% | 9.227% | Fails |
| Collar material region, original support | 22.596% | 22.960% | 9.201% | Fails |
| 30mm mesh request, original support | 19.558% | 19.666% | 20.450% | Fails |

The first row is the retained, source-bound control from the previous round. New
support trials change only the erased Concept guide or its named edge selection.
The shared rest/arrangement content key for the 60mm trials remains
`42C204F0BE495216B6CB3C2C3087EC8C786135D3EE71FE2D465BCFB4D468BA8B`.
Source hashes differ because guides, pose declarations and comments are separate
authoring context. Body artifact SHA-256 remains
`0a0ad03e86447fc56448940c7aa56b54ea6683e8a874f833e01fd56a65a2d0e5`.

The collar region selects a 48mm material-space band around the named collar
curves: 56 vertices and 121 modified structural stencils. Stretch compliance is
scaled by 0.25 and bending compliance by 4. Rest lengths, masses, seam compliance
and cross-region stencils remain unchanged. The complete regional run has exact
static/midpoint replay and releases all temporary guides. It is still rejected:
right-back armhole link 331/332, rest length 10.770mm, dominates fitting and motion.
No regional settings or support changes become defaults.

Denser geometry moves the dominant failure. At 30mm, link 54/55 on the left-back
armhole adjacent to the shoulder seam has rest length 19.736mm and reaches
20.450% wearing strain. Seam gap improves to 0.353mm, while sampled clearance
violation remains below 0.001mm. Improved sewing accuracy does not establish an
accepted material fit. More density is not a substitute for resolving that
local strain failure. Its concentration beside the shoulder seam suggests a
contact/structural conflict, but these trials do not isolate that causal mechanism.

`GarmentMeshInspection.StretchOutliers` now owns the shared structural diagnostic.
CLI evidence records named-panel/material-coordinate outliers at fitting,
midpoint and wearing checkpoints, rather than reporting only the final frame.

## Mesh quality and bounded startup cost

The mesher's interior lattice pitch is 80% of `meshSize`. Requests of 60, 30 and
15mm therefore produce median edges near 48, 24 and 12mm. The same analytic cut
is resampled, not resized; small rest-area differences come from curved boundary
chord approximation.

| Request | Vertices / triangles | Median edge | Minimum angle | Triangles below 10 degrees | Lumped area ratio | Five startup frames |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 60mm | 611 / 992 | 48mm | 10.33 degrees | 0 | 26.32 | 9.17s |
| 30mm | 1,944 / 3,486 | 24mm | 19.02 degrees | 0 | 15.32 | 20.55s |
| 15mm | 7,224 / 13,672 | 12mm | 19.01 degrees | 0 | 11.74 | 61.40s |

All have zero unused vertices. Rest areas are 0.804074, 0.803821 and 0.803607m².
The prefix probe uses the real T-pose body, temporary guide, solver, contact
queries and first five sewing compliance values. It is not a completed drape or
convergence test. Position/velocity replay agrees exactly. Fifth-frame strain is
51.54%, 93.70% and 98.28% respectively; these early sewing transients are not
qualification checkpoints.

Timing is a local observation including diagnostic samples, not a hardware or
continuum-material benchmark. Link compliance is an uncalibrated discrete
authoring control; keeping it fixed across resolutions does not establish equal
physical fabric stiffness. The complete 30mm run took about 641 seconds and
overlapped the independent regional trial. The 15mm complete sequence is not run:
its prefix costs roughly 6.7 times the coarse prefix, and the completed medium
trial worsens final strain. A longer, denser repetition has no established benefit.

## Optional presentation binding

`Aetheris.Cloth3D.ClothPresentationBinding3D.Compile(plan, levels)` constructs
deterministic sparse Loop interior stencils for zero, one or two refinement
levels. Material boundaries are fixed; inserted boundary vertices remain exact
linear samples. This includes sewn panel boundaries: the operation does not
weld them or hide measured seam gaps. Compiled weights retain original simulation
vertex correspondence and material coordinates. Budgets stop before exceeding
65,536 display vertices or 262,144 display triangles.

Evaluation accepts only a snapshot belonging to that compiled cloth key. It
produces a finer surface without changing physics, stored vertices, rest lengths,
constraints, contact geometry or qualification. In Aurelian:

```csharp
var artifact = ClothGarmentArtifact3D.Load("dress.garment.json");
var agent = ClothAgentDefinition3D.FromGarment(artifact).WithPresentation(2);
```

Compilation occurs in the explicit authoring call. Scene projection evaluates the
binding and normals without stepping the agent. It has a distinct presentation
identity, so display topology does not alias the original mesh. The current
presentation evaluator is CPU-based.

| Display levels | Vertices / triangles | Maximum sampled clearance violation | Sampled body penetration |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 611 / 992 | below 0.001mm | 0 |
| 1 | 2,210 / 3,968 | 1.648mm | 0 |
| 2 | 8,384 / 15,872 | 2.041mm | 0 |

Here clearance includes the authored body margin plus half cloth thickness;
body penetration uses half thickness only. The refined surface spends some of
that margin but does not enter the sampled body. This is a sampled diagnostic,
not an exhaustive intersection proof. On all three displays, simulation strain
remains 9.228% and seam gap remains 1.1325mm.

Front/side/back renders show a modest smoothing benefit. They still show the
projecting neckline, stiff silhouette and visible center seam. Refinement cannot
invent textile construction or fix the remaining physical fit. Blender presents
the engine-generated meshes with no additional fitting, subdivision or simulation.

## Regional material capability

`ClothDefinition3D.MaterialRegions` supplies disjoint named vertex sets with
finite stretch/bend compliance scales in `(0,1000]`. A structural constraint is
modified only when its whole stencil belongs to one region. Stitches retain
their own authored compliance. Empty, invalid, duplicate or overlapping regions
stop before simulation. Regional data enters the content key and garment
transport; definitions without regions preserve their established keys.

This is a typed C# capability. `schema Garment` still authors one shared Fabric;
no speculative regional Firmament syntax is introduced. The existing Vulkan
storage ABI receives the compiled compliance values without another shader path.

## Reproduction

Use the repository CLI and actual gameplay body. `control-30.firmament` is the
canonical guided source with only `meshSize: 60mm` replaced by `meshSize: 30mm`.
The lower collar trial replaces `shoulderHeight + 45mm` with `+15mm`. The shoulder
trial selects `left_ftorso.edges.edge3`, `right_ftorso.edges.edge2`,
`left_btorso.edges.edge2`, and `right_btorso.edges.edge3` instead of collar edges.

```powershell
dotnet Aetheris.CLI/bin/Release/net10.0/aetheris.dll garment drape `
  artifacts/local/garment/fit-resolution-round/control-30.firmament `
  --body artifacts/local/humanoid-production/antonia.gameplay-body.json `
  --ticks 60 --out-dir artifacts/local/garment/fit-resolution-round/control-30 --json

dotnet run -c Release scripts/experiment-garment-fit.cs -- prefix `
  fixtures/Canonical/Garment/garmentcode-dress-guided.firmament `
  artifacts/local/humanoid-production/antonia.gameplay-body.json `
  artifacts/local/garment/fit-resolution-round/prefix

dotnet run -c Release scripts/experiment-garment-fit.cs -- regions `
  fixtures/Canonical/Garment/garmentcode-dress-guided.firmament `
  artifacts/local/humanoid-production/antonia.gameplay-body.json `
  artifacts/local/garment/fit-resolution-round/regions-60
```

Presentation mode takes a matching source/body/output directory and reads
`input-garment.json` in that directory. It rejects a source-hash mismatch instead
of accepting a superficially similar source. The retained control uses its
original `armhole-round/anatolia-guided-transition.firmament` source, not the
later canonical source with different comments.

The tested scene projection remains distinct from native GPU body draping.
Fitting guides and triangle-body contacts remain CPU-only; no friction, CCD,
garment self-contact or physical fabric calibration is newly qualified.

## Validation

Both Release solution builds succeed. The complete Aetheris solution test run
passes 4,522 tests with test collections serialized; the complete Aurelian
solution passes 1,219 tests, including 28 cloth tests. Presentation tests exercise
actual scene compilation, mounting and projection without advancing simulation.
Regional tests cover transport round-trip, content identity, preserved rest
metrics and masses, seam exclusion, invalid selections and scalar GPU packing.

The first Aetheris run encountered the existing five-second CAD display deadline
in `MissingDisplayPatch_IsSeparateFromEngineering_WithSourceFaceIdentity`.
That test passes alone and in the serialized complete rerun. No CAD geometry,
test budgets or qualification limits were changed. The test-generated tracked
STEP witness was restored after validation.

The actual `Aurelian.GraphicsProof --cloth-systems` path compiles
`Cloth3D.v.ts` and runs Vulkan compute on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070. Its added
25-vertex regional case runs eight steps with a deformed initial surface;
maximum CPU/GPU position disagreement is 0.004554mm. Same-device position and
velocity replay agrees exactly. The full proof emits
`AURELIAN_CLOTH_SYSTEMS_PASSED`; detailed evidence remains in Copeland's ignored
`artifacts/local/garment-fit-round-vulkan/`.

This GPU result qualifies regional constraint execution, not Anatolia triangle-body
draping or GPU evaluation of the new presentation stencils. The complete garment
experiments all remain rejected by their unchanged fit gates. No commercial
geometry, textures, morphs or extracted assets are inputs to these experiments.

docs/public/experimental/garments/garmen.title: Starting from GarmentCode sewing patterns
docs/public/experimental/garments/garmen.markdown:
# Starting from GarmentCode sewing patterns

> **Experimental.** Garment work is research, not part of the supported product. Its APIs, syntax and results may change or be withdrawn. See [experimental modules](../README.md).

Garment authoring can begin with an actual programmed sewing pattern rather
than an approximate garment silhouette. Aetheris imports resolved GarmentCode
JSON into ordinary `schema Garment` source: pure profile `Feature`s, arranged
`Panel`s and explicit `Interface<Stitch>` declarations. The existing profile
resolver, analytic seam inspector, panel mesher and cloth solver retain authority.
There is no Python dependency in the application runtime.

Credit: Maria Korosteleva and Olga Sorkine-Hornung,
[*GarmentCode: Programming Parametric Sewing Patterns*](https://igl.ethz.ch/projects/garmentcode/),
SIGGRAPH Asia 2023. The [upstream code](https://github.com/maria-korosteleva/GarmentCode)
is MIT licensed. See `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and the complete preserved license
in `fixtures/Canonical/Garment/GarmentCode/LICENSE.txt`.

## Import, inspect, modify

```powershell
dotnet Aetheris.CLI/bin/Release/net10.0/aetheris.dll garment import-garmentcode `
  fixtures/Canonical/Garment/GarmentCode/dress.json `
  --out-dir artifacts/local/garment/imported-dress --json

dotnet Aetheris.CLI/bin/Release/net10.0/aetheris.dll garment build `
  artifacts/local/garment/imported-dress/garment.firmament `
  --out-dir artifacts/local/garment/imported-dress/build --json
```

Import emits `garment.firmament`, the retained `specification.json`, an analytic
`patterns.svg` preview and `import-evidence.json`. It does **not** claim to mesh,
simulate or fit a new figure. Evidence records the input hash, original panel
names, edge-index mapping, boundary reversals and measured seam lengths.
Keep the original specification's license with imported derivatives.

The importer admits resolved relative curves, explicit units and panel transforms,
one closed loop per panel, line/circular/quadratic/cubic edges and two-sided
stitches. Quadratic curves are elevated exactly to cubic Beziers. Circular
arcs retain radius, side and major/minor selection. Unsupported curves, unresolved
parameter programs, invalid references and reused seam spans stop with diagnostics.

The source's local XY coordinates remain the flat material pattern. Upstream
Y-up placement maps to Aetheris Z-up; Euler rotation order is retained. Clockwise
loops are normalized to Firmament's counterclockwise outer boundary and seam
correspondence is adjusted by the same reversal parity. `right_wrong` stitches
retain their upstream same-direction pairing. Numeric edge IDs remain in the
names even when semantic armhole/collar labels are present.

Upstream JSON does not carry Aetheris fabric properties or a material grain
direction. The generated source exposes **Aetheris defaults** explicitly for
review and replacement. Upstream unequal seam lengths become an explicit
measured `ease` value; mismatches above Aetheris's 25% budget are rejected.
Analytic cut lengths govern admission. Polygonal chord errors during meshing
do not redefine authored ease.

## Known templates

`fixtures/Canonical/Garment/garmentcode-dress.firmament` is the imported
non-fitted `Shirt` block with sleeves disabled and upstream length multiplier
2.2. It has four half-torso panels and six seams, with real curved armholes
and different front/back collar cuts. `GarmentCode/shirt.json` retains the
original sleeved shirt control with eight panels and sixteen seams.

`garmentcode-dress-template.firmament` adds a native `hemDrop: Length` parameter
to those same pure profile recipes:

```firmament
Feature left_ftorsoCut = left_ftorsoPattern(hemDrop: 100mm);
```

Apply the same adjustment to all four cuts. Zero produces the same compiled
cloth as the reference import; a positive value lowers the hem without changing
armhole, collar or shoulder construction. Existing profile deltas remain the
owner for other named-span edits. This is a resolved starter block, **not** a
port of the entire upstream measurement-driven configurator.

## Reproduce the research controls

The external checkout is pinned to
`d449629979028123a5c4dc9e732a2ec19b7fce31`.
`scripts/research-garmentcode.py --upstream <checkout> --out-dir <ignored-directory>`
calls the real upstream `Shirt` program and its SVG/JSON exporter. The checked-in
designs, measurement YAML, provenance and independently sampled curve oracles
document the inputs. Canonical presentation ordering makes generated JSON repeat
byte-for-byte despite upstream component discovery using a Python set.

Pattern-only Python dependencies used in the isolated research venv:
`numpy<2`, `pyyaml`, `scipy`, `svgwrite`, `svgpathtools`, `psutil`, `matplotlib`,
`CairoSVG`. The venv and checkout remain under `artifacts/local/garment/research/`.

For a matching **external** unrigged reference mesh, the shared
`GarmentDraping.SettleOnSurface` API runs the same sewing/settling/replay path
using `IClothBodySurface3D`, without inventing skeletons or skin weights.
It rejects named figure/pose bindings and measured fits; those must use their
actual humanoid binding. The bounded research harness accepts upstream Y-up,
metre, triangle-only OBJ input:

```powershell
dotnet run --file scripts/qualify-garmentcode-reference.cs -c Release -- `
  artifacts/local/garment/imported-dress/garment.firmament `
  <external-checkout>/assets/bodies/mean_all.obj `
  artifacts/local/garment/reference-body
```

The harness retains body/specification hashes, actual solver metrics, replay,
contact/stretch outliers and OBJ artifacts. A failure returns code 2. These are
discrete one-way CPU contact experiments without friction, CCD or self-contact;
they do not qualify animation or production cloth. Body meshes and the separate
GarmentCodeData dataset are not included or relicensed by this source adoption.

## Current experiment results

Follow-up: [garment draping research](draping-research.md) audits the
retained mesh and strain distribution, compares primary research, and defines
the next controlled experiments. It does not relax these qualification gates.
The [mesh and settling implementation](meshing-settling-experiment.md)
records the new mesh, residual histories and solver split experiment separately
from these historical controls. The dress still fails qualification.

The real upstream shirt and dress patterns match their independently generated
curve oracles (five samples and length per edge, 0.00001mm tolerance), then build
through the normal CLI mesher. A 100mm native hem extension keeps collar and
armhole geometry unchanged; zero reproduces the reference compiled cloth.

The first drape controls use the same 60mm mesh request, cotton defaults,
30 sewing ticks and 30 gravity ticks. Blender renders only the retained solver
OBJ output. These controls **fail** the existing 15% peak strain budget:

| Control | Peak stretch | Maximum seam gap | Maximum surface penetration | Replay |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Original upstream sizing/arrangement on Anatolia | 42.35% | 3.51mm | <0.001mm | Exact |
| Original cut on matching upstream `mean_all` reference body | 85.62% | 11.30mm | <0.001mm | Exact |
| Matching reference body, arrangement raised 100mm, cut unchanged | 154.72% | 4.20mm | 1.49mm | Exact |
| Anatolia, same raised arrangement and unchanged cut | 50.82% | 1.28mm | <0.001mm | Exact |

The unraised dress slips below the shoulders on both bodies. Raising arrangement
improves seam closure but worsens peak strain, so an arrangement offset alone is
not a qualified fix. The raised control's largest outlier is a 1.48mm rest link
near the front neckline, despite the 60mm mesh request. This isolates mesh quality
and sewing/body-contact convergence as the next investigation; it does not prove
that short links alone caused the failure. Neither changing the reference cut
nor relaxing the acceptance budget is justified by these results.

Retained evidence: `artifacts/local/garment/garmentcode-dress/` contains imports,
sources, `antonia-reference-sizing/`, `reference-body/`, `raised-reference-body/`
and their metric/outlier reports. The upstream simulator was not run. No
production garment fit, animation or new-body automatic measurement mapping is
claimed by these pattern/interchange controls.

The raised arrangement stays on the shoulders in the reference-body render;
its improved silhouette does not override the failed strain check. The same
arrangement is retained as `anatolia-raised.firmament` and `anatolia-raised/`,
with an unchanged flat cut and no hidden supports. Both still need solver/mesh
convergence work. Both Release solution builds passed; the full Aetheris suite
passed 4,479 tests, and the Aurelian consumer suite passed 1,217 with its installed
Naga selected through `AURELIAN_NAGA`.
