docs/public/firmament/glb.md.markdown:
# Static GLB presentation export

Aetheris exports GLB from the same compiled assembly display meshes used by USD.
BRep and STEP retain engineering authority. GLB carries downstream presentation
geometry for web, DCC, game assets, and presentations.

```powershell
dotnet run --project Aetheris.CLI -c Release -- asm export-glb `
  fixtures/Canonical/AssemblyInterfaces/IndustrialAtlas/atlas-industrial.firmament `
  artifacts/local/presentation-3d-x0/atlas-display.glb `
  --materials fixtures/Canonical/AssemblyInterfaces/IndustrialAtlas/appearance.json `
  --state Shoulder=-75 --state Elbow=-140 --state GripLeft=10 --state GripRight=10 --json
```

The output defaults to ignored `artifacts/local/glb/`. `.firmasm` assemblies are
also supported. Definitions become shared indexed triangle meshes. Occurrences
retain their hierarchy and rigid local transforms. Separate face normals retain
sharp features. One root transform converts right-handed Z-up millimetres to
right-handed Y-up metres: `(x,y,z) → .001 × (x,z,-y)`.

Appearance JSON maps exact definition identities to `red`, `green`, `blue`,
`metallic`, and `roughness` values in `[0,1]`. RGB factors are linear, as in the
existing USD preview mapping. Optional `baseColorTexture` names a PNG/JPEG relative
to the appearance file, and `textureCoordinates` supplies two values per display
vertex in glTF UV convention. Images are physically embedded in GLB, so moving the
asset requires no external files. UV seams must already be represented by separate
display vertices. Invalid units, frames, normals, indices, hierarchy, materials,
and texture bindings fail explicitly.

The polished examples use their existing Aetheris-generated USD/Blender
presentation scenes. `scripts/export-presentation-scene.py` preserves product
positions and polygons, embeds the ATLAS maker label, and bakes the guitar's
existing procedural sunburst/wood base color. It does not translate general
material graphs or alter guitar geometry. Procedural grain bump is omitted.
The presentation qualifier regenerates the guitar USD and shaded scene from
current Firmament source on every run; it does not reuse a cached guitar `.blend`.

ATLAS is an independent Aetheris demo robot. Aetheris is not affiliated with,
endorsed by, or associated with Boston Dynamics. The shared name is coincidental.

The existing C# slide writer supports `Model3D(Source, Preview, X, Y, Width,
Height, Camera, Name)` through `DrawingPptxWriter.WriteModel3DDeck`. Placement is
in millimetres; `Model3DView` specifies the glTF centre in metres, presentation
scale, Euler rotation and camera distance/field of view. Each object requires a
PNG preview. The compiler physically embeds both assets and emits the Office
3D object with a static fallback.

```powershell
dotnet run --project Aetheris.CLI -c Release -- presentation compile `
  fixtures/Canonical/Presentation3D/interactive-3d-demo.json `
  artifacts/local/presentation-3d-x0/interactive-3d-demo.pptx --json
```

Paths in the JSON authoring input resolve relative to that input. After
compilation, the PPTX needs no external model or image files. Desktop PowerPoint
rotation and save/reopen qualification is separate from package/schema checks.

See [PRESENTATION-3D-X0](../../development/reports/2026-10/PRESENTATION-3D-X0.md) for artifact and
PowerPoint qualification status. No animation, glTF import, compression, or
game-engine integration is included.

docs/public/firmament/grooves-and-ribs.m.title: Grooves and manual ribs
docs/public/firmament/grooves-and-ribs.m.markdown:
# Grooves and manual ribs

Use named Concept guides or Paths to locate a channel or reinforcing rib. The
guide retains layout intent; the feature supplies its section and dimensions.
Both features produce one integrated analytic body, rather than overlapping
tool solids.

## Manual rib

This complete example is
[manual-rib.firmament](../../../fixtures/Canonical/Features/PathFeatures/manual-rib.firmament):

```firmament
Model ManuallyRibbedPlate {
    units: mm
    Concept Struct Layout on XY {
        Point2 Start { position: [-18mm, 0mm] }
        Point2 End { position: [18mm, 0mm] }
        Line2 Spine { from: Start; to: End }
    }
    Box Plate { size: [60mm, 40mm, 6mm] }
    Modify Plate {
        Rib<Rectangular> Stiffener {
            on: face(Plate.Top)
            path: Layout.Spine
            thickness: 3mm
            height: 10mm
            draft: 2deg
            ends: Round
        }
    }
}
```

`Rib` adds material to an existing host. It does not run AutoRib, relocate a guide,
or select a reinforcement network.

- `path` names a line, circular arc, circle, or a Path resolving to one such
  segment. Guide coordinates are XY coordinates local to the support.
- `thickness` is the full base thickness, centered on the guide.
- `height` is measured outward from the support.
- `draft` defaults to `0deg`. Positive draft narrows both sides toward the top:
  top thickness = base thickness − 2 × height × tan(draft).
- `ends` defaults to `Flat`. Straight guides also admit `Round`, giving
  semicircular ends in plan. Flat end planes remain at the guide endpoints:
  side draft does not shorten the guide. Flat end faces therefore have zero
  end draft, even when the band sides have positive draft.
- A closed circular guide has no ends; omit the field.

For a rounded straight rib, the guide endpoints are the centers of its rounded
ends. Overall length is guide length plus thickness at the relevant height.
An [arc rib](../../../fixtures/Canonical/Features/PathFeatures/arc-rib.firmament)
uses exact conical sides when drafted.

## Rib junctions and mixed features

Separate named ribs may meet as T, L or X junctions. Their footprints are
united into one material boundary; internal overlapping walls are removed.
Zero-draft line, arc and circular ribs may have different heights. Drafted
junctions currently require straight Flat-ended ribs of one common height.
The compiler proves the boundary stays affine through every possible section
event; topology-changing taper rejects rather than emitting an approximate loft.

The complete [reinforced mounting plate](../../../fixtures/Canonical/Features/PathFeatures/reinforced-mounting-plate.firmament)
combines two crossing drafted ribs, counterbored and countersunk through holes,
and a top perimeter fillet. Top-entry `ThroughAll` holes and one `+Z` perimeter
Fillet or Chamfer reuse the ordinary stock feature builders. Rib and groove
footprints must clear the holes' largest entry diameter and the perimeter finish.
The holes do not require a perimeter finish. Noninteracting grooves may share the same stock. A hole crossing a rib, or a
groove crossing another path feature, is explicitly rejected.

Build JSON exposes `ribPlanning`: the selected construction, candidate admission
and utility, and checked section intervals. Existing isolated constructions are
preferred to preserve their geometry. A completely buried/redundant named rib
is rejected because no independent feature boundary survives. Feature order does
not change a junction network's generated geometry or semantic names.

## Plate channels and circular face grooves

[plate-channels.firmament](../../../fixtures/Canonical/Features/PathFeatures/plate-channels.firmament)
contains two separate straight channels. Inside `Modify Plate`, write:

```firmament
Groove<Rectangular> Channel {
    on: +Z
    path: Upper
    width: 4mm
    depth: 2mm
    ends: Round
}
```

`Groove<Rectangular>` removes a centered band of the specified width and depth.
`Groove<Semicircular>` takes `radius` instead: opening width is twice the radius
and depth equals the radius. Supplying independent width/depth to a semicircle
is rejected.

For Round-ended straight channels, guide endpoints are cap centers: the opening
extends by half its width beyond each end.

A straight semicircular channel has a cylindrical bottom and, with Round ends,
spherical end patches. A circular or arc channel has a toroidal bottom.
[plate-seal-groove.firmament](../../../fixtures/Canonical/Features/PathFeatures/plate-seal-groove.firmament)
demonstrates a circular face groove.

## Cylindrical grooves

[shaft-seal-groove.firmament](../../../fixtures/Canonical/Features/PathFeatures/shaft-seal-groove.firmament)
declares a coaxial Circle2 with the shaft radius, then uses:

```firmament
Modify Shaft {
    Groove<Rectangular> SealSeat {
        on: face(Shaft.OuterWall)
        path: Layout.Seal
        station: 20mm
        width: 4mm
        depth: 2mm
    }
}
```

`station` is the axial center measured from the stock base (Z = 0). Width is
axial; depth is radial into material. `OuterWall` cuts inward, and `InnerWall`
cuts outward. The latter requires a top-open `Cylinder<Hollow>` host; its guide
circle radius equals the inner radius. See
[bore-seal-groove.firmament](../../../fixtures/Canonical/Features/PathFeatures/bore-seal-groove.firmament).
Both rectangular and semicircular sections are supported. The cut must leave
positive wall and axial end margins.

These constructs define geometry. An O-ring gland's squeeze, fill, clearances,
material compatibility and pressure suitability require separate engineering
requirements; a groove is not an automatic seal-design approval.

## Current limits

- Planar ribs/channels require a direct Box's top support (`+Z`, `Top` or
  `face(Body.Top)`). Other faces, Extrude/Compose and imported-body hosts reject.
- Cylindrical grooves require coaxial full circles on a direct Cylinder or
  top-open `Cylinder<Hollow>`, with no bottom blend. Cylindrical ribs,
  axial/helical cylinder channels and arbitrary surface paths reject.
- Open arcs require Flat ends and a positive sweep of at most 180 degrees.
  Compound Paths and arbitrary sections reject; junctions use separate named ribs.
- Planar footprints must remain strictly inside the support. Rib networks use
  exact line/arc arrangements. Grooves remain separate; their interactions reject.
  Groove-only sets retain conservative disjoint XY envelope admission.
  Cylindrical groove axial envelopes must be disjoint.
- Box ribs/channels may combine with the bounded holes and perimeter finish
  described above. Perforation, Thread and mixed cylindrical-groove operations
  remain unsupported. No requested operation is silently dropped.
- A rib top may not collapse under draft; a groove must leave positive material.
  No base fillet, molding-release certification or automatic rib placement is
  implied. Existing PlasticShell AutoRib retains its separate qualified limits.
- Construction points and guides must have unique names, including across
  Concept Struct scopes. Non-XY construction frames are
  rejected for these support-local feature consumers.
- Feature names and source provenance are retained. This does not introduce
  public selectors such as `face(Stiffener.Top)`.
- Authoritative volume assertions and SDF measurement are not yet qualified for
  these composite bodies. The CLI reports that limitation; topology inspection
  and explicitly numerical mesh comparisons remain available.

Related: [Profiles and construction](../reference/language/profiles.md),
[material offsets](material-offsets.md), [PlasticShell](plastic-shell.md),
and [solids and features](../reference/language/solids-and-features.md).

docs/public/firmament/imported-feature-r.title: Imported through-hole revisions
docs/public/firmament/imported-feature-r.markdown:
# Imported through-hole revisions

Firmament can move or remove one isolated round through-hole in a pinned imported STEP
body, retaining the actual residual BRep. A move retains the
hole diameter and depth; removal fills its proved material column. It does not reverse-engineer the
whole part or reconstruct stock from a guessed HostSize.

The executable golden source is
[`ctc01-hole-move.firmament`](../../../fixtures/Regression/InlineStep/production/ctc01-hole-move.firmament).
It moves a Ø25 mm hole on NIST CTC-01 from (-160,45) to (-130,45) mm, through the
same Z=-50..0 mm material column.

```firmament
Model Revision {
    units: mm
    InlineStep Source {
        path: "ctc01.stp"
        textSha256: "341cea888fb316673ed683e59391c11b4f96cff2542d9387e135f06682dbd745"
        importTolerance: 0.01mm
        geometryOnly: true
    }
    Recognize Source {
        Region MountHole {
            kind: HoleShaft
            stepFaceEntities: ["#764", "#765"]
            evidence: { radius: 12.5mm; through: true }
        }
    }
    Replace Source.MountHole with Hole<Shaft> MountHole {
        on: Source.Face(98)
        center: Point3(-130mm, 45mm, 0mm)
        diameter: 25mm
        end: ThroughAll
        within: {
            min: Point3(-175mm, 30mm, -50mm)
            max: Point3(-115mm, 60mm, 0mm)
        }
    }
}
```

Put the unmodified CTC-01 STEP beside this example as `ctc01.stp`, or use the
repository fixture's relative path. Prefer `aetheris lock revision.firmament` to
generate a dependency receipt, then omit the source hash field. For a source-only
specimen, choose exactly one explicit pin:

- `sha256` checks exact file bytes. Obtain it with PowerShell
  `Get-FileHash file.stp -Algorithm SHA256`.
- `textSha256` checks decoded source text encoded as UTF-8 with CRLF/CR converted
  to LF. No other whitespace or characters are changed. The fixture uses this
  explicit mode because Git stores the corpus as LF while older Windows worktrees
  can contain CRLF. Import still consumes the original text; no file is rewritten.

There is no fallback between these modes. Build JSON records the chosen hash kind
and actual input byte hash (UTF-8 resource hash for browser snapshots). Re-inspect
entity selectors before intentionally updating a pin after an upstream revision.

## Discover, name and plan a revision

Agents do not need to author BRep ordinals or guess edit bounds. Start with the
actual imported geometry:

```shell
aetheris imported-features inspect ctc01.stp --import-tolerance .01 --json
```

The report is explicitly `InspectionOnly`. It returns measured cylindrical groups,
original STEP wall entities, axis, diameter, and, when proved, through-depth,
entry/exit faces and center. `Recognized` means the bounded through-hole proof
passed. `CanPlan` additionally requires import qualification; it does **not**
certify a new destination. Unsupported groups carry rejection reasons. Strict
.001 mm inspection of CTC-01 still reports measurements but blocks planning.
No original design history or manufacturing process is inferred.

Select one candidate using these facts, then pass its exact ID. For the pinned
CTC-01 source, the upper-left diameter-25 hole has this ID:

```shell
aetheris imported-features plan ctc01.stp --candidate "through-hole:step-764+765" --as MountHole --offset 290 0 --geometry-only --import-tolerance .01 --source-out artifacts/local/imported-features/revision.firmament --json
aetheris validate artifacts/local/imported-features/revision.firmament --json
aetheris build artifacts/local/imported-features/revision.firmament --output artifacts/local/imported-features/revised.step --json
```

`--offset du dv` uses the radial coordinates of the proved upper opening:
YZ for X-axis holes, XZ for Y-axis holes, and XY for Z-axis holes;
`--to x y z` supplies an absolute Point3 instead. All numbers are millimetres.
Use `--remove` instead of either placement mode to fill the selected hole.
Exactly one of `--offset`, `--to`, or `--remove` is required. `--clearance` defaults to .1 mm and must
exceed import uncertainty. The plan qualifies its generated source through normal
build admission before committing outputs; a refused plan leaves no new source file.

`--as MountHole` names the existing `Region` and replacement feature. There is no
additional Firmament `as` grammar. The emitted declaration is:

```firmament
Recognize Source {
    Region MountHole {
        kind: HoleShaft
        candidate: "through-hole:step-764+765"
    }
}
```

`candidate` is mutually exclusive with `faces` and `stepFaceEntities`. Candidate
IDs are stable within the pinned source, not across arbitrary STEP re-exports or
entity renumbering. A missing or unsupported candidate rejects; the compiler never
chooses a nearby hole. CLI planning writes `firmament.lock.toml` alongside the
hash-free revision source, and qualifies that saved source through the normal
compiler before reporting success. Previous source/lock files are restored on a
qualification failure. An existing receipt for another root rejects. Re-inspect
and review a changed STEP in a new revision/project; a lock update cannot rebind
surgery selections. The SDK source-only `PlanMove` result retains its explicit
`textSha256` pin for compatibility and immutable resource planning.

New in-plane positions use a **0.1 mm authoring grid**, midpoint ties away
from zero. Safety bounds round outward. Imported diameters and support stations
remain source-derived: a 6.35 mm hole stays 6.35 mm, and a plate thickness does
not move to a different plane merely to remove floating-point noise from source.
Generated source uses `Source.MountHole.diameter`, `.entry.Y`, `.exit.Y`, and
`.center.Y` for FTC-09, whose thickness runs along Y. The plan records
`authoringIncrementMillimetres: 0.1` for newly authored move coordinates.

Inside imported `Replace` and `Remove` field expressions, a proved named region
exposes `diameter`, `depth` (Length), `center`, `entry`, `exit` (Point3), and their
`.X`, `.Y`, `.Z` components (Length). Entry is the maximum principal-axis station;
exit is the minimum. These facts bind directly through the unified AST against
the pinned source. They are currently local to these imported edit fields;
arbitrary Static/Concept expressions cannot yet consume them. Unknown facts reject.

The numerical `importTolerance` keeps its own precision. It is distinct from
manufacturing tolerance; the authoring grid creates no `tol` requirement and does
not round retained STEP geometry. A requested resize or off-plane move rejects.

The CTC-01 generator retains its named `Concept Struct` Point3; destination bounds reference
its `.X` and `.Y` components. Editing that one point moves the requested hole and
reruns clearance checks without duplicating coordinates. The executable
[recovered fixture](../../../fixtures/Regression/InlineStep/production/ctc01-recovered-hole-move.firmament)
moves the hole across the central boss to (130,45) mm without editing the boss.

The .NET SDK exposes the same path through `FirmamentImportedFeatures.Inspect`
and `PlanMove`/`PlanRemove`. Snapshot planning uses the immutable inspected resource text;
file-backed planning rechecks the pin through the ordinary loader. Explicit
geometry-only approval remains required in both paths.

## What the fields mean

`stepFaceEntities` selects original STEP entity IDs. `faces` is the historical
sequential face-number alternative; the two number spaces are not interchangeable.
Select the complete cylindrical wall group, including legitimate split half-walls.
Recognition proves that the group has complete circular openings on two parallel
planar supports and is an inward through-void. An authored kind, confidence or
evidence label cannot override failed geometry checks.

`on` selects one of those proved supports. In the pinned CTC-01 source, sequential
face 98 is the plane at Z=0. `center` is a Point3 in imported-body coordinates,
which coincide with Model world coordinates in this single-body workflow. It
must lie on the selected plane. Imported UV origins are not inferred from a Point2.

`within` authorizes the local edit volume. One bounds object must contain both
holes with positive clearance and span the support planes. Alternatively,
`within: [sourceBounds, destinationBounds]` takes exactly two bounds objects,
each `{ min: Point3(...); max: Point3(...) }`. They authorize suppression and
reinsertion separately; no swept movement corridor is edited. Separate regions
currently require provable line/circle support trim boundaries, and the
destination must be inside both material domains, excluding other openings.
An exterior destination cannot manufacture stock. The compiler proves
that no other boundary can interfere. A conservative refusal means the current
planner cannot prove that envelope safe; it is not necessarily a physically
impossible edit. Support faces can extend outside the box: their support surfaces,
outer loops and all unrelated inner loops remain intact.

`importTolerance` is a numeric import/trim qualification budget in mm, **not a
manufacturing tolerance or a `tol` requirement**. It defaults to 0.001 mm. CTC-01's
original polynomial intersection curves deviate about 0.0034 mm from their analytic
supports and the file declares 0.01 mm source accuracy. The example explicitly
admits that accuracy; strict 0.001 mm admission rejects. Source geometry is not
fitted or moved to hide that discrepancy. Export carries declared distance
accuracy rather than claiming native precision for retained imported geometry.

## Imported annotations

`geometryOnly: true` explicitly excludes the source annotation layer. It does not
modify the original STEP. The compiler emits a warning and reports the choice.
This first bounded revision workflow requires explicit geometry-only import for
every pinned source. Generic source PMI migration is not admitted, including
annotation graphs that the bounded inspector does not recognize. Without explicit
exclusion the edit rejects; it never silently discards imported requirements.

The new named Hole produces semantic diameter/depth PMI associated with its new
wall faces. Additional supported Firmament PMI can be authored against the revised
bindings. Importing geometry only does not certify, translate or preserve the
vendor's original dimensions, datums or GD&T.

## Admission and reports

The current family is one isolated round principal-axis (X, Y or Z) through-hole, unchanged diameter
and depth, between two parallel planar supports in one qualified closed oriented
body. Blind, intersecting, breakout, threaded, blended-entry, counterbore,
countersink, slot and oblique-axis revisions reject. Unknown fields and placements reject.
No arbitrary-body Boolean fallback or general healing is performed. An unedited
pinned body can be re-exported through the qualified import owner; a pin does not
imply a replacement operation. Additional Modify operations still reject rather
than bypassing revision admission.

The operation suppresses the old wall/openings, materializes fresh analytic hole
geometry and reinserts it with fresh topology IDs. Unchanged topology keeps its
identity; a face correspondence map records the revision. Cached construction
geometry is invalidated. Required trim, boundary and STEP roundtrip checks must
pass before success. `validate` and `build` use the same admission path.

CLI build JSON exposes `importedHoleRevision`, including strategy, import accuracy,
annotation exclusion, retired/new walls, preserved entity counts and correspondence.
`inlineStepMigration.residualSurgery` is true for this operation. Syntax diagnostics
and kernel admission failures retain source context.

## FTC-09 move and removal

FTC-09 is a qualified XZ plate at the default 0.001 mm numerical budget.
Inspection finds 25 admitted round through-holes among 59 cylindrical groups;
partial slot walls, countersinks, stepped holes and breakouts remain unsupported.
Separate surface-model faces are not material in the selected closed solid.

```shell
aetheris imported-features inspect ftc09.stp --json
aetheris imported-features plan ftc09.stp --candidate "through-hole:step-1255+1282" --as MountHole --offset 15.09 0.05 --geometry-only --source-out move/revision.firmament --json
aetheris imported-features plan ftc09.stp --candidate "through-hole:step-1255+1282" --as MountHole --remove --geometry-only --source-out remove/revision.firmament --json
```

The first moves the 6.35 mm hole to X=-70, Z=19.1 mm while preserving its Y
support station. The second independently fills that original hole:

```firmament
Remove Source.MountHole {
    within: {
        min: Point3(-88.4mm, Source.MountHole.exit.Y, 15.7mm)
        max: Point3(-81.8mm, Source.MountHole.entry.Y, 22.4mm)
    }
}
```

Use the tracked [move](../../../fixtures/Regression/InlineStep/production/ftc09-round-move.firmament)
and [removal](../../../fixtures/Regression/InlineStep/production/ftc09-round-remove.firmament)
fixtures for complete runnable sources. Each Model admits exactly one move **or**
removal; batching/chaining edits is not yet qualified. Removal suppresses the void
walls and the two support inner loops; no guessed caps or stock reconstruction
are involved. Surviving topology retains identity. Retired faces have no successor
mapping. Build JSON exposes `importedHoleRemoval` and `inlineStepMigration.removals`
with actual retired walls and preserved counts. Removal creates no hole PMI.
Explicit authored PMI on a removal Model currently rejects pending successor
annotation rebinding; original vendor PMI is excluded only by explicit
`geometryOnly: true`, just as for moves.

## Historical compatibility

The older HostSize-based Box/shaft replacement prototype remains a compatibility
route, reporting `holeShaft-bounded-rebuild` and `residualSurgery: false`. It does
not provide this imported-body preservation contract. Its historical admission
limitations are recorded in the [audit](../../development/reports/2026-10/HOLE-RECOGNIZE-REPLACE-AUDIT-2026-10-20.md).
Use the pinned `within` form for the qualified production operation.

See the [production closeout](../../development/reports/2026-10/IMPORTED-HOLE-REVISION-PRODUCTION-2026-10-20.md)
for test evidence and the [design contract](../../development/architecture/imported-hole-revisions.md)
for ownership and limits.

See the [recovery-assistance qualification](../../development/reports/2026-10/IMPORTED-FEATURE-ASSISTANCE-2026-10-21.md)
for the cross-boss revision and admission evidence.

docs/public/firmament/incremental-compil.title: Incremental assembly compilation
docs/public/firmament/incremental-compil.markdown:
# Incremental assembly compilation

Keep a `FirmamentCompilationSession` alive across builds to reuse successful exact
part materializations. This is a bounded in-memory cache, with no new Firmament
syntax, disk cache, background process or dependency graph solver.

```csharp
using var session = new FirmamentCompilationSession(maximumDefinitions: 256);
var first = session.CompileProject(project);
var next = session.CompileProject(editedProject);
Console.WriteLine(next.Reuse?.ReusedDefinitions);
Console.WriteLine(next.Reuse?.RebuiltDefinitions);
```

`CompileFile(path)` and `Compile(source, sourceIdentity)` are also available.
Reuse evidence lists every requested distinct definition, whether it was reused,
and its reason. `Clear()` drops cached definitions; disposal releases the cache.
Calls within a session are serialized. Capacity uses deterministic insertion-order
eviction, retaining one latest entry per authored definition identity.

## What is reused

Ordinary template parts reuse the exact producer STEP payload, scalar/datum
semantic evidence and definition metadata. SectionChainFile, LoftFile and external
STEP definitions use their own source contents as inputs. Each hit reimports a
fresh BRep body from the original payload, avoiding geometry construction while
isolating the cache from public mutable topology and geometry stores. Metadata
arrays and semantic provenance are copied at the cache boundary.

Parsing, port binding, assembly solving, placement, mate residual checks and solid
interference checks still run. Display tessellation and export also run normally.
Moving a part can therefore reuse geometry while still reporting a new overlap.
Camera rotation continues to be a display operation, separate from compilation.

## Conservative invalidation

Keys include source identity, authored specialization identity and exact input
contents. Ordinary parts use the parser's entire non-assembly declaration catalog.
A shared feature, specification, declaration or relevant source-offset change
therefore invalidates ordinary parts conservatively. File-backed geometry uses its
own contents and does not depend on unrelated declaration changes. Assembly edits
reuse ordinary parts when the parser's declaration catalog is unchanged; edits
that alter blanked spans before/between declarations can invalidate them too.
Exact text is retained to protect source-span provenance rather than guessing
semantic equivalence from formatting.

Invalid inputs still go through current parsing and validation. Failed part
materializations are not stored. InlineStep resource dependencies, domain-specific
materializer delegates, geometry-valued semantic ports and non-STEP-backed producer
branches are outside this first cache qualification and use the uncached route.
There is no cross-process reuse; ordinary one-shot CLI commands retain their
existing behavior.

Web Runtime model sessions now retain this cache for assembly rebuilds and expose
reuse evidence under snapshot `timings.reuse`. Standalone Web Runtime part builds
continue through their existing uncached path. The .NET session API is also the
multi-document snapshot entry point; this does not add a multi-file browser editor.

## Guitar benchmark

```powershell
dotnet run --project demos/GuitarSurfacingX0 -c Release -- fixtures/Canonical/AssemblyInterfaces/GuitarX0/guitar.firmasm artifacts/local/incremental-guitar/timings.json
```

The harness measures cold and warm uncached compilation, then a populated-session
compile. Cache population is outside the measured incremental run. Every run
must produce byte-identical USD to the uncached baseline. Display preparation is
measured separately; process startup and dotnet build are excluded.

On the guitar snapshot before Concept-directed material seating was added,
measured compilation was 9.885 seconds
cold, 4.137 seconds warm uncached, and 0.244 seconds with the populated session
(about 17 times faster than warm uncached). All 53 definitions were reused; none
were rebuilt. Every run produced identical USD. Display preparation remained
separate: 0.568, 0.404 and 0.292 seconds respectively.

The guitar snapshot regression changes the neck's section geometry and proves
one definition rebuilt while 52 were reused, with a changed neck STEP hash.
Other regressions cover exact export parity, placement-only edits, fresh overlap
validation, specification/shared-recipe changes, failed inputs, missing documents,
caller mutation, bounded eviction and explicit Clear/Dispose.

Qualification passed the Release solution build (including Web Runtime), all
eight focused incremental tests, the fast core lane (1,004 tests), and the full
serial solution lane (4,050 tests). Fresh CLI assembly inspection also succeeded.
Web Runtime wiring is build-qualified here; this run did not perform a browser
interaction qualification.

Recorded evidence is under ignored `artifacts/local/pickup-features/`:
`incremental-final-timings.json`, `incremental-final-focused.log`,
`incremental-final-build.log`, `incremental-final-fast.log` and
`incremental-final-full.log`.

## Owl authoring update

Canonical assembly inspect --repeat 2 retains a session and reports per-build elapsed time and reuse/rebuild reasons. Appearance catalogs are excluded from geometry definition inputs; length-changing look-only edits reuse geometry. Placed route Point3 bindings are part of specialization identity, so endpoint placement changes invalidate the affected route. See [source-owned guitar authoring](source-owned-guitar-authoring.md).

docs/public/firmament/inventory.md.title: Inventory Records and module references
docs/public/firmament/inventory.md.markdown:
# Inventory Records and module references

Use `include` for a short composition whose declarations can share names in one
module. Use an `Inventory Record` when named, qualified dependencies make a larger
Assembly or Scene easier to organize. Neither form has a one- or two-part limit.

For a short typed import, name the resource directly:

```firmament
include bearing: Part = Step("vendor/bearing");
include drive: Assembly = Step("vendor/drive");
include bracket: Part = Firmament("parts/bracket").Bracket;
```

Use `bearing`, `drive` or `bracket` as an occurrence's initializer. These are
module references, with the same admission and identity rules as catalog members.
They do not inject the imported module's private declarations into the caller.
The original `include "parts/bolt";` remains declaration composition.

Firmament's importable module kinds are Part, Subassembly, Assembly and Scene.
Inventory references inside occurrence Patterns bind before expansion.
An Inventory member is a reference to an exported definition or admitted typed family. Adding it to a catalog
does not place geometry or establish a Mate; occurrences and relationships do that.

## A typed catalog

```firmament
Inventory Record Components {
  bracket: Part = Firmament("parts/bracket").Bracket
  drive: Subassembly = Firmament("assemblies/drive").Drive
  machine: Assembly = Firmament("assemblies/machine").Machine
  laboratory: Scene = Firmament("scenes/laboratory").Laboratory
  bearing: Part = Step("vendor/bearing")
  gearbox: Assembly = Step("vendor/gearbox")
}
```

This is a declaration fragment: provide the named files and exports in your project.
`Firmament(...)` selects a named root declaration; `Step(...)` supplies one exact
Part through the existing STEP importer. An explicit `Assembly = Step(...)`
retains the imported product tree, local occurrence transforms and shared leaf
geometry. Foreign hierarchy must be trustworthy: this form rejects the importer's
fallback that normalizes ambiguous multiplicity to a flat assembly. Missing or
ambiguous exports and kind mismatches reject. A Part still requires one body;
there is no implicit first-body selection.

An unchanged STEP Part consumed by `InlineStep` can retain
[semantic PMI](pmi.md#imported-semantic-pmi-and-units). Raw STEP components
materialized in an Assembly still require explicit
`Step("vendor/gearbox", geometryOnly: true)` when the source contains PMI;
part annotations are not promoted into assembly requirements. That exclusion
is retained in the binding receipt; the original file is untouched. It does not
relax geometry admission.

The normal spelling omits the extension. `Firmament("parts/bracket")` resolves
`.firmament` or `.firmasm`; `Step("vendor/bearing")` resolves `.step` or `.stp`.
Exactly one candidate must exist. An explicit extension is also accepted and is
the repair when both candidates exist. No search path, directory scan or global
package registry chooses a resource behind the author's back.

Locators resolve relative to the document containing the declaration and must
stay inside the existing allowed source root. Source snapshots resolve from their
provided document map, without reading files from disk. Snapshots can include
`.step`/`.stp` text assets and the optional lock alongside Firmament source.

## Place the referenced definitions

Given the catalog above, an Assembly can place its Part and Subassembly entries
through the existing product tree:

```firmament
Assembly Machine {
  <Assembly Machine>
    <Part Bracket = Components.bracket>
      Placement { from: Origin; to: World; }
    </Part>
    <Assembly Drive = Components.drive>
      Placement { from: Origin; to: World; translateLocal: [100mm, 0mm, 0mm]; }
    </Assembly>
  </Assembly>
  Anchor: Machine;
}
```

Use `<Assembly ...>` for both Assembly and Subassembly entries. They retain their
own locally solved product tree and published semantic contracts. Definition-owned
ports participate in the ordinary Interface/Mate solver. Tree nesting supplies no
mechanical relationship by itself. Existing interference checks still apply.

A Scene can place Part, Assembly/Subassembly or Scene entries. A nested Scene uses
its own units, rooms, definitions and placements, composed into its parent's world
frame. Its cameras remain private to that Scene; they do not replace parent cameras.
Nested Scene placement currently starts at `Origin`. For example, inside a Scene:

```firmament
<Scene laboratory = Components.laboratory>
  Placement { from: Origin; to: World; translateLocal: [10m, 0m, 0m]; }
</Scene>
```

Complete executable projects are [the machine](../../../fixtures/Regression/Inventory/machine.firmasm)
and [the factory Scene](../../../fixtures/Regression/Inventory/factory.firmament).

## Scope, exports and compatibility

Inventory names use PascalCase; member names use camelCase. Imported export names
and other domain/user symbols retain their authored spelling. Names resolve in
lexical scopes: a local Inventory shadows an outer Inventory, and sibling catalogs
remain private. Parameters, local values and Pattern iteration names protect their
own names from an enclosing catalog. Members are qualified, such as `Components.bracket`. Unknown
members, repeated names, invalid headers and unsupported adapters produce errors.

Root Model, Struct and Part declarations can satisfy a Part entry. Model and
Struct retain their existing geometry meanings inside the defining source; the
import does not redesign those frontends. Other root products in that file are
excluded from the selected Part's engineering compilation. Supporting Records,
Statics, Features, Templates and Concept scaffolding remain in their owning module.
Identical export or Record names in different imported modules do not collide.

Part and Subassembly entries can reference typed Template exports. Supply named
arguments at the occurrence, for example `<Assembly Cylinder = Units.cylinder<config: config>>`.
The common Template/Record binder checks the values against the definition's
signature. The definition keeps its own private Records, Statics, Inventory and
supporting declarations. Caller data does not replace that environment. A missing
specialization or an unknown argument rejects. Imported Part Templates currently
admit scalar/enum parameters; bind Record/type arguments in their defining module
or a typed Subassembly. The compiler rejects that unsupported boundary explicitly
rather than capturing a same-named private Record. Assembly and Scene Template imports
remain outside this bounded extension; export concrete products of those kinds.
Caller-defined type arguments also require specialization in the defining module.

`with` derives immutable Record values. It does not edit a module or mutate an
occurrence. A keyed `Set<CylinderConfig>` can contain `standardCylinder with { ... }`
entries and feed one Assembly Pattern. See [the V8 source](../../../fixtures/Canonical/EditableV8/engine.firmasm)
and its [single Cylinder definition](../../../fixtures/Canonical/EditableV8/assemblies/cylinder.firmament).

`include "parts/bolt";` remains admitted, including the established explicit
`.firmament` spelling. Includes share declarations in the consuming module. The
existing snapshot-only project-root-relative include spelling remains accepted
when a document-relative target is absent. Inventory always uses document-relative
locators. New code should use that rule for both forms.

The graph retains source files, dependency hashes, selected exports and Inventory
binding receipts in Assembly IR and the compiled Scene source model. Syntax, resource and Inventory lookup errors
retain original spans. Existing engineering lowerers still have bounded source
adapters; when they cannot provide a precise expression location, errors identify
the enclosing exported Part and disclose that limitation. This pass does not
claim complete generated-source provenance across every domain lowerer.

Unused Inventory entries are resolved and kind-checked; engineering geometry is
constructed for placed occurrences. Inventory availability does not imply an
occurrence count or a bill of materials.

## Typed resource metadata

Use ordinary typed Records, not another metadata dictionary syntax:

```firmament
Record VendorInfo { manufacturer: String partNumber: String revision: String }
Static BearingInfo: VendorInfo {
  manufacturer: "Example supplier"
  partNumber: "BRG-01"
  revision: "B"
}
Inventory Record Components {
  bearing: Part = Step("vendor/bearing", metadata: BearingInfo)
}
```

`metadata:` also works on `Firmament(...)` and typed short includes. The normal
Record binder checks the selected Static value. The binding receipt exposes its
type and flattened fields in Assembly IR. Resource metadata is descriptive; it
does not infer fits, manufacturing tolerances, materials or PMI, and it is not
automatically translated into vendor-specific AP242 properties. Two aliases for
the same imported Part retain one geometry definition even with different receipts.

Assembly `provenance: Release;` selects a typed release Record for the existing
AP242 header and product annotations. Canonical fields are `author: String`
(or a nested Record with `name: String`), `date: Date`, `version: Version`, and
`description: String`; `organization: String` is optional. Nested values refer to
other typed Static Records. Additional typed fields remain inspectable. Legacy
PascalCase fields remain accepted; providing both aliases rejects. Authors and
approval states must be supplied truthfully; the compiler invents neither.

## Optional dependency lock

Run `aetheris lock main.firmasm` to generate `firmament.lock.toml` beside the root.
Commit it with a reproducible project. Normal builds work without one; if a lock
exists, both validation and compilation enforce it. `aetheris validate main.firmasm
--locked` and `aetheris build main.firmasm --locked` additionally require its presence.
Compilation never rewrites the lock. Use `aetheris lock main.firmasm --update` for
an intentional dependency refresh.

Version 1 receipts contain the root identity and sorted dependency entries with
`path`, `format`, `hashKind` and `sha256`. STEP hashes cover exact file bytes;
Firmament hashes cover decoded UTF-8 source text. Snapshot STEP text is represented
by its UTF-8 bytes, so byte-identical receipts require identical encoding/BOM and
line endings. Paths use the loader's allowed source root: the Aetheris repository
root for repository files, otherwise the root document's directory; snapshot paths
are relative to the supplied project. A receipt belongs to one compilation root.
Unknown TOML fields, missing entries, changed dependencies and a different root
reject. Unused old entries are tolerated, and a lock command refresh removes them.

A changed STEP with bound `Recognize`/`Replace`/`Remove` intent refuses even an
explicit update. Reinspect and regenerate its selections in a new reviewed
revision/project receipt. Refreshing a hash cannot establish that a face still
has the same engineering meaning. Locks establish identity, not geometric quality
or permission to discard PMI. This version uses one conventional sidecar name;
custom lock locations and cross-root lock workspaces are outside this pass.

## InlineStep: local annotation and surgery

For mixed products, use Part/Assembly imports. Use `InlineStep` when a Model needs
to annotate or revise one imported body. It can select an existing STEP Part binding:

```firmament
Inventory Record Components { housing: Part = Step("vendor/housing", geometryOnly: true) }
Model Revision {
  units: mm
  InlineStep Source {
    from: Components.housing
    geometryOnly: true
    importTolerance: 0.01mm
  }
}
```

This fragment requires a matching generated lock. `from` and `path` are mutually
exclusive; `from` admits a STEP Part reference, not a native Firmament Part or
STEP Assembly. Direct `path: "vendor/housing.step"` remains supported. Explicit
`sha256` and `textSha256` remain compatible for self-contained pinned source;
the lock can supply the pin instead. Import tolerance is a numerical budget,
separate from authored dimensions. A locked, qualified body can be re-exported
unchanged without pretending to perform a replacement. Surgery still uses the
bounded [Recognize/Replace contracts](imported-feature-recognition.md).

docs/public/firmament/language-style.md.title: Firmament V2 language style
docs/public/firmament/language-style.md.markdown:
# Firmament V2 language style

Firmament uses mixed casing to make artifact definitions stand out from their
descriptions. Preferred casing does not rename authored identifiers; admitted
built-in spellings and aliases are defined by their compiler owners, without
global case folding. The [design proposal](../../development/proposals/casing-and-layout.md) records the reasoning.

| Role | Convention | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Artifact, declaration, construction form | PascalCase | `Model`, `Assembly`, `Scene`, `Room`, `Door`, `Window`, `Camera`, `Concept Struct`, `Profile`, `Feature`, `Placement`, `Mate` |
| Type and reusable recipe | PascalCase | `Length`, `PickupSpec`, `Humbucker`, `ControlKnob` |
| Concrete value, local geometry, occurrence, parameter, port | camelCase | `layout`, `outline`, `neckPickup`, `bottomSeat`, `width` |
| Built-in property label | camelCase | `units`, `size`, `from`, `translateLocal`, `minimumBendRadius` |
| Linking and scope word | lowercase | `using`, `as`, `from`, `to`, `on`, `over`, `with`, `return`, `include`, `expose`, `bind` |
| Scalar function | camelCase | `fretDistance`, `halfWidth` |
| Engineering symbol, enum, external identity | Preserve domain spelling | `XY`, `+Z`, `Outer`, `World`, `Origin`, `Fixed`, `Periodic`, `Stock`, `mm`, `m`, `304_Annealed` |

The root product may keep its definition name: `Assembly GuitarX0` and
`<Assembly GuitarX0>`. Feature constructors such as `Coil` remain PascalCase.
Use two-space indentation, spaces after list commas, blank lines between major
definitions, and separate closing tags for multiline occurrences. Preserve
numbers and units; formatting must not round derived surface controls.

User-defined identifiers and published members remain case-sensitive.
`beam`, `Beam`, `mainDeck`, and `MAIN_DECK` remain valid wherever an identifier
is admitted. Case alone does not assign a semantic type. Material designations,
standards, imported identities and part numbers retain their source spelling.
Existing PascalCase properties and supported historical aliases remain accepted,
without style warnings. Older examples need not be rewritten wholesale.

The table describes preferred style, not universal case folding. Profile endpoint
and mirror-header links prefer `from`/`to`, with `From`/`To` retained as aliases.
Mirror/radial fields prefer `across`, `source`, `about`, `count`, `angle`; their
PascalCase aliases bind to the same AST fields. Unknown and duplicate fields
reject. `Reverse`, `Close` and `TraceLoop` remain PascalCase geometry operations.
The formatter recognizes these linking/field positions structurally and preserves
authored identifiers. It does not impose this grammar on unrelated domain owners;
the [syntax review](../../development/reports/2026-10/FIRMAMENT-SYNTAX-REVIEW-2026-10.md) tracks the
remaining differences. Formatting is still not proof of successful compilation.

```firmament
Feature Coil(center: Point2, width: Length, depth: Length,
             height: Length, support: Plane) -> Boss {
  RoundedRect2 outline { center: center; size: [width, depth]; radius: 3mm }
  Profile section { Loop Outer { outline |> TraceLoop } }
  return Boss { on: support; profile: section; height: height }
}
```

## Safe formatting and bounded compatibility

`aetheris format <file.firmament|file.firmasm>...` prints preferred vocabulary
spellings; add `--write` to update the explicitly named files, or `--json` for a
change summary. This conservative pass preserves layout, comments, strings,
numeric literals, user names and occurrence identities. It prepares every input
before writing and refuses a rewrite that changes normalized source text.
It is **not validation**: validate/build the consuming assembly after a sweep.

The same pass is available as
`FirmamentLanguageAnalysisService.FormatConventions`. The existing standalone
V2 `Format` API also prefers these spellings while arranging part layout, and checks
both token equivalence and parser admission. For valid shared-syntax modules and
assemblies, `Format` selects the conservative spelling pass and preserves layout.
Validate imported modules with their consuming project's compiler; they are not
standalone parts. Formatting refuses malformed shared syntax and does not claim
that a module will compile in every consuming context.

Compatibility is scoped to schema-owned properties, AST-position Profile links
and symmetry fields, plus the bounded frame, assembly, point and wire
vocabularies used by the guitar. The parser maps
these aliases back to existing semantic identities. Unknown blocks, Record and
Static data, explicit station keys, named template/Feature arguments and dotted
members are not guessed or renamed by the formatter. Property completion accepts
either prefix spelling; generated entry snippets prefer the new spelling, while
schema/field identities in inspection APIs remain stable.

Historical lowercase `model`/`solid` scopes are compatibility syntax, not the
preferred style. Their primitive solids, immutable Box derivations, exposure
aliases and Hole modifications now bind through the shared AST and existing
engineering owners. The spelling pass leaves this grammar untouched: converting
`solid stock: Box` to `Box stock` also requires making inherited length units
explicit. Remaining PMI, lattice and manufacturing scopes retain their semantic
owners; see the [migration boundary](../../development/reports/2026-10/FIRMAMENT-LOWERCASE-AST-MIGRATION.md).

Use lowercase `using` and `as` in Profile headers and pipelines. `Using` and `As`
remain grammar-position aliases, and convention formatting prefers lowercase.
This does not rename a user-defined member or identifier named `As`.

Authored names require a manual, binding-aware edit. For example, `.Frame`,
`.BottomSeat`, `Spec`, `R` and `H` can be authored public contracts; their casing
must change together with every declaration and use. The guitar sweep deliberately
retains its established public ports, template argument names, occurrence paths
and generated span keys. Its private pickup geometry, record fields and scalar
functions demonstrate the quieter convention. Remaining casing stragglers are
acceptable. An exhaustive migration or symbol rename service is outside this pass.

Current assembly definition identities can retain whitespace in specialization
arguments. Preserve those argument spellings when preserving identities; this
formatter does so. General whitespace canonicalization of definition keys is a
separate compiler concern.

Semicolons are optional wherever the owning grammar already admits newline/block structure as a field delimiter.
The bounded `Function` expressions and `Points` recipes currently require explicit
semicolon terminators; see [Concept points and Functions](concept-points-and-functions.md).
Root assembly `provenance` selections and `Pmi Note` fields also require explicit
semicolons; see [PMI](pmi.md). Use semicolons when they improve readability in dense one-line Records, Tables, or `ProfileDelta` members; their presence must not select a different language path where optional.

Built-in aliases exist only where the owning grammar admits them.
A field uses `name: value`; braces delimit
declarations, brackets delimit lists, and semicolons are optional where the
owning grammar is unambiguous.

Different target grammars are intentional. Native Model geometry uses axis faces and semantic selectors; Sheet Metal uses named planar regions and paths; native and imported Analysis use body-qualified faces; Assembly uses typed roles, ports, interfaces, and DatumFrame references. Similar engineering ideas do not make these value types interchangeable.

Firmament V1 is compatibility history, not canonical V2 authoring. Speculative or expected-failure `.firmfixture` bodies do not define the public language.

## Preview 3 migration note

Preview 3 originally documented PascalCase vocabulary and fields. Its supported
lowercase and `solid name: Primitive` inputs remain accepted where documented.
New examples prefer mixed casing and direct named primitives with `units: mm`.
