docs/public/firmament/section-chains.md.markdown:
# Section chains

A SectionChain builds a surface or closed body from an ordered sequence of framed profiles. G1 is the normal freeform authoring default; explicit G0/Ruled remains available when straight generators are intentional.

For two framed circle or ellipse profiles, [`Loft` and `Loft<Hollow>`](loft.md) provide concise ruled authoring with explicit point correspondence and optional twist. They lower into the same SectionChain path.

## Circular stations and checked dimensions

Use a capped `SectionChain` when framed profiles and their correspondence express the design. The complete [circular-station witness](../../../fixtures/Regression/CodeNativeAssembly/fastener-sections.firmament) uses named `Static` lengths, `Circle2` guides, traced Profiles and four named Sections. For a shaft built from cylindrical and conical masses, [primitive Compose](../reference/language/solids-and-features.md#coaxial-primitive-compose) and a named edge finish express that intent more directly. Build the SectionChain witness through the normal command:

```powershell
aetheris build fixtures/Regression/CodeNativeAssembly/fastener-sections.firmament --out artifacts/local/fastener-sections.step --json
```

The shared compile-time binder checks scalar `Static` values before their nominal dimensions reach profiles and station frames. Manufacturing tolerances on those values are currently rejected with `section-chain-tolerance-consumer-unsupported`; this domain does not project them into PMI.

Declare Concept plane values as fields when tracing them into construction frames:

```firmament
Concept Struct stations {
    tip: Plane { origin: [0mm, 0mm, 0mm]; normal: [0, 0, 1]; up: [0, 1, 0] }
}
Construction Plane tipFrame { trace: stations.tip }
```

A full circular profile gets four exact arc spans named `CircleQuadrant0` through `CircleQuadrant3`, starting at local +X and progressing counterclockwise. Corresponding circles share these span identities even when their guide names differ. In the `G0`/`Ruled` lane, coaxial matching arc spans produce exact cylindrical or conical supports. Rotated phase, different sweeps or noncoaxial stations do not qualify for that analytic recognition. Existing explicitly segmented profiles retain their authored span names.

For assembly placement, expose a terminal frame such as `Body.Section.Head.Frame` and bind it through an Interface and Mate. The [bracket and fastener assembly](../../../fixtures/Regression/CodeNativeAssembly/assembly.firmasm) uses primitive Compose with an explicit design-owned seating frame instead. A mathematical seating frame identifies placement; it does not itself assert planar material at the frame origin.

## Sections and correspondence

```text
Section0 -> Section1 -> Section2 -> Section3
```

Each `Section` owns a stable `SectionId`, a complete right-handed frame (`Origin`, `XAxis`, `YAxis`, `Normal`), and one closed outer `SectionProfile`. A profile is an ordered loop of semantic spans such as `South`, `East`, `North`, and `West`; its declared seam identifies the first span. X3's qualified profile curves are line, circular arc, and non-rational polynomial B-spline.

Adjacent sections use one-to-one semantic span correspondence. Matching IDs may establish strong semantic identity, while explicit `AdjacentSectionCorrespondence` records the mapping in the flagship. Aetheris does not silently use nearest points, nearest edges, or tessellated vertex indices to define topology. The X3 lane requires the same span count and seam-relative order on both sides of a transition.

Continuity intent and transition law are separate. `Continuity: G0` selects the existing `Ruled` law. `Continuity: G1` selects local `SmoothPolynomial` transitions. G0 makes adjacent surfaces meet. G1 also makes their tangent planes agree, so highlights and silhouettes flow smoothly across section boundaries.

For G1, Aetheris transforms corresponding polynomial controls into world space and derives a shared tangent field at every section. Interior tangents use a nonuniform three-section quadratic-derivative stencil; cumulative frame-origin chord length is the station metric, and endpoints use a bounded one-sided chord derivative. Three deterministic magnitude policies are qualified for foldover and overshoot before the Judgment Engine compares bending energy and normal variation. Continuity is a hard eligibility constraint, never an aesthetic score.

Each matched span becomes an exact non-rational cubic transition in the longitudinal direction. Lines are exactly degree-elevated to cubic when needed; compatible polynomial B-splines retain their boundary geometry and knot structure. Circular arcs used in G1 now enter the bounded surfacing-only normalization described below. Mixed incompatible existing polynomial knot structures still fail with `section-chain-g1-degree-limit`; Aetheris never introduces rational weights or a faceted fallback. The G0 path still preserves exact plane/cylinder/cone recognition where applicable.

Every internal section edge is allocated once. The preceding and following transition faces use that same edge, curve, vertices, and parameter direction. For G0, editing one section rebuilds its two adjacent transitions. G1 has a bounded dependency neighborhood: editing section `i` recomputes tangent fields `i-1..i+1` and may rebuild transitions `i-2->i-1` through `i+1->i+2`. Distant transitions and terminal conditions remain preserved in `SectionChainEditDelta`; there is no global loft solve.

Every transition and cap coedge also owns a face-local pcurve. Aetheris builds these through the same bounded Plane/Cylinder/non-rational-B-spline machinery used by trimmed SURF faces, then independently checks reconstruction deviation, surface-domain containment, both oriented endpoints, and UV loop closure. The two faces meeting at an internal section therefore share one authoritative 3D edge while retaining separate local 2D representations.

The terminal vocabulary is `Cap` and `Open`. `Cap/Cap` closes the two planar profile loops and yields a closed solid. Any open terminal is truthfully classified as `OpenShell`; the general STEP command currently emits only the capped witnesses.

## Sweep relationship

A Sweep transports one profile through a trajectory. A SectionChain allows the profile itself to change at explicitly framed stations. Both use ordered geometry and stable parameter correspondence, but the current circular Sweep keeps its specialized line/arc-path materializer. That path preserves Paperclip's exact cylinders and tori, planar transported-frame policy, and sweep-specific clearance checks; forcing it through generic ruled faces would weaken the representation.

## Firmament authoring

SectionChain authoring reuses ordinary `Concept Path` and `Profile` declarations, including `Profile ... Using` an explicit `Concept Struct ... On XY` sketch. A `Section` associates that reusable 2D profile with a named right-handed `Construction Plane`; it does not expose vertices, faces, or raw BRep surfaces. The [explicit sketch fixture](../../../fixtures/Canonical/SectionChain/explicit-sketch-ruled.firmament) shows two differently sized sections on tilted frames.

```firmament
Concept Path NoseOutline {
    Start: Point2(-5mm, -3mm)
    Heading: 0deg
    Line Bottom { Length: 10mm }
    Line Right { Turn: 90deg; Length: 6mm }
    Line Top { Turn: 90deg; Length: 10mm }
    Close Left
}
Profile NoseProfile From NoseOutline

SectionChain Fairing {
    Continuity: G1
    Section Nose {
        Frame: NoseFrame
        Profile: NoseProfile
        Seam: Bottom
    }
    Section Front {
        Frame: FrontFrame
        Profile: FrontProfile
        Seam: Bottom
    }
    Start: Cap
    End: Cap
}
```

Equal ordered span identities infer correspondence. When identities differ, author a `Correspond` block with `From`, `To`, and explicit `Source -> Target` rows. Missing, incomplete, reordered, or duplicate mappings fail before BRep construction. Omit `Continuity` for the G1 default, or write `Continuity: G0` and `Transition: Ruled` for intentionally faceted/straight-generator construction. G2 is not claimed. `Cap` and `Open` remain separate termination intent; planar caps meet the transition at G0 unless separately designed.

```firmament
Correspond NoseToFront {
    From: Nose
    To: Front
    Bottom -> South
    Right -> East
    Top -> North
    Left -> West
}
```

Profile coordinates use the construction plane's local axes: profile X follows frame `XAxis`, profile Y follows `YAxis`, and the chain progresses between section origins/normals. If one Profile is referenced by several Sections, editing it changes each of those yielded states; locality is the union of their adjacent transitions. The current CLI reports one compiled state but does not yet compare two authored files or serialize `SectionChainEditDelta`.

A SectionChain is useful as a geometric generator: each framed profile is an ordered state, and Aetheris materializes the transition between adjacent yielded states. This is a mental model, not a general-purpose iterator language.

## CLI

For an authored standalone SectionChain, use the domain command:

```powershell
aetheris section-chain build fixtures/Canonical/SectionChain/eight-section-ergonomic.firmament --out artifacts/local/handle.step --json
```

Ordinary `build` currently routes standalone Profile/SectionChain source into the extrusion parser and can report `profile-extrude-missing-or-mismatched`. This does not mean the chain needs an Extrude. BodyState `AddSectionChain` and `RemoveSectionChain` use ordinary `build` as shown below. A Section's `Frame` currently names a `Construction Plane` alias; a direct `ConceptStruct.PlaneMember` reference is not accepted there.

Generate and inspect the eight-section flagship through the production BRep/STEP path:

```powershell
aetheris section-chain inspect flagship --json
aetheris section-chain build flagship-g0 --out artifacts/local/surf-x4/surf-x4-ergonomic-g0.step --json
aetheris section-chain build flagship --out artifacts/local/surf-x4/surf-x4-ergonomic-g1.step --json
```

On a source checkout where the tool is not installed, replace `aetheris` with `dotnet run --project Aetheris.CLI -c Release --`.

The compatibility command supports `flagship` (G1), `flagship-g0`, `twist`, and `two-profile`. Its structured inspection/evidence includes continuity intent, tangent derivation, candidate/rejection metrics, the selected policy, measured G0/G1 errors, representation, pcurves, topology, SHA-256, and STEP reimport. Its sibling preview uses the same general [BRep wireframe renderer](../reference/wireframe.md) exposed by `aetheris wireframe`; SectionChains no longer own a private visualization implementation.

A bounded `BodyState` composition lane. `AddSectionChain` retains the chain, terminal Section, semantic support, span correspondence, authorized envelope, preservation contracts, and requirements as one typed replay operation. `RemoveSectionChain` retains the changing-profile tool and both explicit penetration supports. Neither lowers to public `Union` or `Difference`; a SectionChain-specific builder emits the known shared topology directly.

The admitted additive lane attaches an `Open` first terminal to the complete planar `HousingSideEast` boundary, progresses in support-relative +X, and caps the free end. The admitted subtractive lane runs an `Open/Open` four-line-span chain monotonically from `HousingSideWest` to `HousingSideEast`, strictly inside the housing Y/Z boundary. These restrictions make intended attachment, remote intersection, connectedness, and opening topology explicit and deterministic.

Canonical BodyState sources are [`surf-x3b-add-section-chain-grip.firmament`](../../../fixtures/Canonical/BodyState/surf-x3b-add-section-chain-grip.firmament) and [`surf-x3b-remove-section-chain-duct.firmament`](../../../fixtures/Canonical/BodyState/surf-x3b-remove-section-chain-duct.firmament). Build them with the ordinary command:

```powershell
aetheris build fixtures/Canonical/BodyState/surf-x3b-add-section-chain-grip.firmament --out artifacts/local/surf-x3b-add-section-chain-grip.step --json
aetheris build fixtures/Canonical/BodyState/surf-x3b-remove-section-chain-duct.firmament --out artifacts/local/surf-x3b-remove-section-chain-duct.step --json
```

The current canonical grip qualifies 24 faces, 50 edges, 28 vertices, and 100 pcurves after STEP reimport. The canonical duct qualifies 24 faces, 54 edges, 32 vertices, and 108 pcurves. These are regression evidence for the named fixtures, not general formulas for arbitrary chains.

## Current limits

The standalone lane has one closed outer loop, no holes, same-topology one-to-one correspondence, G0/G1 pairwise transitions, and Cap/Open terminals. It checks frame handedness, loop closure/orientation, profile self-intersection, physical spacing, semantic mapping order, transition Jacobian foldover, bounded overshoot, non-neighbour crossings, remote cap penetration, pcurves, and realized continuity. The triangle proxy is conservative detection evidence, not a global proof. BodyState composition remains limited to the planar housing support lanes; arbitrary supports, branches, G2, rail lofts, topology-changing correspondence, and arbitrary freeform Boolean composition fail closed.

Stable diagnostic families include `section-chain-correspondence-missing`, `section-chain-correspondence-duplicate`, `section-chain-profile-orientation-mismatch`, `section-chain-transition-foldover`, `section-chain-self-intersection`, and `section-chain-pcurve-error`. `section-chain validate` returns a nonzero exit status and emits no STEP when any of these blocks materialization. Transition identities are formatted `SourceSection->TargetSection` in structured evidence and diagnostic detail.

## Bounded profile normalization and curvature inspection

The [rounded-section fixture](../../../fixtures/Canonical/SectionChain/normalized-rounded-sections.firmament) admits ordinary line/circular-corner profiles to the G1 lane. `ApproximationTolerance: 0.00001mm` is the default optional SectionChain field. Source arcs remain semantic arcs; only the smooth surfacing construction uses their normalized counterparts. Ordinary profile extrusion and the G0 route are unchanged.

Each arc uses degree-5 non-rational Hermite polynomials that match its endpoints, tangents, and second derivatives. The Judgment Engine selects from 1, 2, 4, 8, or 16 segments, admitting only candidates whose error bound meets tolerance, then preferring fewer segments. Corresponding curves share segmentation across the chain. A line corresponding to an arc is represented exactly in the same degree/knot basis. Existing polynomial tracks remain unchanged; an existing polynomial opposite an arc must already have the selected compatible degree and knots. Arbitrary degree/knot conversion is not inferred.

The positional bound is `sqrt(2) * radius * abs(segmentSweep)^6 / (720 * 64)`, plus a coordinate-scale roundoff allowance. This follows the componentwise quintic Hermite remainder; dense sample error is reported separately. Endpoints and endpoint tangent directions are also checked numerically. The hard limit is degree 5 and 16 spans per source arc. A tighter unachievable tolerance fails with `section-chain-normalization-tolerance-unmet`, without STEP or a modified body.

`section-chain inspect`, `validate`, and `build` report `profileNormalization`: source identities/types, degree, segment count, tolerance, bound, sampled deviation, endpoint position/tangent error, control hash, and deterministic segment choices. `geometricJoins` reports both internal section joins and neighboring profile-span seams. It evaluates analytic first/second B-spline derivatives and compares second fundamental forms in a shared orthonormal world tangent basis. The curvature residual has units 1/mm; it is not a comparison of raw second parameter derivatives. G0 and tangent-plane checks must pass before a curvature status is assigned. Caps are not included in this join report.

`G2WithinSampledTolerance` is an inspection result at the reported samples, not a new G2 construction guarantee. The samples include endpoints, 33 regular parameters, and applicable spline knots. The rounded-section fixture measures zero position/normal mismatch but a 0.125/mm curvature jump at its R8 line/arc seams. Those joins are G1. Arc normalization does not smooth away source curvature jumps. `Continuity: G2` remains rejected for SectionChain.

Editing a section normally retains the existing bounded G1 derivative neighborhood. If an edit changes the common normalization segment count, all transitions on that chain must be regenerated; the edit delta truthfully reports this wider dependency and does not claim the terminations are preserved. Source semantic span identities remain stable. See the [SURF-G2-X1 progression report](../../development/history/eras/08-domain-expansion.md) for the remaining G2 boundary-condition work.

## Owl authoring update

Generic Profile recipes and keyed Section Patterns now lower inline Concept frame/Profile values through this same binder. Generated section keys and associations appear in root-aware inspection. See [source-owned guitar authoring](source-owned-guitar-authoring.md).

docs/public/firmament/sheet-metal.md.markdown:
# Sheet Metal

Authored Sheet Metal uses a specialized semantic model: a base region, named flanges and bend strips, and cuts on named planar regions. It can emit formed STEP, thickness-bearing flat STEP, and flat SVG; it also carries material, K-factor, DFM, semantic layout, and manufacturing definitions on qualified routes.

A closed boundary has the same `Profile` meaning in mechanical and sheet-metal
construction. Use canonical 2D shapes for a compact boundary, or the ordinary
`Loop`/`Segment`/pipeline forms for an authored boundary. The consuming operation
then checks its own capabilities.

**Complete file — a bracket with a reusable blank and rounded opening:**

```firmament
Profile blank = Rect2 { center: [40mm, 25mm]; size: [80mm, 50mm] }
Profile ventilation = Slot2 { center: [0mm, 0mm]; length: 12mm; width: 6mm }

SheetMetal MountingBracket {
    thickness: 1.5mm
    material: "5052-H32 Aluminum"
    kFactor: 0.42
    Base deck { profile: blank }
    Flange upright {
        from: deck.Rear
        length: 30mm
        angle: 90deg
        insideRadius: 2mm
        direction: Up
    }
    Cut vent { on: deck; profile: ventilation; at: Point2(40mm, 20mm) }
}
```

`Profile blank = Rect2 { ... }` is also admitted in a mechanical Model and consumed
by `Extrude stock { profile: blank; from: 0mm; to: 1.5mm }`. The shape's existing
field schema, closure checks and exact Profile lowerer remain authoritative.
`Profile copy = blank` names an immutable derived boundary. Detailed boundary
editing continues to use the ordinary `Profile { from: ... }` and `Replace` forms.
There is no separate sheet-metal sketch language for new named boundaries.

Use PascalCase for constructs/types and domain symbols (`Base`, `Rect2`, `Up`,
`Rear`), camelCase for fields and authored value names. PascalCase field spellings
remain compatible. Semicolons and newlines separate fields in the sheet,
semantic-layout, ProfileDelta, manufacturing and PMI owners. Unknown fields,
unknown statements, duplicate aliases and unsupported header placements reject.

### Layout, requirements and release data

A layout Datum is a named region-local **construction point**. It is not a PMI
DatumFeature or a 3D DatumFrame. Declare `Datum center { on: deck; at: deck.Center }`
in a Concept Struct, then refer to `layout.center`. `at` admits `Point2(...)`,
legacy tuples, region centers and scoped Datums, optionally plus a `Vector2`
offset. Short names resolve in their layout; forward references work and cycles
reject. Layout `on XZ` is unsupported and rejects rather than producing XY.

Keep reusable construction data in Concept Structs; put material operations in
the consuming SheetMetal body. A single legacy Concept Struct containing sheet
effects remains supported with its existing identities. Multiple implicit effect
bundles reject as ambiguous. `intent:` does not select between several effect
bundles; move those operations into the sheet body.

Sheet fields consume the same checked scalar Static/Record values as mechanical
models. `Require name => predicate` uses the common Boolean/Concept evaluator,
and `SheetMetal name: Contract` checks every structural member regardless of
semicolons. Legacy brace Require records still support RequiredMembers,
EqualSize, EqualPitch and Mirror. Spatial checks require one owning region;
Mirror accepts `axis: X` or `axis: Y` when its `about` names a Datum. Arbitrary
geometric constraint solving is not part of these checks.

Named `Set<Point2>` values and ordinary `Pattern name over points { point =>
Recipe(point) }` use the existing Feature/Pattern expansion. Sheet recipes may
return `Hole` or `Cut`; mechanical `Hole<Shaft>` is a different domain operation.
Generated identities use Pattern/Set keys, such as `mounting.left`, independently
of entry order. See the complete
[keyed recipe example](../../../fixtures/Regression/SheetMetalSemantics/keyed-features.firmament).
The legacy centered Count/Pitch Pattern retains its placement and index IDs.
Its `Slot` and `Rectangle` feature spellings both retain the historical capsule
with a straight-run Length; use shared Rect2/Slot2 Profiles for new boundaries.

`Manufacturing release { ... }` describes material/process data and general
allowance policies. A sheet selects it with `manufacturing: release`. A single
legacy release remains implicitly selectable. Multiple unselected releases
reject; reusable unselected releases are still checked for invalid fields.
An ordinary quoted process string may contain `//` or `#`.

Use one root-contained `Pmi { ... }` for explicit projection. One named top-level
Pmi remains compatible; multiple Pmi blocks reject. PMI does not require a
Manufacturing block. `Dimension width { kind: Linear; target: deck;
dimension: plate.width }` projects a bound toleranced Length; geometry consumes
its nominal. Record/Static origins are retained on the bound dimension. Literal
`value` and `tolerance: PlusMinus(...)` remain compatible but cannot be combined
with `dimension:`. Allowances must be nonnegative, quantities positive integers,
and kinds one of Thickness, Linear or Diameter.

Sheet PMI targets named regions, bends, parts, authored cuts and generated
features. `DatumFeature`, `Position` with `datumRefs`, and `Note` (legacy
`Annotation`) retain their existing AP242 roles and face associations. General
GD&T support is not implied. Check the exported result with `analyze --json`.
The complete [typed layout/release example](../../../fixtures/Regression/SheetMetalSemantics/modern-layout-release.firmament)
uses a Record requirement for both construction and PMI.

ProfileDelta fields use the same AST consumption and dimensional binding.
Prefer `anchor: FromStart(0mm)` / `FromEnd(...)` / `CenteredAt(...)`; the historic
`Anchor: FromStart 0mm` spelling remains a local compatibility production.

### Coordinates and capability admission

A Base currently admits one axis-aligned rectangular Profile in local XY. Its
minimum corner becomes the physical base origin; it is not silently recentered.
An optional Base `origin` adds a physical translation. A circle or arbitrary
polygon cannot serve as this rectangular base merely because it has bounds.
Non-axis-aligned or non-XY bases reject explicitly.

A Cut admits one closed line/arc Profile or a circle. Its coordinates are local to
its named sheet region. Optional `at: Point2(x, y)` adds a translation; without
`at`, the authored Profile coordinates are used directly. Curves remain exact in
the formed and flat contours. Inner islands, ellipses, splines and non-XY Profile
frames are not admitted by this sheet cut owner. Crossing a region boundary or
bend zone still rejects. Structural parsing alone does not admit a geometry
capability.

`Slot2.length` is the **overall** rounded-slot length, including its semicircular
ends, exactly as in mechanical profiles. `Circle2` uses `radius`; `Rect2` uses
`size`. This avoids the old sheet-specific dimension vocabulary for new Profiles.

The sheet region's `Rear`/`Front` members are attachment semantics; a Profile's
`Top`/`Bottom` members name its planar boundary. They are not global-axis aliases.
Named regions, attachment paths, ProfileDelta programs and formed/flat identity
remain useful sheet-metal concepts; ordinary Profile boundaries and edits now
feed them through the shared boundary authority.

### Compatibility

Existing `Base: Rectangle(w, d)` and named
`Base deck { Profile: Rectangle { Width: 80mm; Height: 50mm; }; }` retain their
geometry. To modernize an implicit Base while preserving its established region
and bend identities, use `base: blank` with a named rectangular Profile. This
feeds the same Profile capability binder as `Base deck { profile: blank }`.
Choosing a named Base changes the public identity family; it is not a cosmetic
rewrite of the implicit Base field. The
[compatibility witnesses](../../../fixtures/Compatibility/FirmamentV2/SheetMetal/README.md)
check exact formed STEP, region/bend/feature IDs and flat hashes.

Legacy cuts using `Profile: Rectangle`, `Circle` or `Slot`, including
inline dimensions and tuple placement, remain admitted. **Legacy `Slot` cuts are
rectangular** in this route; they are not silently converted into capsules. Use a
named `Profile` built with `Slot2` when a rounded slot is intended.

Sheet Metal does not use a Model `units` declaration in this authored route;
dimensional fields carry explicit units. `thickness`, `material`, `kFactor`, and
the named Base belong directly in the `SheetMetal` body.

[`modern-bracket.firmament`](../../../fixtures/Regression/SheetMetalSyntax/modern-bracket.firmament)
and its legacy reference qualify formed STEP parity. Build and flatten it:

```powershell
aetheris build fixtures/Regression/SheetMetalSyntax/modern-bracket.firmament --output artifacts/local/bracket-formed.step --json
aetheris sheetmetal flatten fixtures/Regression/SheetMetalSyntax/modern-bracket.firmament --step artifacts/local/bracket-flat.step --svg artifacts/local/bracket-flat.svg --json
```

[`profile-delta-tab-family.firmament`](../../../fixtures/Canonical/SheetMetal/profile-delta-tab-family.firmament)
is the data-driven edge-edit example: a finite Table selects `ProfileTabSpec`,
`with` derives the shop variant, and the standard-library `ProfileDelta Tab`
modifies the wall edge while preserving formed/flat semantic identity.

Flat inspection distinguishes `MaterialArea` from `BoundingArea`. `MaterialArea` is exact line/arc integration of the final flat material contour after additive ProfileDelta regions, notches, holes, cutouts, and overlap clipping. `BoundingArea` is only the rectangular nesting envelope. If no validated exact blank contour exists, material area is reported as unavailable rather than reconstructed from feature bookkeeping.

Sheet Metal holes use `Hole Mount { On: Base; Center: (40mm, 20mm); Diameter: 8mm; }`. Model-domain `Hole<Shaft>` is deliberately rejected here with `sheetmetal-hole-domain-syntax`. `On` targets a named planar semantic region (`Base`, a named flange, or a verified exposed region/path), not `face(+Z)`. Manufacturing PMI likewise uses `DatumFeature A { Target: Base; }` inside `Pmi`; Model-domain `Datum`/`face(-Z)` syntax is rejected with `sheetmetal-pmi-domain-syntax`.

The JSON `part.features` count is the number of lowered cuts/openings in `SheetMetalPartIr`; bends are reported separately as `part.bends`. Authoring and imported reconstruction are separate workflows. Commands such as `sheetmetal recognize`, `recover-flat`, and `recover` operate on imported STEP and may be partial; they do not turn arbitrary geometry into authoritative authored intent.


### Domain schemas before assembly binding

`Use SheetMetal.ProductFamilies` supplies the family's Record schemas as well as
its Templates. `EnclosureProductFamilies.Compile` and `SheetMetalFirmament.Compile`
resolve those imports through the same owner before shared value admission. API
clients using the low-level Assembly parser directly can call
`SheetMetalFirmament.ResolveImports(source)` first; the Core parser does not
invent or duplicate SheetMetal schemas. This preparation does not materialize
geometry or grant build success.

docs/public/firmament/sketcher.md.title: IntelliDraft and Profile dimensions in Helios
docs/public/firmament/sketcher.md.markdown:
# IntelliDraft and Profile dimensions in Helios

IntelliDraft edits ordinary Firmament source. There is no separate saved
sketch model, browser constraint solver or mesh-to-profile conversion.

## Construction, trace, part

**IntelliDraft** in the viewport toolbar authors the same retained construction
used in Firmament code. A new draft opens ready to draw: the first shape creates
its layout (a Concept Struct on the plane chosen in the toolbar, XY by default).
`Rect2` supplies right angles and equal, parallel opposite sides. Its type and
dimensions remain authoritative when Trace selects boundary spans from its named
edges and corners.

The toolbar draws lines, arcs, rectangles, circles, ellipses, slots and rounded
rectangles; the line, circle and rounded tools have a type menu. Keys: V select, L line, A arc, R rectangle, C circle, E ellipse,
S slot, U rounded, T trace, F fit, Delete removes the selection, Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y
undo and redo, Escape steps back. A tool stays active after drawing and proposes
the next free name (`rect1`, `rect2`, …). Points snap to a grid that follows the
zoom; Alt snaps to 0.1 mm.

- **Line** writes a `Line2` between named points. Ends that land on an existing
  named point (a rectangle corner, another line's end) reuse it; new ends are
  written as `Point2 <line>Start` / `<line>End`. The line menu also declares an
  `Axis2 { origin; direction }`: an unbounded reference direction that is shown
  on the canvas but never traced.
- **Arc** (in the circle menu, key A) drags from the centre to the start, then
  clicks the end (15° steps; Alt is free). It writes
  `Arc2 { center; from; to }`: the counter-clockwise arc between named points.
  Named points on an arc split it into spans for tracing.
- The rounded menu also draws `SmoothRoundedRect2` (continuous-curvature
  corners) with its `cornerExtent`.

While drawing, a click snaps to a named point, a line's midpoint, a point on a
curve, or the level of (or the line under) a named point, and a marker says which.
Snaps only place points; nothing remembers them. Alt draws freely.

Selected shapes show their dimensions on the canvas; click one to type a value.
A value can also be an expression over parameters, such as `outerWidth / 2`
(parameter names complete as you type); it is written to source, so the dimension
becomes driven and shows in parentheses. **Align … to** moves the selected shape so
its edges or centre line up with another shape, which stays put; this too is
written as plain coordinates.
Values driven by an expression are dashed and read-only. Resizing a shape whose
edge is lined up with another shape's edge asks once whether to move that shape
too; nothing is stored, and drags never ask. Rename and Delete act on the selected
shape, line, arc or axis. A shape that is part of the traced outline is not
deleted until the outline is retraced without it.

The sidebar's searchable shape list selects retained construction. Its checkboxes
show or hide construction in the workspace; hidden shapes are excluded from
picking and alignment, but their source and any traced Profile remain intact.
Temporary alignment guides help placement while dragging; they do not link
shapes. Hold Alt to bypass alignment.

Choose **Trace** and click inside an enclosed area to trace it in one step, or click
the edges of the outline on the canvas: rectangle
sides, lines and arcs between named points, across shapes. Click order and
direction do not matter; the outline is written counter-clockwise. The sidebar
shows whether the outline is closed. The canvas marks open ends (nothing continues
from them) and ends that meet only by position (two named points that happen to
coincide, which an edit could pull apart). **Use this outline** writes the Profile;
**Use whole shape outline** traces one closed shape. Picks are also available
as a list under **Edges as a list**.

Explicit dimension-driven relationships remain optional under **Advanced**.
The top-right inset preset intentionally creates expressions and shared inputs;
it is not the default placement behavior. Existing expressions remain read-only
at their derived controls and are edited through their inputs, never flattened
by a drag.

Named **Point**, **Line**, **Circle** guides and Paths remain under **Advanced**,
with a manual guide trace. Alternatively, create a **Path**, then append named
Line or Arc steps with lengths, radii and signed turns. **Close Path with line**
explicitly adds a closing line. **Trace this Path** resolves that boundary to a
Profile. Trace's **Close** checks an already closed boundary and never supplies a
missing edge.

Complete examples:

- [L plate from independently placed rectangles](../../../fixtures/Regression/IntelliDraft/independent-rectangles-l.firmament).
- [L plate from explicitly related rectangles](../../../fixtures/Regression/IntelliDraft/rectangles-l.firmament)
  and [its dimension-driven revision](../../../fixtures/Regression/IntelliDraft/rectangles-l-revised.firmament).
- [Low-level L plate from named points and lines](../../../fixtures/Regression/IntelliDraft/named-lines-l.firmament).
- [D plate from a circle span and chord](../../../fixtures/Regression/IntelliDraft/arc-chord-d.firmament).
- [Rounded outline from ordered Path steps](../../../fixtures/Regression/IntelliDraft/line-arc-path.firmament).

Choose an extrusion depth, **Extrude Profile**, then **Build and use part**.
Incomplete construction is staged source, not a valid engineering part. Compiler
rejection, including a move that breaks an existing Profile, retains the preceding candidate and the current built model. Undo and
Redo navigate staged edits; Cancel discards them. A complete candidate must pass
the normal build before replacing the current document. Updating construction
in an existing part is one normal undoable source transaction.

The advanced objects list edits named points and literal driving dimensions. Point moves
retain connected Line2 references. Expression-driven positions and dimensions
are not replaced with coordinates. Canvas point placement rounds to a 0.1 mm
grid; explicit typed values can use finer precision. Paths created by the UI use
XY; the layout frame banner identifies local axes and the world-space normal.

## Editing an existing part's Profile

**IntelliDraft** also opens on parts written in code. It projects the document's
Profiles; when there is more than one, a **Profile** menu chooses which. Double-
clicking a Profile or shape node in the graph opens IntelliDraft on it. Shapes the
Profile consumes outside any layout are listed with the layout's shapes and are
edited the same way, on the canvas or in the sidebar. A Profile on another plane
shows that plane under the workflow steps. **Command palette → New IntelliDraft
part** starts an empty draft.

Dimensions follow the source:

- A literal is a directly editable driving dimension.
- A directly referenced literal `Static` is edited at its declaration. The sidebar
  names that shared parameter, so other consumers changing is explicit.
- An expression is read-only and dashed on the canvas. **Edit source** closes the
  draft and shows it in the source editor; edit its driving inputs in Parameters
  or Source. Dragging never replaces a formula or typed tolerance with a literal.

Every edit is one source transaction checked by the compiler. An invalid edit is
refused without changing source; **Build and use part** runs the normal
engineering build before the document is replaced. Lengths display in
millimetres and rotations in degrees. Slot **overall length** includes both
semicircular ends.

## Mounting openings that follow their dimensions

For a Profile whose explicit outer loop traces an unrotated Model-level Rect2,
**Add circular opening** (in the IntelliDraft sidebar) offers its center, corners and edge midpoints.
Choose the rectangle, anchor, inward X/Y insets and opening diameter, then
**Add opening**. Inapplicable insets are disabled. For a four-hole plate, add one
opening at each corner with the same insets.

The operation shares the rectangle's driving values through named `Static`
parameters. Literals/expressions are promoted when necessary; existing named
inputs are reused. For example, the resulting relationship can read:

```firmament
Static OutlineCenterX: Length = 0mm
Static OutlineCenterY: Length = 0mm
Static OutlineWidth: Length = 80mm
Static OutlineHeight: Length = 50mm
Rect2 Outline {
  center: [OutlineCenterX, OutlineCenterY]
  size: [OutlineWidth, OutlineHeight]
}
Circle2 MountOpening {
  center: [OutlineCenterX + (OutlineWidth / 2 - 8mm),
           OutlineCenterY + (OutlineHeight / 2 - 8mm)]
  diameter: 4mm
}
```

This is dimensional dependence through existing compile-time values. It does
not introduce an `Outline.Right.Offset(...)` expression or store sampled edge
coordinates. The opening becomes an explicitly named inner Profile loop. It is
a profile opening, rather than a drilled Hole feature with drill-point or
counterbore semantics. The compiler rejects overlapping/touching circular
openings and openings outside the rectangle. Complex inner-loop clearance and
other reference families are not offered yet.

## Planes

Local 2D Concept layouts admit these right-handed principal frames when consumed
by `Profile ... using Layout`:

| Layout | Local +X | Local +Y | Extrusion +normal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `on XY` | world +X | world +Y | world +Z |
| `on XZ` | world +X | world +Z | world -Y |
| `on YZ` | world +Y | world +Z | world +X |

Omitting `on` retains XY. Arbitrary origins/orientations use a traced
Construction Plane. A principal-plane layout is a frame for local 2D guides and
scalar data; it does not implicitly rotate typed 3D semantic members or override
the admission rules of Sheet Metal, Assembly mates or other consumers.

Extrude uses that resolved frame. Compose inherits its Base Profile frame and
requires all authored Base/Add/Remove Profiles to share it. Legacy explicit
Placement can transport unplaced XY Profiles; it cannot override a different
oriented Profile. Oriented Compose with Boss/Pocket/Hole/Slot/EdgeFinish is
explicitly rejected while those support adapters still assume world XY.

## Current boundary

IntelliDraft edits authored Rect2, Circle2, Ellipse2, Slot2, RoundedRect2 and SmoothRoundedRect2 fields
and displays the resolved line/arc/ellipse/cubic curves of other Profiles.
Generated Template/Feature bodies do not become writable source through their
expanded geometry. Profiles must have an unambiguous authored name in the
document; edits do not reach into included files.

IntelliDraft currently authors one unambiguous Model, retained closed shapes,
named Point2/Line2/Circle2 guides, Axis2 references, line/arc Paths, one outer
trace and a positive extrusion. Strokes snap to named points, not to arbitrary
intersections. The optional Advanced related-rectangle preset shares a top-right corner with
an unrotated rectangle in the same Concept Struct. Its wall/inset values and the
rectangle dimensions remain compile-time source expressions. Trace selection
uses named landmarks on the compiler's bounded guides; it does not invent
arbitrary intersection points. Soft alignment currently uses shape bounds in
the same layout. General intersection/point snaps, arbitrary one-way geometric references, boundary-edit tools, arbitrary
trim/extend and simultaneous constraint solving are not implemented. Existing code-authored geometry
continues to use its normal compiler owners.

docs/public/firmament/source-owned-guita.title: Source-owned guitar authoring
docs/public/firmament/source-owned-guita.markdown:
# Source-owned guitar authoring

The remaining guitar recipes now live in reviewed Firmament files. Python is a
read-only CLI reproduction harness; Blender remains a downstream presentation
step. Neither authors or replaces the guitar BRep.

The guitar now demonstrates the [mixed-case naming convention](language-style.md):
artifact/type vocabulary remains prominent, built-in properties and scope words
read quietly, and private pickup locals and fret functions use camelCase. A safe
formatter pass followed by a bounded manual pass retained published ports,
occurrence paths, template specialization identities and exact export bytes.
Older snippets below remain accepted compatibility spellings.

## Profiles and finite sections

Generic Templates may output `Profile`. Local Point2/Curve2 guides are namespaced
per specialization; Loop span names remain stable for section correspondence.
Profiles are output values here, not higher-order Template arguments.

```firmament
Include "neck-profile.firmament";
Record NeckStation { Y: Length; Depth: Length }
Static Stations: Set<NeckStation> {
 Shaft => NeckStation { Y: 440mm; Depth: 10.1mm }
 Nut => NeckStation { Y: 660mm; Depth: 7mm }
}
SectionChain Neck {
 Pattern Sections Over Stations {
  s => Section Station {
   Frame: Plane { Origin: [0mm,s.Y,55mm]; Normal: [0,1,0]; Up: [0,0,1] }
   Profile: NeckBack<HalfWidth: 21mm, WidthHandle: 11.6mm,
     Depth: s.Depth, DepthHandle: 4mm, SeatHandle: 14mm>
   Seam: Edge0
  }
 }
 // Supply transition and termination intent as in the actual Neck fixture.
}
```

The actual guitar keeps its approved straight shaft taper, adds two isolation
stations before the nut, and uses two more sections for the headstock transition.
`Sections_Nut` is the generated section identity; inspection retains its `Nut`
source key. Inline frame/profile values lower to existing Concept planes and
ordinary Profiles before the SectionChain binder runs.

`Point2` profile controls accept finite, dimension-checked scalar arithmetic after
Template substitution, such as `Position: [-Width / 2, -Depth * 0.55228475]`.
This reuses the existing bounded scalar evaluator. Wrong units, division by zero
and unresolved values produce `profile-layout-point-invalid`; no host source is
executed. The neck's original cubic D-profile is split exactly at its midpoints
so six spans can correspond to the rectangular headstock root. This changes the
span layout without approximating the original cross-section.

The short scarf beneath the veneer is an ordinary exact extrusion seated on the
headstock's published Base frame. The neck, scarf, slab and veneer remain separate
witness solids; their construction is not a certified fused manufacturing joint.
The tuner stem lives inside `GuitarTuner`, so the two three-instance patterns also
reuse it. The tailpiece's exact semicircular rail publishes `StringCrown`; the
bridge forwards that frame as `TailStringPlane`, and string bindings use zero
height offset there.

Body boundary replacements may request `Derivatives: Periodic`. A centered cyclic
Hermite derivative is derived from the ordered replacement knots on straight seed
carriers, with a 1,024-knot limit. Exact closure, cusp and self-intersection checks
still apply. Partial ranges and non-straight seed carriers are rejected. This is a
bounded interpolation recipe, not a general equation-curve or fairness solver.

## Physical material and finish

```firmament
Appearance BareSteel { Color: [0.55,0.57,0.60]; Metallic: 1; Roughness: 0.2; }
Appearance PaintedRed { Color: [0.45,0.02,0.01]; Metallic: 0; Roughness: 0.25; }
Material Steel { Identity: "steel"; Appearance: BareSteel; }

// Inside an ordinary Part occurrence:
Material: Steel;
// Or, for a finish that retains the same physical identity.
Material: Steel with { Appearance: PaintedRed; };
```

Color channels, Metallic and Roughness must be finite and within 0..1. The `with`
override selects only appearance. Material identities are nominal physical
designations, not certified engineering properties; existing material/FEA
qualification remains separate. A decorative pickup compound is explicitly a
presentation placeholder.

Precedence is occurrence `with` override, then physical material default. Authored
occurrence bindings are stronger than legacy exporter definition-material JSON.
Unassigned legacy occurrences retain that compatibility path. USD carries both
physical material and appearance identities as custom properties; Cycles consumes
these identities rather than occurrence-name or specialization-string matches.
Sunburst, lacquer, pearl and pickup feature shading are downstream shader choices.
They do not alter the exported geometry. Look-only edits preserve exact definition
buffers and reuse successful materializations, including length-changing look edits.

## Placed public route endpoints

```firmament
// Lead is a Struct Template with A/B/C: Point3 inputs and one WireRoute.
<Part Wire = Lead<>>
 Placement { From: Origin; To: World; }
 Bind {
  A { At: Point3(0mm,0mm,0mm); On: Product.Start.Entry.Frame; }
  B { At: Point2(0mm,0mm); On: Product.Nut.Top.Frame; }
  C { At: Point3(0mm,0mm,0mm); On: Product.Tuner.StringEntry; }
 }
</Part>
```

Fixed assembly placement resolves first. Each public datum lifts a local Point2/3
to world space and converts it into the consuming route occurrence's coordinates
exactly once. Those resolved Point3 arguments become ordinary specialization/cache
inputs. Inspection reports the port, world point, local point and bound definition.
Changing a terminal placement rebuilds its affected route while unchanged terminal
definitions reuse their materializations.

The first lane requires a fully fixed assembly, ordinary route Templates without
published outputs, and 1..16 named bindings. Dynamic joints, private ports and
route-dependent published frames fail explicitly. Reusable subassembly definitions
remain local prototypes; final occurrence route bindings are recorded separately.
The guitar's tailpiece string rail retains an explicit 5mm decorative stand-off
above its published top plane; this is not a claim of a modeled string hole.

## First locked guide

```firmament
Concept Struct HarnessLayout {
 Line3 Groove { From: Point3(0mm,0mm,0mm); To: Point3(100mm,0mm,0mm); }
}
WireRoute Signal {
 Diameter: 2mm; MinimumBendRadius: 10mm;
 Path {
  Start { At: Point3(0mm,-40mm,0mm); }
  Follow MainGroove { Curve: HarnessLayout.Groove;
    From: 20mm; Distance: 60mm; Direction: Forward; }
  End { At: Point3(120mm,0mm,0mm); }
 }
}
```

This lane follows a finite literal Concept Line3 interval, derives an entry fillet
at the requested minimum bend radius, and requires the end to extend along the
outgoing tangent. It lowers through the existing exact WireForm cylinder/torus
authority. Invalid intervals, insufficient approach room and non-tangent exits
fail. Reverse traversal is supported. Arbitrary/circular/spline guides, exact Via,
multiple corners and obstacle search remain separate qualification work.

## CLI and editor

`aetheris build <root.firmasm> --output artifacts/local/guitar.step` delegates to
the existing native assembly exporter. Root-aware `inspect` delegates to assembly,
SectionChain or ordinary part inspection. For an ordinary assembly:

```powershell
aetheris inspect fixtures/Canonical/AssemblyInterfaces/GuitarX0/guitar.firmasm --json --profile --repeat 2 --out artifacts/local/guitar/inspect.json
python scripts/create-guitar-x0.py --out artifacts/local/guitar
```

`--repeat` retains one explicit compilation session for 1..16 builds. JSON includes
per-build elapsed time, reuse/rebuild reasons and optional phase timings. It is not
a disk cache: placement, validation, tessellation and export still run each build.
The reproduction harness hashes its inputs and never rewrites fixtures.

Compiler-owned editor metadata covers route/Follow, keyed Sections, point recipes,
appearance/material and placement fields. Project-snapshot analysis and lexical
cross-file definition navigation support profile recipes and material aliases.
Single imported modules report that project context is needed instead of running
an unrelated part parser. Navigation does not grant private-port placement access.
Whole-project diagnostics currently retain aggregate locations; full generated-span
mapping, every draft grammar and editor-client integration are not claimed here.

## Deliberate remaining boundaries

The guitar already has physical planar seating evidence at its deck datum. No new
guitar case requires arbitrary tangent-frame evaluation, trim/seam attachment rules
or full curved-base footprint proofs. Those contracts, richer fit predicates, G2/
explicit surface laws, equation curves and higher-order geometry remain follow-ons.
The bounded source-authoring milestone does not add a general constraint solver.

docs/public/firmament/spans.md.title: Geometric spans
docs/public/firmament/spans.md.markdown:
# Geometric spans

`Span<T>` is a named, bounded, oriented view of existing parameterized geometry. It preserves its parent's semantic identity and does not copy geometry.

The curve lane admits `Span<Line>`, `Span<Arc>`, and `Span<Curve>`. It uses named endpoints, so the bounds remain attached to the parent guide rather than to newly authored helper geometry.

```firmament
Span<Line> MountingEdge {
    On: Stock.Bottom
    From: MountLeft
    To: MountRight
}
```

Use the resulting name wherever a normal pipeline guide is accepted. `Orientation: Reverse` reverses traversal; it does not change the bounded domain. Curve inspection reports the parent, endpoint domain, orientation, length, and provenance through `aetheris inspect-spans part.firmament --json`.

`Span<Plane>` represents a bounded semantic region on an existing planar support. It preserves the parent support identity and constrains where dependent features may apply. Its closed, non-self-intersecting boundary is an ordinary named Profile evaluated in parent-local 2D coordinates.

```firmament
Span<Plane> MountArea {
    On: MountPlane
    Boundary: MountBoundary
}

Hole<Counterbore> MountHole {
    On: MountArea
    Center: [16mm, 9mm]
    Diameter: 8mm
    CounterboreDiameter: 16mm
    CounterboreDepth: 3mm
    End: ThroughAll
}
```

`MountPlane` must be a named `Construction Plane`; a span never finds a nearby BRep face to replace a missing parent. `Hole`, `Boss`, and `Pocket` accept a planar Span on the current prismatic top support. Hole containment checks the complete shaft/counterbore disk, and Boss/Pocket containment checks the actual Profile footprint. Pattern expansion validates every generated feature independently.

Points on the boundary are boundary-valid. Containment uses the same `1e-7 mm` analytic line/arc tolerance as the Profile arrangement engine. Inner Profile loops are excluded and contribute negatively to inspected area. Invalid or missing parents and boundaries fail; consumers never fall back to the whole plane.

A `Span<Plane>` is not automatically a BRep Face. It may describe a region inside one Face, and STEP export continues through the parent body's existing topology without splitting that face merely to carry a name. `inspect-spans --json` reports the boundary, area, inherited normal and frame, consumers, and validity. Feature inspection retains both the Span and its parent support.

The current FEA frontend requires an exact `BoundaryRegionCapability` backed by a continuum or BRep region, and current PMI records target admitted faces, holes, or recognized regions. Planar Span binding for those consumers is not yet qualified; neither silently expands a Span to its parent face.

The constraint-first ladder is:

```text
Concept<T>  what must be true
Span<T>     bounded subset where it is true
Feature     semantic transformation applied against those constraints
```

`Span<T>` is a built-in closed language type, not Template generic programming. Other types—including `Material`, `Body`, and `Feature`—are rejected during binding. A Span is contiguous; use separate named spans for separate intervals.

docs/public/firmament/step-import.md.title: STEP import and inlineSTEP
docs/public/firmament/step-import.md.markdown:
# STEP import and inlineSTEP

Use [surface and trim inspection](surface-inspection.md) in Cadmata or Helios to compare filled geometry, BRep wire, translucent overlays and isolated source faces without changing the camera.

Direct STEP inspection is available through the native CLI/Cadmata workflows.
For mixed Part/Assembly products, prefer typed `include` or an
[Inventory Record](inventory.md). `Step("vendor/drive")` can supply an explicit
Assembly with its existing hierarchy and transforms. `InlineStep` is the local
annotation/surgery binding for one body; it can use `from: Components.housing`
or a direct path. An optional generated dependency lock supplies its source pin,
so authors do not need to write SHA-256 strings. See the Inventory guide for lock
commands, metadata and assembly imports' explicit source-PMI exclusion policy.

Helios also provides **Import STEP** for the bounded canonical `InlineStep` part
workflow described below. It retains the input as an immutable text asset and
creates a Firmament annotation layer. This is not arbitrary vendor STEP or
assembly import: the existing canonical-input and importer checks still apply.

In Helios, select an imported planar face to **Add datum**, or a cylindrical face
to **Add diameter**. Diameter authoring shows the measured value separately from
the requirement and requires explicit upper/lower allowances in millimetres.
Compilation checks the actual surface type and exports real AP242 geometric face
associations. Recognition labels are optional; direct `part.face("#191")` targets
use importer provenance, not STEP line order. Annotation changes do not edit the
imported geometry.

**Save workspace** downloads a `.helios.zip` containing the original STEP text
and Firmament source; **Open file** reopens it. Local checkpoints retain both too.
Cloud single-document saves cannot store these workspaces and refuse rather than
omit the asset. An unchanged `InlineStep` can retain an existing semantic PMI
layer, normalize its length measures to millimetres, and add explicit controls.
Foreign graphical glyphs are excluded with a warning; advanced semantic forms
can be retained in STEP without promising their 3D label projection. See
[PMI transfer and explicit GD&T](pmi.md#imported-semantic-pmi-and-units) for
admission limits. Reopen a saved workspace to preserve its editable source layer.

The browser SDK accepts `.step`/`.stp` text assets in `projectDocuments`:

```js
const source = 'Model Imported { units: mm InlineStep part { path: "body.step" } }';
const result = await cad.compile(source, {
  sourceName: 'part.firmament',
  projectDocuments: { 'body.step': stepText },
});
```

Paths resolve relative to the source document inside the explicit snapshot;
missing assets never fall through to native disk. The admitted source text,
SHA-256 and topology map remain bound to that compilation. Imported face picks
report `ImportedStable`, the source selector, surface kind and measured cylinder
diameter; these do not imply a native editable feature history.

GLB part export projects supported datum/diameter PMI into separate font-outline
and leader line primitives, surface witnesses and structured `asset.extras.pmi` records
(`aetheris/pmi-display/1`, millimetres). Body vertex/index buffers are preserved.
Datum leaders terminate inside the selected plane on a small gold patch. Diameter
leaders terminate on the analytic cylindrical wall, whose trimmed surface and
physical rims are highlighted in gold; parameter seams are not highlighted as rims.
A short surface-normal stem and arrow identify each attachment. The default body
appearance is lightly translucent during PMI inspection/export; explicit authored
appearances are retained. All markers are presentation only and do not intercept
engineering picks. `target` metadata records the witness geometry, normal and a
tiny `surfaceOffset` used only to prevent coincident-surface rendering artifacts.
The leader anchor stays on the exact support; engineering geometry is not offset.
Callout text uses static XY-plane outlines; the viewport legend remains readable when
the geometry text is edge-on. These are presentation assets, not AP242 semantics
or manufacturing approval.
Unsupported callout kinds/associations fail annotated GLB export explicitly;
an unavailable viewport callout is reported as a warning while STEP remains
authoritative. USDA, STL and OBJ do not carry this annotation layer.

Use `aetheris analyze part.step --json` to inspect STEP topology, analytic surface families, bounds, manifold assessment, and semantic PMI. When a part is easiest to understand by its manufacturing section, inspect it first with `aetheris analyze section part.step --xy|--xz|--yz --offset value --json`; use `--origin x,y,z --normal x,y,z` for an arbitrary construction plane and `--out section.svg` for deterministic visual evidence. This section-first path preserves analytic line/arc trims and reports closed-loop nesting instead of asking a tessellated view to carry design intent. Use `aetheris sheetmetal recognize` for bounded Sheet Metal recognition rather than treating generic topology analysis as manufacturing intent.

`analyze --json` also reports `splineRecovery`: counts of analytic, exact spline, recovered spline, and unsupported edge/face geometry; the worst measured recovery deviation; and the requested engineering tolerance. The default `ImportPolicy.RecoveryToleranceMillimetres` is 0.1 mm after STEP unit normalization. Rational curves and surfaces are recognized as analytic geometry where qualified; otherwise the importer attempts bounded generic spline recovery and records provenance on recovered geometry. The maximum deviation is sampled evidence.

For bound geometry, `pcurveQualification` reports the face-edge use count, source and reconstructed pcurves, failed uses, worst sampled 3D lift deviation, and surface-family counts. `qualified` means every coedge is bound and the independent pcurve validator accepts edge/surface agreement, endpoint sense, and loop closure. `inspectable-unqualified` means the body can still be inspected, but its recovered pcurves do not form a complete qualified trim set; STEP export then omits that partial set while retaining valid source pcurves. `ImportPolicy.PcurveQualificationToleranceMillimetres` defaults to 0.001 mm. A recovered curve or support can use a larger local allowance based on its measured geometry-recovery deviations, capped by the separate 0.1 mm geometry recovery budget. The CLI reports the observed lift deviation separately from geometry recovery deviation.

`summary.importQualification` distinguishes `Qualified`, `Inspectable`, `Degraded`, and `Failed` from authoritative BRep evidence. Parser/API success means geometry was retained; it is not a qualification verdict. `status` and `geometryStatus` report engineering qualification independently of the viewport. `displayStatus` separately reports `NotAssessed`, `Complete`, `RefinementLimited`, or `Partial`, with display reasons and missing face identities. Missing trim bindings remain `Inspectable`; detected invalid trims or incomplete intended solid shells are `Degraded` even when a useful preview is complete. Exact faces can receive derived face-local pcurves without being classified as recovered geometry.

An unchanged `InlineStep` can be annotated and re-exported when strict production
output checks pass, even when optional UV recovery is incomplete. Source pins
prove the identity of the imported data; they do not select a stricter operation.
Export checks topology/bindings, imported shell enclosure, canonical representation
and 3D boundary consistency within the declared budget, capped at 0.1 mm. This is
a recovery allowance, not a machining tolerance. Invalid UV traces are omitted
with `step-export-recovered-pcurves-omitted`; STEP uses its 3D edge curves and
vertices to define those boundaries. The source qualification report is retained.
`Remove`/`Replace` operations that depend on face-local trims keep their own
qualified-trim requirements. Tessellated-only source cannot enter this exact
part path through an automatic approximation fallback.

`aetheris canon` applies the same strict geometry boundary in both metadata modes:
`deterministic` selects deterministic headers; `production` preserves source
metadata. Both retain supported semantic PMI and report exclusions or omitted UV
traces in JSON `diagnostics` and text warnings. Neither mode promotes an open
surface into a solid. Open inputs remain available to `analyze` and inspection.
The [closed ellipse extrusion](../../../fixtures/Canonical/Boundary2/closed-ellipse-extrusion.firmament)
is a complete source witness with analytic elliptical boundaries and planar caps.

Legacy AP203/AP214 import uses the same topology and geometry path. Viewport quality is chosen automatically from model scale and bounded adaptive sampling. Viewport triangles are disposable approximations: STEP export, topology selection, and engineering qualification consume BRep directly. A convincing preview cannot qualify invalid engineering geometry. The frozen 26-file McMaster corpus and the original closeout evidence are recorded in [STEP-LEGACY-CLOSEOUT-X2](../../development/reports/2026-10/STEP-LEGACY-CLOSEOUT-X2.md); the subsequent visual investigation and ball roundtrip repair are in [STEP-LEGACY-FINAL-X3](../../development/reports/2026-10/STEP-LEGACY-FINAL-X3.md). Vendor files and generated meshes stay local; the tracked manifest retains the X0 baseline metadata and outcomes.

In Cadmata, expand **Surface / trim inspection** in the viewport. Compare **Surfaces only**, **BRep wire only**, **Translucent + BRep wire**, and **Face colors + BRep wire** without changing the camera. Red lines carry kernel edge identities; the wire and translucent views show them through surfaces. Select a patch from the list, or click a surface in an inspection view, to isolate its occurrence and face with the source STEP entity, support family, and boundary edges. STEP imports currently display BRep meshes, with no SDF field. These diagnostic controls change presentation only.

Dense rectangular spline trims retain native parameter grid cells as the existing `QuadCell` IR before final triangle lowering. Physical span lengths balance the grid rather than assuming equal U/V units mean equal lengths. Nearly coincident grid lines are merged only within a small sampled fraction of the display budget. Each retained quad is split along a deterministic valid diagonal. Axis and triangle caps can limit cell proportions; this path is bounded to rectangular trims and does not turn arbitrary trim bounding boxes into filled surfaces.

Dense nonrectangular spline trims reuse that knot-aware grid to decompose the actual outer-minus-holes region into local polygons. Existing constrained ear clipping triangulates each region before bounded chord/normal refinement. Only convex intersections of already validated seed triangles may use an anchor fan; general polygons never use an averaged centre. Periodic charts are normalized upstream, and display subdivision retains the original face and occurrence identity for picking. Quality limits remain explicit in display diagnostics. See [STEP-TRIM-TRIANGULATION-X4](../../development/reports/2026-10/STEP-TRIM-TRIANGULATION-X4.md) for the corpus and product evidence.

Rational source supports may be evaluated and displayed. Production AP242 uses
analytic or non-rational geometry after bounded recovery and independent boundary
validation. Native ellipsoid octants are the explicit exception: their exact STEP
projection uses rational quadratic patches. Arbitrary rational NURBS fallback is
not admitted, including through auxiliary PMI geometry. Intentional polynomial
B-spline curves and surfaces remain supported. Ordinary imported parts can use an
explicit recovery allowance of at most 0.1 mm; tighter source and application
requirements still matter for small features. Recovery reports sampled deviation
rather than claiming an exact mathematical error bound. Unsupported normalization
fails explicitly. Display mesh quality never supplies export evidence.

Firmament `inlineSTEP` consumes Aetheris-canonical AP242 on the bounded production path. Imported faces are selected by source entity identity, for example `body.face(#170)`, and recognized regions may supply stable semantic aliases. [`inline-step-cantilever.firmament`](../../../fixtures/Canonical/FEA/inline-step-cantilever.firmament) demonstrates FEA on a checked-in canonical STEP resource.

The single-body importer does not promise arbitrary containment, multi-root assemblies, or every AP242 surface family as one native body. `aetheris analyze compound part.step --json` is the exact inspection path for disconnected rigid roots: it reports each root independently and never silently selects or merges one. Multiple geometric roots alone do **not** establish product structure, occurrence transforms, mates, or interfaces. Use assembly import when the STEP product graph carries that semantics, and use Firmament assembly authoring when the intended component relationships must be stated explicitly. Unsupported containment in FEA reports `firmament-analysis-inline-step-containment-unsupported`; missing files and unresolved face identities are fatal diagnostics.

docs/public/firmament/surface-inspection.markdown:
# Surface and trim inspection

Choose a practical [viewport theme](viewport-themes.md) for inspection, or a presentation theme for sharing the same model.

Cadmata and Helios expose **Surface / trim inspection** in the WebGPU viewport. It compares the displayed geometry with source BRep curves using the same camera, occurrence transforms and renderer. Orbit, pan and zoom work throughout inspection.

Choose **Surfaces only** to see the filled mesh or field, **BRep wire only** to see source curves, **Translucent + wire** to expose curves through the surface, or **Face colours + wire** to distinguish adjacent source faces. Red lines are BRep edges, including trim boundaries where transported; they are not triangle edges. These views help distinguish filled holes, excess surface coverage, long facets and mismatched boundaries.

Choose a face in **Isolated display face**, or click a surface while an inspection view is active. Isolation uses occurrence plus source face identity, so repeated parts remain distinguishable. Choose **All faces** to restore the complete model. Cadmata additionally shows the source STEP entity, support family and face boundary edges when available. Changing the view or isolated face preserves the camera; loading a new model resets isolation.

Helios SDK packets currently carry source face ranges and occurrence edges without face-edge adjacency. Its isolated wire therefore shows all edges of that occurrence, and the control states this limitation. Cadmata's richer imported-face packet can restrict wire to the isolated face's boundary edges.

Whole-model surface and translucent views retain the actual CIR/SDF field when active. A field shader has no per-face trim mask. Face colours and face isolation explicitly show its retained BRep mesh proxy, with a notice in Helios. Proxy pixels must not be mistaken for proof of the field's silhouette. Compare the whole field with the proxy to investigate a discrepancy.

Recovered trims must reconstruct their shared 3D edge within the qualification
tolerance. Polynomial Bezier patch boundaries can be checked with a conservative
control-net and parameter-error bound over the whole trim. In the BRep API this
reports `BezierBoundaryControlHull`: the maximum lift deviation is an upper
bound, and zero lift samples means the bound replaced sampling. It does not mean
the trim was unchecked. The recovered coordinates and tolerance are unchanged;
rational, multi-span and other unqualified representations retain sampled checks.

The reusable API is exported by `@aetheris/three-telos`:

```ts
import { inspectSurfaces, surfaceInspectionFaces } from "@aetheris/three-telos";

const faces = surfaceInspectionFaces(sourceScene);
host.setScene(inspectSurfaces(sourceScene, "overlay", faces[0]));
// Use the same host/camera for the next comparison; do not call fit here.
host.setScene(inspectSurfaces(sourceScene, "wire", faces[0]));
host.setScene(inspectSurfaces(sourceScene, "normal"));
```

Projection keeps engineering authority in the source scene. Packed faces share the complete immutable geometry and GPU buffers; triangle draw ranges preserve original triangle indices for source selection. It never reconstructs BRep edges from tessellation or changes export geometry. Products own controls, source metadata and screenshots; Three Telos owns drawing, camera and picking.

For reproducible corpus review, `scripts/inspect-step-legacy-cadmata.mts` captures five matched-camera views, face inventories and optional orbit/zoom/source-face click witnesses through real STEP upload. Outputs belong under ignored `artifacts/local/`. The canvas `data-surface-inspection` and `data-surface-inspection-pick` attributes expose the active projection and actual hit for automation. Contact sheets are review evidence, not engineering qualification or human signoff.

docs/public/firmament/syntax.md.markdown:
# Firmament syntax

The material that used to live on this page is now split up:

- **New to Firmament?** Work through the [lessons](../learn/README.md). Six short
  lessons, each with a complete example that the test suite builds.
- **Looking something up?** Use the [language reference](../reference/language/README.md).

## The language in one screen

```firmament
Model Plate {
  units: mm
  Profile outline = Rect2 { center: [0mm, 0mm]; size: [80mm, 50mm] }
  Extrude stock { profile: outline; from: 0mm; to: 8mm }
  Modify stock {
    Hole<Shaft> mount { on: +Z; center: [0mm, 0mm]; diameter: 8mm; end: ThroughAll }
  }
}
```

- A `Model` is one part with one material body.
- Constructs and types are PascalCase (`Profile`, `Rect2`, `Hole<Shaft>`); fields,
  your names and linking words are camelCase or lowercase.
- Every length carries its unit.
- Construction geometry (a `Rect2`, a layout) is not material until something
  such as `Extrude` consumes it.
- Anything the compiler cannot build exactly as written is rejected with a
  diagnostic. Nothing is silently skipped.
