docs/public/reference/cli.md.markdown:
# CLI reference

Primary public commands:

Commands use `aetheris` unless a separate executable is shown. The optional `aetheris-3dm` tool includes native Rhino3dm; [installation and source usage](3dm-recovery.md).

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `validate <file> [--json]` | Check admission; generic mechanical validation includes in-memory geometry preflight |
| `frontend-shadow <file> [--json] [--ast] [--validate] [--benchmark]` | Developer-only original-source structural evidence and bounded production comparison |
| `build <file> [--output path] [--json]` | Materialize and export exact STEP AP242 |
| `inspect <firmament-or-step> [--json]` | Inspect source semantics or route STEP to analysis |
| `aetheris-3dm inspect <file.3dm> [--json]` | Inventory Rhino/OpenNURBS metadata, units, BRep topology, and unsupported objects |
| `aetheris-3dm recover <file.3dm> [--body N [--edge N\|--face N]] [--json]` | Measure provisional analytic/non-rational recovery candidates; see [3DM recovery evidence](3dm-recovery.md) |
| `analyze <step> [--json]` | Reinspect topology, surfaces, bounds, manifold state, and PMI |
| `analyze section <step> ((--xy\|--xz\|--yz) --offset value\|--origin x,y,z --normal x,y,z) [--out section.svg] [--json]` | Extract trim-aware analytic section loops in a principal or arbitrary plane and optionally render deterministic SVG evidence |
| `analyze compound <step> [--json]` | Inspect every disconnected rigid root without silently selecting or merging one |
| `view <file>` | Open in bundled Cadmata |
| `fea <file> --out-dir dir [--json]` | Compile and solve the bounded linear-elastic analysis |
| `sheetmetal ...` | Inspect, recognize, recover, compare, or flatten Sheet Metal |
| `sculpture build <source> ...` | Build the bounded non-manufacturing Sol 1 AP242 artwork, evidence, and SVG preview |
| `section-chain <build\|inspect\|validate> <file.firmament\|flagship\|twist\|two-profile> ...` | Lower authored SectionChain, `Loft`, or `Loft<Hollow>` into SectionChain IR and report frames, spans, correspondence, pcurves, conservative intersection qualification, STEP, and reimport evidence |
| `wireframe <model.step> [--out preview.svg] [--view iso\|front\|top\|right] [--density N] [--json]` | Render deterministic exact-edge and trim-clipped surface-isoline SVG evidence |
| `asm ...` | Inspect/execute/import/export assemblies |

Generic mechanical `validate` now runs the existing engineering compilation in memory, including selection binding, capability checks and geometry/STEP preflight. It writes no output file. Its report includes `validationLevel` (`Built`, `BuildRejected`, or `ParsedNotBuilt`) and developer-only `parserRoute` metadata. `--explain` prints the route, admission level and available instance counts. `--parse-only` explicitly requests static analysis and reports `parsed-not-built` on success. Drawing, Analysis, PlasticShell, Sculpting, Plateau and Piping currently lack that separate static admission path: they reject this option with `firmament-validation-option-unsupported` and `NotValidated`, rather than silently materializing geometry. Structural and Garment reuse their existing static analyzers. External `--forge-pack` validation is also labelled `parsed-not-built`: those descriptor providers are not installed into normal build. Domain-specific validators retain their separate scope; inspect their reports. This is not a promise that unchanged source can never encounter a later environment or kernel failure.

Mechanical Model and material-bearing Struct documents now use the unified lexer/AST admission path (`UnifiedMechanical`). The ignored Compose Fillet, erased Rect2 field and unused Slot2 route-perturbation cases are repaired. Profile/Compose build execution consumes admitted engineering inputs. Other dedicated domains retain their existing owners; see the [production migration qualification](../../development/reports/2026-10/FIRMAMENT-MECHANICAL-FRONTEND-MIGRATION.md) for its scope and evidence.

`validate file.firmament --shadow --explain --json` opts into the developer
envelope: `shadow` contains original-source syntax status, AST summary, original
diagnostics and a bounded comparison against the generic production projection;
`productionValidation` contains the ordinary validation command's unchanged
report. `Parsed` means `StructuralOnlyUnbound`, not engineering validity. The
comparison explicitly reports unqualified declarations and fields. `--ast` adds
the detailed source tree and trivia only when requested. `frontend-shadow`
without `--validate` collects syntax/projection evidence without geometry.

`frontend-shadow --corpus fixtures` writes JSON and Markdown under ignored
`artifacts/local/frontend-x1/corpus` by default. It includes invalid, legacy and
speculative sources; exit zero means collection completed, while `qualified:
false` remains explicit. Per-file exit one means structural rejection or, with
`--validate`, production rejection. Normal mechanical compilation uses the same syntax parser through its production
AST binder; the developer comparison does not control admission. `--benchmark` measures twenty warm structural parses and current
thread allocations, excluding file IO, production parsing, comparison and geometry.

Run `aetheris <command> --help` for exact options. JSON is a public automation surface, but its root is command-specific: process exit status is authoritative, `validate` reports `firmamentV2Validation.status`, and materializing/analysis commands report `success` where documented. Diagnostics are structured; artifact paths are explicit; wireframe reports trim/pcurve coverage and a deterministic SVG hash; Sheet Metal reports regions, bends, and lowered features separately; FEA reports requested/result artifacts; sculpting builds report every `BodyState`, `GeometricDelta`, validation evidence, surface-family inventory, and the sibling `.delta.json` path; other builds report emitted features and PMI export evidence. Counts describe semantic items at the stated layer, not arbitrary STEP entity counts.

Generic STEP analysis reports analytic placement and size information where it is present: planes include origin and normal; bounded cylinders and cones include axis, axial extent, and circular-boundary angular extent; spheres include center and radius; and circles include center, axis, radius, sweep, orientation, and their actual trimmed endpoints. Circular-edge bounds and section output are computed from those trims rather than from the supporting full circle. `analyze section` returns normalized closed loops with deterministic orientation and nesting metadata; `--out` is intended as compact geometry evidence, not a substitute for the JSON record.

## Part mesh exports

```sh
aetheris mesh part.step --format stl --output artifacts/local/part.stl --json
```

STL export checks paired opposite-direction edge uses, connectedness, nondegenerate
triangles and positive signed volume. It repeats those checks after converting to
STL's float32 coordinates and merging equal stored positions. Precision collapse
rejects before replacing the destination file. Build nearer the coordinate origin
or use a representation retaining greater coordinate precision if float32 cannot
preserve the part's detail.

JSON includes `orientationConflictEdgeCount`, `consistentlyOriented`,
`outwardOriented` and `meshSignedVolumeMm3`. The volume describes the stored
triangle approximation, not the exact engineering part. `maxChordalDeviation`
describes shared boundary sampling; it is not a bound on volume error. `watertight` reports the
mesh checks above; it does not prove freedom from self-intersection or fidelity
to a nominal design. OBJ reports the same directed-edge diagnostics while
retaining the structured polygon representation.

## Assembly display meshes

For a standalone BRep part, use
`aetheris mesh part.firmament --format display-json --output artifacts/local/part.display.json --step-output artifacts/local/part.step --json`.
This exports the shared display schema in millimetres with one definition and
one identity-frame occurrence. The optional `--step-output` writes the exact
body from the same compilation. Compilation and tessellation finish before
either output is written; filesystem write errors may still leave one output.
This is the transport used by [Aetheris CAD for Blender](../blender.md).

`aetheris mesh <assembly.firmament|assembly.firmasm> --format assembly-json --output <file.mesh.json> --json` exports shared local definition meshes and stable world-space occurrences. Failed geometry is not omitted. The default destination is `artifacts/local/mesh/<name>.mesh.json`. See [editable mechanisms](../firmament/editable-mechanisms.md) for the schema and a working consumer.

## Generate engineering drawings

`aetheris drawing generate <part.firmament|model.step> --out-dir <directory> --json` creates PDF, SVG, editable PPTX, Drawing IR and validation evidence. The default automatic path requires a complete nominal dimension plan; currently rectangular plates/boxes with disjoint Z-through holes are qualified. `--linear-tolerance`, `--angular-tolerance` and `--material` are explicit drawing requirements. `--reference-only` emits clearly incomplete visualization. See [drawing generation](../drawings.md) for admission, reconstruction qualification and manufacturing limits. Use `drawing compile` for authored drawings and assembly BOMs.

docs/public/reference/diagnostics.md.title: Diagnostics and failure recovery
docs/public/reference/diagnostics.md.markdown:
# Diagnostics and failure recovery

Drawing generation reports `drawing-definition-incomplete` when no qualified plan
accounts for the complete nominal body. `--reference-only` requests explicitly
incomplete review views. `drawing-pmi-geometry-mismatch` identifies conflicting
diameter/depth/quantity requirements; `drawing-tolerance-envelope-invalid` and
`drawing-tolerance-zero-width` reject contradictory dimensional limits. Missing
material, linear or angular requirements are recorded independently in definition
evidence and visibly marked on the PDF. Process capability is not inferred from a
successful export. See [drawing generation](../drawings.md).

Generic V2 build/validation errors use structured objects with `code`, `severity`, `message`, `sourceFile`, optional `sourceSpan`, `line`, `column`, and `locationNote`. The existing `fatal` spelling means an error that prevents admission; `warning` remains nonfatal. Parser route metadata is for debugging. An enclosing-declaration span is explicitly labelled when the legacy producer supplied no precise original-source provenance. Monaco consumes the same compiler presentation. Specialized domain commands are not yet all migrated to this representation.

Unknown canonical statements and Box fields are errors. Local 2D Concept layouts admit XY, XZ and YZ for Profile consumers. `profile-layout-placement-unsupported` rejects other layout selectors instead of substituting XY; `profile-layout-spatial-members-unsupported` identifies a non-XY layout mixing local guides with spatial semantic members. Use a traced Construction Plane for arbitrary supported orientations. `SemanticSourceNotFound` preserves the missing source and the provenance explanation. An accidental through-depth Pocket fails; explicit `end: ThroughAll` selects the admitted through cut. Box top-boundary Fillet with disjoint ThroughAll shaft/counterbore holes is supported; `CombinedFeatureInteractionUnsupported` identifies a hole touching the finish band or another hole. Unsupported combined selectors retain `CombinedFeatureSelectionLost` at the EdgeFinish declaration.

## Exact face grafts and subdivision meshes

- `surf-face-pmi-projection-unsupported` / `surf-face-associated-target-unsupported`:
  this edit cannot retain the required PMI/interface meaning. The predecessor
  remains authoritative; no metadata is silently dropped.
- `surf-face-boundary-mismatch` / `surf-face-graph-unsupported`: retain the named
  four-line boundary and affine parameter grid, or use explicit mesh sculpting
  for the broader deformation. `FaceN` handles become stale after replacement.
- `mesh-conversion-deviation-exceeded`: increase sphere cage segments or
  explicitly authorize a larger finite conversion budget.
- `mesh-vertex-unresolved` / `mesh-edge-unresolved`: inspect the current cage;
  historical handles are not rebound by proximity.
- `mesh-preservation-failed` / `mesh-local-foldover`: the edit violates its
  protected vertex contract or reverses a predecessor face triangle.
- `mesh-subdivision-budget-exceeded`: refinement exceeds 24,576 faces.
- `sculpt-mesh-export-format-unsupported`: the selected MeshState produces STL
  or GLB, not STEP. Validation reports `MeshBuilt` and
  `stepExportAvailable: false`; select an exact state for STEP.
- `mesh-export-precision-exhausted`: 32-bit coordinates cannot retain a finite
  closed output mesh. No new artifact is emitted.
- `mesh-export-precision-budget-exceeded`: coordinate quantization exceeds the
  inherited `maximumDeviation` budget, even though topology may remain closed.

Global mesh self-intersection remains `NotCertified`, independent of successful
topology and local foldover checks.

## Profile rim finishes

- `ProfileBoundaryEdgeFinishSequenceUnsupported`: this Profile/Compose owner
  admits one finish operation. Multiple requested finishes cannot be compiled
  as a first-operation-only result. Uncalled recipes do not count as operations.
- `ProfileEdgeFinishInsetCollapse`: the requested circular-segment finish reaches
  or exceeds its inradius. Reduce the radius/distance to retain a cap.
- `ProfileBoundaryFilletInsetInvalid` / `ProfileBoundaryChamferInsetCollapse`:
  an inset polygon edge collapses or reverses; reduce the finish size.
- `ProfileEdgeFinishJunctionUnsupported`: a sharp curved junction lacks a
  qualified shared intersection for this profile family. This does not require
  ordinary CAD authors to supply a general surface blend.
- `ProfileEdgeFinishMixedShellFinishExceedsHostThickness`: the finish consumes
  the full thickness rather than leaving the admitted stock region.
- `ProfileBoundaryFilletEndClearanceRequiresOpenChain`: remove `endClearance`
  from a closed-loop finish, or select the intended open chain.
- `ProfileEdgeFinishMiterNumericToleranceExhausted` / `ProfileEdgeFinishMiterRefinementLimit`:
  the finite miter representation cannot meet its certified tolerance within the
  bounded numerical budget. No artifact is admitted.

When a planner reports one unambiguous EdgeFinish operation, the diagnostic uses
that enclosing declaration's span; expanded provenance is mapped where retained.

## Circular Sweep

- `firmament-sweep-section-invalid`: circular diameter is missing, non-finite, or non-positive.
- `firmament-sweep-path-disconnected`: a segment does not continue from its predecessor.
- `firmament-sweep-path-not-tangent`: adjacent segments meet at a sharp corner.
- `firmament-sweep-path-nonplanar`: the path is outside the supported planar XY boundary.
- `firmament-sweep-bend-radius-too-small`: an arc radius does not exceed the section radius.
- `firmament-sweep-self-intersection`: nonadjacent centerline regions violate required clearance.
- `firmament-sweep-material-unresolved`: the material identity is absent from the deployed catalog.

## Formed Wire

- `wireform-diameter-invalid`: stock diameter is missing, non-finite, or non-positive.
- `wireform-start-frame-invalid`: Origin/Tangent/Up is missing, the tangent is zero, or Up is parallel to the tangent.
- `wireform-straight-length-invalid:<operation>`: Straight length is not finite and positive.
- `wireform-bend-radius-invalid:<operation>`: centerline bend radius is not positive or does not exceed `Diameter / 2`. This local geometric check runs before body construction.
- `wireform-bend-angle-invalid:<operation>`: Bend angle is zero or exceeds ±180°.
- `wireform-bend-plane-invalid:<operation>`: Plane is not current local `Up` or `Right`.
- `wireform-material-unresolved`: the material identity is absent from the deployed catalog.
- `wireform-self-intersection:<opA>:<opB>`: nonadjacent wire portions violate diameter clearance. This later global check uses conservative 3D chord/sagitta bounds and rejects intentional contact.

The Standard Paperclip template has stricter product policy (`InnerBendRadius > WireDiameter`) than generic WireForm's geometric `Radius > Diameter / 2`; named Template `Require` clauses can therefore reject a Paperclip specialization before WireForm lowering.

## Surface trim closure

- `surf-intersection-none`: the qualified supports do not intersect inside the bounded domains.
- `surf-intersection-ambiguous`: multiple branches exist without an admissible seed/reference boundary.
- `surf-pcurve-invalid`: a face-local UV curve is missing, outside its domain, misoriented, or reconstructs away from the shared 3D edge.
- `surf-trim-loop-open`: ordered trim coedges do not close through shared topology vertices.
- `surf-inner-loop-invalid`: an opening loop is not a valid bounded hole in the replacement face.
- `surf-extension-unsupported`: the surface family, degree, stability envelope, or requested extension is outside the qualified matrix.
- `surf-imported-selector-unresolved`: a STEP `ADVANCED_FACE` identity does not resolve to exactly one current face.
- `surf-association-target-removed`: PMI or an Assembly Interface has no explicit `Preserved` correspondence; Aetheris refuses name- or proximity-based rebinding.
- `surf-association-current-geometry-missing`: an explicitly preserved association references a face absent from the output `BodyState`.
- `surf-blend-g2-unsatisfied`: a constructible blend candidate fails the hard transverse normal-curvature contract and is rejected before scoring.
- `surf-blend-candidate-rejected`: compact per-candidate evidence emitted when the complete request has no selectable candidate.
- `surf-blend-no-eligible-candidates`: representation, continuity, topology, locality, or preservation gates leave no candidate at the declared minimum continuity.
- `surf-blend-override-ineligible`: `UseCandidate` names an absent candidate or one that fails the active hard requirements.
- `surf-blend-locality-violation`: a candidate exceeds the authorized transition envelope and cannot enter utility judgment.
- `surf-boundary-g2-violation`: realized exact boundary second-difference evidence exceeds the planar-shoulder normal-curvature tolerance.
- `surf-certified-bounds-invalid`: a claimed exact polynomial bounds certificate does not contain deterministic surface samples.
- `surf-selector-target-replaced`: a historical native or imported selector has an explicit successor and cannot be reused.

## Construction-state replay and SectionChain sculpting

- `bodystate-operation-replay-failed`: replay stopped atomically at the named typed operation; the reported predecessor remains authoritative.
- `bodystate-operation-order-invalid`: an operation's authored predecessor does not equal the preceding operation's authored output; replay does not reorder or guess intent.
- `bodystate-operation-version-unsupported`: the retained operation payload version is not admitted.
- `bodystate-operation-support-missing`: a semantic support read by an operation is absent; Aetheris does not guess a nearest face.
- `bodystate-preserved-region-modified`: realized construction touched a protected semantic region.
- `section-chain-add-not-attached`: the additive terminal does not exactly correspond to its support, or no positive connected volume resulted.
- `section-chain-add-remote-intersection`: a non-terminal additive section crosses the predecessor outside the intended attachment.
- `section-chain-remove-no-material`: the admitted removal corridor does not remove positive bounded material.
- `section-chain-remove-disconnects-body`: a duct reaches the protected outer boundary and would sever the admitted housing result.
- `section-chain-housing-base-unsupported`: an upstream crown/patch changed the predecessor outside the currently qualified planar composition lane.

Start with `aetheris validate source.firmament --json`; use `build` when geometry, AP242, assertions, or artifacts are involved. A diagnostic code is the stable automation key, while its message identifies the value/target and expected category where useful.

Common recovery patterns:

| Failure | What to check |
|---|---|
| unknown keyword/Template | spelling, `Use` declaration, and qualified Template name |
| missing Template argument | the Template's typed parameter list or Forge `describe` output |
| unit mismatch | use the required dimension (`mm`, `deg`, `N`) rather than a bare/wrong-dimension value |
| `firmament-v2-polyhedron-face-count-unsupported` | `Polyhedron<N>` requires a compile-time regular convex face count: 4, 6, 8, 12 or 20; N is not the side count of a prism. |
| `firmament-v2-ellipsoid-radii-invalid` | Supply three finite positive X/Y/Z semiaxes with length units in `radii`. |
| `firmament-v2-uniform-stock-fillet-unsupported` | Use one `EdgeFinish<Fillet>` with `target: AllEdges`, positive `radius` and no face selector on untouched direct Box or regular Polyhedron stock. Arbitrary bodies, hollow stock, other edits and construction adapters are outside this capability. |
| `UniformFilletRadiusTooLarge` | Reduce the radius below the reported stock inradius; this construction requires positive remaining planar faces and edge spans. |
| `drawing-pmi-target-unlocated` | The PMI needs a geometric face association. Automatic generation refuses a model-center leader. |
| `drawing-pmi-value-unavailable` | Supply an admitted finite PMI nominal/depth; a missing measure is not interpreted as zero. |
| `drawing-layout-impossible` | Use fewer PMI entries per authored view or a larger allocation; labels, strokes and sheet keepouts must remain clear. |
| `drawing-title-block-overflow` / `drawing-notes-overflow` | Shorten presentation metadata/notes or use an additional authored sheet. Text was not truncated. |
| `drawing-signoff-incomplete` | Provide both a role name and its ISO date, or leave both blank; unperformed reviews must remain blank. |
| unknown material | one of the four exact catalog references in the materials guide |
| unresolved PMI target | named hole/face selector exists in the same semantic domain |
| invalid tolerance | `PlusMinus(plus, minus)` uses Length values for a diameter |
| Sheet Metal region mismatch | use a named planar region such as `Base`, not `face(+Z)` |
| `sheetmetal-hole-domain-syntax` | replace Model `Hole<Shaft>` with Sheet Metal `Hole Name` syntax |
| `sheetmetal-pmi-domain-syntax` | use `Manufacturing` plus `DatumFeature` targeting a named Sheet Metal region |
| inlineSTEP file/face failure | resolve the file relative to the source and use an existing AP242 face identity |
| empty FEA selection | selected face exists and intersects occupied cut cells at the requested lattice |
| unsupported constitutive model | Preview 3 production scope is linear elastic isotropic |

Successful builds enforce PMI/AP242 parity. `firmament-v2-pmi-export-evidence-mismatch` means a supported record failed independent export reinspection; no artifact is written. See [targets](targets.md) for cross-domain forms.

docs/public/reference/known-issues.md.markdown:
# Aetheris 2.0.0 known issues and limitations

- Bundles target Windows x64, Linux x64 (glibc) and macOS arm64 (Apple Silicon). The macOS bundle is not Developer ID signed or notarized. Intel Macs, Linux arm64 and Alpine/musl have no qualified bundle. See the [launch guide](../release-bundle.md) for requirements.
- `inlineSTEP` FEA supports the documented single-body imported class and stable imported face identities. Arbitrary imported containment and multi-root assembly-like STEP are rejected explicitly; some OCCT B-spline containment cases remain outside the qualified class.
- The generic tessellated mass verifier can report `Unavailable` for some valid combined analytic Boss/Pocket/hole models when a face cannot be triangulated. STEP reimport, manifold checks, analytic surface inventory, bounds, and route-specific analytic volume remain available; do not interpret an unavailable tessellation estimate as a topology failure.
- Composed profiles admit bounded +Z through counterbore/countersink entries with complete disjoint footprints and positive shaft length. Oriented Compose hole adapters, entry breakouts and chamfer corridors crossing a cavity transition remain explicitly rejected. Sheet Metal Counterbore and Countersink are rejected because those formed-opening semantics are not implemented.
- Composed-body fillets require a cavity-preserving adapter over the existing body. The standalone Profile fillet planner constructs a new extrusion; the compiler rejects applying it to Compose rather than losing existing material features. Disjoint composed perimeter chamfers are supported within their station/corridor limits.
- STEP import normalizes recognized declared length units to millimetres, and the parsed document retains the conversion factor. Public engineering measurements use millimetres; imported topology does not preserve the original unit entity as an editable semantic object.
- Standard Library material resolution is qualified for Firmament FEA and authored Sheet Metal. Ordinary prismatic CAD STEP export does not yet persist a general solid-material designation; do not infer one from the geometry artifact.
- Cadmata may emit one Three.js `Clock` deprecation warning in the browser developer console. It does not affect loading, navigation, selection, PMI interaction, or model switching.
- Canonical STEP byte hashes can differ across operating systems because recovered trim coordinates have tiny floating-point differences. Compare engineering geometry rather than using byte hashes alone for cross-platform CI comparisons; the qualified platforms retain strict separate corpus snapshots.
- Normal validation includes domain-specific engineering preflight. Swept and spline-heavy models can take seconds; parse-only validation is explicitly limited. Expansion source maps are incomplete, so some diagnostics disclose enclosing locations rather than an exact authored token.

docs/public/reference/language/assemblie.title: Assemblies and motion
docs/public/reference/language/assemblie.markdown:
# Assemblies and motion

An assembly lists occurrences of parts and subassemblies and the relationships
that place them. [Lesson 6](../../learn/06-assemblies.md) builds a complete
two-part assembly; the [assembly guides](../../firmament/assemblies.md) cover
stack-ups, reusable subassemblies and keyed component sites.

## Occurrences

The tree is written with `<Assembly>` and `<Part>` tags (brace bodies are also
accepted). Each `<Part Name = Definition<args>>` is one occurrence;
occurrences of the same specialized definition share one exact body. Nesting
describes product structure only. It never creates a mate.

`anchor:` fixes an occurrence in place. A `Placement { from: ...; to: ...; }`
block places an occurrence explicitly: `to: Parent` is relative to the parent
occurrence and `to: World` is the assembly root. See
[assembly authoring](../../firmament/assembly-authoring-foundation.md).

## Ports, interfaces and mates

Parts publish ports with `Semantic` blocks, usually inside `expose`. A port is a
reference such as a `DatumFrame`, `Axis` or `Dimension`, never extra material.

A typed interface family states what two ports must satisfy. Declare a reusable
contract once and apply it with a named `Mate`:

```firmament
Interface<Fixed> Installation { }
// Inside the consuming Assembly:
Mate InstallBracket: Installation {
    A: Machine.Frame.Mount;
    B: Machine.Bracket.Mount;
}
```

Or apply it inline, as in lesson 6:
`Interface<Fixed> Install { a: Machine.Frame.Mount; b: Machine.Bracket.Mount; }`.

- `Fixed` needs ports with datum frames and makes them coincide. `Revolute` and
  `Prismatic` leave one rotation or translation free; they are the joints motion
  can drive.
- `A` and `B` are role names, written as the family declares them. The inline
  form also accepts lowercase `a` and `b`.
- A Mate is applied at compile time. It is not a runtime call.
- Unknown clauses, duplicate assignments and unresolved roles reject.

Older source uses custom `Interface` blocks with `Role ... requires ...` and
`Lower ...` clauses. They still compile, but new relationships should use the
typed families, and `Interface<Custom>` only when explicit low-level relations
are really needed.

## Shared datums and articulated motion

An assembly `Concept Struct` can publish derived three-dimensional frames. Use
`from`, `translateLocal` and `rotateLocal` rather than authoring trigonometric
basis components:

```firmament
Concept Struct Layout {
  DatumFrame Shaft { from: World; translateLocal: [3mm,4mm,5mm] }
  DatumFrame Bank { from: Shaft; rotateLocal: { axis: Z; angle: -45deg } }
  DatumFrame Cam { from: Bank; translateLocal: [0mm,100mm,20mm] }
}
```

A local name such as `Bank` resolves within this Concept Struct. A qualified
name can reference another declared datum. Translation is expressed in the
referenced frame. A sibling `rotateLocal` changes orientation without rotating
that translation; derive an intermediate frame when translation should follow
its rotated basis. Required lengths and angles are dimension checked. Unknown
fields, unresolved sources and datum cycles reject. The existing `DatumFrame`
form with `on`, `at` and `X` on a Plane remains supported.

Reusable Subassemblies retain their local Fixed, Revolute and Prismatic joint
graphs. Occurrences share geometry and own independent coordinates. Exposed
geometric ports follow their actual child occurrence when it moves. At the
compiler API boundary, a nested realized Mate is qualified by occurrence, for
example `Articulated.First.Elbow`; a root Mate keeps its declared name. Names in
motion source address those realized Mates, not the shared Interface type.
Reusable definitions publish their motion coordinates explicitly, for example
`expose { Mate Bend = Elbow; }`. A parent Track uses
`Articulated.First.Bend.angle`; the private local `Elbow` name is not a parent
Motion target. A wrapper can re-export a nested public channel with
`Mate Bend = Unit.Bend;`. These aliases retain the realized Mate's stable ID,
so two public aliases cannot become independent writers for one coordinate.

Declare `Motion` and reusable `Keyframes` in the root Assembly or its module:

```firmament
Motion Cycle {
  duration: 2s
  repeat: Loop
  Track Rotation {
    target: Machine.Crank.angle
    interpolation: Linear
    Keyframe Start { at: 0s; value: 0deg }
    Keyframe Finish { at: 2000ms; value: 720deg }
  }
}
```

This fragment requires an admitted Revolute Mate named `Crank` in `Machine`.
`Time` is a compile-time scalar with `s` and `ms`, normalized to seconds; it can
flow through checked Record fields. Time is distinct from Length and Angle.
A Revolute track writes `angle` in degrees; a Prismatic track writes
`translation` in millimetres. Angles remain unwrapped: 720deg means two turns.
Inline keys use Time, start at zero and end at the declared duration.

Reusable curves declare their domain and value dimensions explicitly:

```firmament
Keyframes<Angle,Length> Lift {
  period: 720deg
  interpolation: Cosine
  Keyframe Rest { at: 0deg; value: 0mm }
  Keyframe Open { at: 360deg; value: 0mm }
  Keyframe Peak { at: 450deg; value: 9mm }
  Keyframe Close { at: 540deg; value: 0mm }
  Keyframe End { at: 720deg; value: 0mm }
}
```

A Track can use `values: Lift` with `input: Machine.Crank.angle`. Input
expressions use the existing typed arithmetic owner; for example, negate the
input for a clockwise crank coordinate or divide an angular coordinate by two.
Reusable Time curves use clip time when input is omitted. Curve domains are
Time or Angle; values are Angle or Length. Interpolation is
explicitly Linear, Hold or Cosine. A periodic curve includes zero and period
keys with equal endpoint values. Without `period`, a curve holds its endpoint
values outside its key domain.

Keys must have unique names and strictly increasing finite domain values.
`repeat: Once` clamps clip time; `repeat: Loop` wraps it, including negative
scrub times, and requires matching physical poses at the clip seam. Compiler
sampling can preserve the final endpoint explicitly. Each independent Mate has
one Track writer per clip. Unknown targets, Fixed targets, conflicting writers,
incorrect dimensions and driver cycles reject with source diagnostics.
Sampling is stateless and retains shared geometry; it does not accumulate the
last frame's transforms.

The complete executable witness is
[`articulated-motion.firmament`](../../../../fixtures/Canonical/AssemblyInterfaces/articulated-motion.firmament).
Inspect or sample it with `aetheris asm inspect` and
`aetheris asm motion <file> --clip Cycle --time 1.25 --json`.

These tracks prescribe admitted rigid joints. They do not yet admit SliderCrank
closure, deform a WireForm spring, export an open Interface contract from a
Subassembly, or create Motion-scoped Patterns. The editable V8 still uses its
existing qualified mechanism adapter for those relationships. A static STEP
export is the compiled engineering configuration; sampling a clip does not
silently replace it with a different posed artifact.


## A complete mechanism

The [editable V8](../../firmament/editable-mechanisms.md) is a complete Inventory/Part/Subassembly/
Assembly/Scene project. Its construction recipes and product structure are authored
Firmament; typed Records carry dimensions and scalar rest inputs. One `Template<config:
CylinderConfig> Subassembly CylinderUnit` is instantiated eight times by keyed
`Pattern` entries derived with immutable `with`. Pattern mapping blocks admit
occurrences with local Concept Struct, Interface and Mate declarations; each key
owns their scope. No per-Part pose tables are required. Assembly
placements bind scalar Static/Record fields through the same checked value owner.
Assembly-owned Semantic datums bind in the owning occurrence; concrete WireForm
winding ports remain available across module boundaries. See the guide for static
Scene versus prescribed-motion limits and the intentional hierarchical identity
change from the old generated flat source.

docs/public/reference/language/checks.md.title: Checks and measurement
docs/public/reference/language/checks.md.markdown:
# Checks and measurement

## What `validate` and `build` check

`validate` runs the full engineering compilation in memory and writes nothing. A
valid result means the part would build. `build` does the same and writes the
artifact. Both evaluate requirements and assertions.

- `--parse-only` stops after static admission and reports `ParsedNotBuilt`. That
  proves the source parses and binds, not that it builds. Domains without a
  static path reject the option as `NotValidated` instead of quietly running a
  full build.
- `--explain` adds developer detail: which front end admitted the file, lexical
  scopes, bound arguments.
- `--json` gives a machine-readable report. See [diagnostics](../diagnostics.md).

Two domains differ:

- **Analysis.** `validate` binds geometry, material, selections and settings and
  reports `BoundNotSolved`; binding does not promise the solver converges.
  `build` (or the dedicated `fea --out-dir`) solves and writes the analysis
  artifacts to the output directory.
- **Drawings.** `validate` and `build` dispatch to the drawing compiler, which
  writes a drawing artifact directory; `drawing compile --out-dir` is the
  dedicated command. [Automatic drawing generation](../../drawings.md) needs a
  supported dimension plan; `--reference-only` explicitly asks for an incomplete
  visualization.

Asking an analysis or drawing build for a `.step` output rejects. Export the
geometry from its own source.

## Assertions

Assertions are available in mechanical parts built from primitives, extruded
Profiles and Compose. Other domains, including Revolve, reject them rather than
accepting the block and ignoring it.

Assertions check the final exported engineering body. They do not alter geometry,
add PMI, or specify a manufacturing tolerance. Normal `validate` and `build` both
enforce them. A failed assertion or an assertion that cannot be verified rejects
the build; it is never a successful build with a hidden `passed: false` result.

**Complete file — exact dimensions and topology:**

```firmament
Model CheckedBox {
    units: mm
    Box Body { size: [10mm, 8mm, 6mm] }
    Assert Volume Body { expected: 480mm^3; tolerance: 0mm^3 }
    Assert Bounds Body {
        min: [-5mm, -4mm, 0mm]
        max: [5mm, 4mm, 6mm]
        tolerance: 0mm
    }
    Assert Topology Body { faces: 6; edges: 12; vertices: 8; shells: 1 }
}
```

`Assert Volume` accepts finite nonnegative `expected` and `tolerance` literals in
`mm^3`, plus an optional string `note`. Exact BRep recognizers take precedence.
Otherwise, a compiler-retained analytic SDF qualified against the exported primitive supplies an adaptive occupied
volume interval. The entire interval must lie inside `expected ± tolerance` to
pass. A disjoint interval fails; an overlapping but inconclusive interval rejects
as **unverified**, including when the deterministic subdivision budget runs out.
The midpoint is an estimate, not an exact volume. Display-mesh mass estimates do
not gate an assertion. A part without an admitted exact recognizer or complete
SDF reports that limitation instead of silently accepting its volume assertion.
The SDF assertion route covers qualified single Box, Cylinder, Cone, Sphere and
Torus primitives, plus complete final-boundary recognition of axis-aligned
rectangular stock with separated circular Z-through holes. This latter path works
for native parts and imported STEP with the same admitted boundary. It requires
one qualified closed material shell and accounts for every face, loop and edge;
an additional unrecognized feature rejects the entire field lowering. A display-only
or legacy Boolean mirror is insufficient evidence that the field matches exported
material, and is not promoted to volume authority.

`Assert Bounds` compares exact world-space minima/maxima, using the optional
nonnegative length `tolerance` (default 0mm). Exact bounds currently cover qualified
rectangular plate/box stock with Z-through holes and planar straight-edge bodies.
It rejects other families rather than treating sampled points or a Boolean field's
conservative enclosing box as the actual extrema. `Assert Topology` checks one or
more nonnegative integer `faces`, `edges`, `vertices`, `shells` counts in the exported
BRep. Counts describe kernel topology, so use them deliberately when topology itself
is the regression contract. All three families accept `note`. Historical PascalCase
field aliases remain accepted; new source uses camelCase.

The target must name the uniquely identified exported product. Requesting an earlier
body in a multi-body program does not measure the last body under the earlier name.
## Tolerance stack-ups

Assembly `Assert ToleranceStackup` checks the worst-case minimum along a unique
dimensional relation path:

```firmament
// Inside an Assembly with these semantic endpoints and dimensional relations:
Assert ToleranceStackup AxialReach {
    between: [BearingModule.FixedSupport.Housing.Datum, BearingModule.Rotor.Shaft.Shoulder]
    require: clearance >= 44.90mm
}
```

The assembly compiler sums nominal values and asymmetric tolerance intervals,
reversing their signs when traversing a relation backwards. Unresolved endpoints,
missing or ambiguous paths, and a minimum below the requirement reject compilation.
This checks declared dimensional relations; it does not infer a tolerance chain
from spatial proximity, perform statistical RSS analysis, or create PMI. Use typed
dimensions and explicit PMI for manufacturing requirements. `Between`, `Require`
and `Clearance` remain compatibility aliases. Unknown or duplicate fields fail.
See [assembly authoring](../../firmament/assembly-authoring-foundation.md).

## Measuring

To discover measured values, including while fixing a failed assertion:

```sh
aetheris measure checked-box.firmament --json
aetheris measure sphere.firmament --sdf --error 50 --compare-mesh --json
```

`measure` admits and builds the geometry but explicitly reports `MeasuredNotAsserted`
and `assertionsEvaluated: false`. It prints measurement methods, volume interval and
uncertainty, exact bounds where available, topology counts, and copyable assertion
templates. `--error` is a requested absolute volume error in mm³, subject to the
bounded work budget (at most 1,000,001 field regions and 30 subdivision levels).
`budgetExhausted` discloses when the requested error could not be reached; the
reported interval remains usable at its actual uncertainty. Suggested tolerances cover numerical uncertainty; select the
design's acceptance range independently. `--compare-mesh` exposes the older mass
estimate for diagnosis, never as a substitute assertion authority.

The default engineering volume path prefers admitted exact BRep formulas, then
bounded SDF integration when the compiler retains a field qualified to represent
the **final exported body**. `--sdf` requests that field path explicitly. A field
for stock before holes or edits is insufficient. Complete rectangular-stock/through-hole
recognition derives its field from the final exported BRep, independently of feature
history. Other STEP imports without a qualified complete field report volume
unavailable; display meshes and sampled point-cloud fields do not silently become
volume authority. This bounded recognizer does not admit slots, blind holes,
counterbores, countersinks, side holes, ribs, blends or arbitrary rotated stock.

For SDF measurements, `fieldQualification` names the evidence family,
`fieldCoveredFaceCount` reports covered final faces, and `fieldSourceStepSha256`
identifies the exact UTF-8 final STEP artifact used by the query. This is an artifact
receipt, including its metadata, rather than a geometry-only identity. Qualification
never comes from merely having a retained display field.

The integrator bounds partially occupied cells using analytic local field envelopes
and plane/box volume integrals. Curvature contributes to the uncertainty; it is not
estimated from a few sample points. Cells crossing unresolved CSG branches, primitive
singularities or unsupported envelope branches retain conservative whole-cell bounds
and subdivide. Thin features cannot disappear merely because their cell corners are
outside. JSON `affineCutRegions` and `intervalFallbackRegions` count visited cells
using each approach, including parents subsequently refined.

These numerical bounds depend on the supported field interval/envelope contract and
finite enclosing bounds. They include floating-point guards, rather than formally
outward-rounded interval arithmetic. They bound occupied volume, not surface-distance
error or manufacturing tolerance.
Cones below the scalar evaluator's supported local generator scale reject bounded
measurement with `sdf-volume-cone-scale-unsupported`; rescale the analytic definition.

SDF integration may be substantially more expensive and less precise than an
available exact formula. Use the returned interval and `budgetExhausted`, rather
than treating the midpoint as an exact value. Mesh export integrity remains a
separate check: a correct field volume does not prove that an STL is closed or
consistently wound.

For assembly values use `aetheris asm inspect assembly.firmament --json`; its
`assemblyIr.toleranceStackups` contains nominal/minimum/maximum, requirement,
pass/fail, and the signed contributor chain. Unlike `measure`, assembly inspection
evaluates declared stackup assertions and returns failure when one fails.

docs/public/reference/language/compatibi.markdown:
# Reading older source

Firmament has been through two generations. Everything in these docs is
Firmament V2. You will still find older source in the repository, in tests that pin
old behaviour, and in files people send you. This page helps you
read it; do not write it.

## Firmament V1

The historical combination `model` with `units mm`, `solid name: Box`, `modify` and `hole<shaft>` are
V1 forms, still accepted for compatibility. Bare lengths inherit millimetres only in the historical
primitive grammar and domain fields that admit them. Length fields in current
mechanical authoring require explicit units. Historical Piping, Structural,
SectionChain and Set positions may accept bare millimetres; WireForm Length
requires a unit. An explicit angle is never a substitute for a length. This is not a second preferred style.

Historical immutable Box derivation uses
`solid tall: stock with { size: [30, 24, 20] }`. Exposure uses
`expose { face(+Z) as top }`, with `=> top` also retained there. These forms do
not make `with`, `as` or `=>` universally interchangeable. Serialization-shaped
V1 `model:` and `firmament:` documents (TOON- or JSON-shaped) are a separate legacy
input with their own compatibility path. Historical JSON-shaped `.firmasm` assembly
files are also legacy; current `.firmasm` uses the V2 assembly syntax.

The formatter preserves names, published members and numeric values. It does
not migrate solid grammar into native declarations or prove a program builds.
Validate the consuming artifact after formatting.

A lowercase `model` wrapping native V2 declarations is a case alias for `Model`;
it does not switch native source into the historical `solid` grammar. Constructs
use PascalCase, built-in fields use camelCase, and connectives such as `using`,
`as`, `on` and `with` use lowercase. Established aliases are normalized at syntax
positions, preserving user-defined names and engineering values.

## Known inconsistencies

Firmament's preferred style is more consistent than what every domain enforces.
Some differences are real domain distinctions; others are compatibility debt or
bugs that are being worked down. You will still meet differences in:

- field casing (older domain examples and some formatters use PascalCase
  aliases; the compiler accepts camelCase everywhere a built-in field is read);
- points written as `Point2(...)` or as lists;
- Pattern element binders (`point =>`, `Item`, `Current`; see [reuse](reuse.md#pattern-finite-repetition));
- statement terminators (some forms require semicolons);
- which declarations may appear at file, Model or Struct scope;
- frame and selector types (`on` means different things in different places);
- what `<...>` and `with` mean in a given position;
- two distinct SectionChain forms, Drawing policy Concepts and Structural table
  column conventions.

Structural, Sculpting, PlasticShell, Analysis, Drawing and Review share the
mechanical parser. Each still owns its statements and fields, and rejects unknown
fields, duplicate aliases, unknown statements and misplaced headers. Structural,
Sculpting and PlasticShell accept predicate and structural `Concept`
declarations and `Require` checks at their product scopes.

Two rules hold regardless:

- **Your names are data.** Record members, Drawing metadata fields such as
  `PartNumber`, Table column names and published ports keep the spelling you
  gave them. The formatter never renames them, and neither should you when
  restyling.
- **Formatting is not migration.** `aetheris format` changes vocabulary spelling
  and layout only. It does not move source to newer forms and does not prove the
  result builds. Validate after formatting.

Lookup is lexical everywhere: Features, product Templates, Records, Statics and
Tables resolve in their declaring scope, callers bind arguments in their own
scope, duplicates in one scope reject, and sibling-private data is invisible.
Source maps through `include` and Template expansion are incomplete;
`validate --json --explain` shows the scopes, bound arguments and
definition/use links the compiler has.

If you find source that is silently ignored, or a documented form that does not
behave as described, that is a bug. Capability limits are listed in
[supported features](../supported-features.md).

Reusable Templates and Features are recipes: material capability and value checks
run on their concrete specializations. An unused recipe does not prove a
supported materialization. Record members and Concept Struct publications are
authored data, not a fixed built-in field vocabulary. Unknown fields in a
materialized built-in construct are errors, including fields inside WireForm
operations, SectionChain guides, assembly occurrences and published Semantic
blocks. `validate --parse-only` reports a limited validation level; normal
validation performs the owning domain admission and required engineering
preflight, which can take time for swept or spline-heavy geometry.

A WireForm part admits one wire product. Its named operations require field
bodies; unsupported placement or parameter headers reject. Use StartFrame for
the authored frame and an Assembly for separate Parts. Comments never contribute
wire operations or operation provenance.

## Admission limits

Normal validation of a mechanical part runs its engineering build. The build
also checks its materialized feature receipts against the admitted operations:
missing Modify or Compose features reject the build. Pattern instances retain
individual identities; one built instance cannot stand in for another.
`build --json` exposes those receipts as `materializedFeatures` separately from
source-derived display reports.

Field closure does not yet cover every value-object body nested in a published
Concept Struct. For example, an extra field inside an inline `Plane { ... }`
value can currently be accepted without affecting that plane. Use only the
listed fields of these value objects; validation does not yet prove that their
entire bodies were consumed. This differs from adding a legitimate new named
member to an open Concept Struct, which is supported authoring data.

Diagnostics for specialized definitions and expanded Pattern instances use the
original field or declaration when it can be mapped. Otherwise they identify
the enclosing material operation or the specialized definition and disclose
that the offsets describe expanded source.

docs/public/reference/language/data-and-.markdown:
# Compile-time data and choices

Firmament data exists only while the compiler runs. Every value is fixed before
geometry is built, and none of it survives into the artifact except as the
dimensions it produced and any PMI you publish explicitly.

## Static values

`Static` binds a name to an immutable value in its scope:

```firmament
Model Plate {
  units: mm
  Static width = 40mm
  Static thickness: Length = width / 8
  Box stock { size: [width, width - 10mm, thickness] }
}
```

`Static width = 40mm` infers `Length`; writing the type, as for `thickness`,
makes intent clearer and is checked. Arithmetic is dimension-checked: adding a
length to an angle is an error. Scalar Statics feed primitive and `Modify` fields
directly, and Compose intervals. Other domains take their inputs through typed
Template parameters instead.

Inside a `Feature`, use `let` for a local derived value. There is no general
`let` outside Feature bodies.

## Records and `with`

A `Record` declares a named data shape with typed fields. A Record value is
data, not a body.

```text
Record PlateSpec { width: Length; depth: Length; thickness: Length }
Static standard: PlateSpec = PlateSpec { width: 80mm depth: 50mm thickness: 8mm }
Static heavy: PlateSpec = standard with { thickness: 12mm }
```

`with` derives a new value with some fields replaced; the original is unchanged.
Overrides are type-checked, and an unknown field is an error. Records may nest,
must be finite and acyclic, and are limited to 128 levels of nesting.
[Lesson 4](../../learn/04-reuse.md) uses these in a complete file.

Record field initializers may carry a tolerance (`diameter: 8mm tol 0.1mm`); see
[requirements](requirements.md#tolerances). Replacing such a field without `tol`
replaces the requirement with an untoleranced value.

## Tables

A `Static Table` holds columns of values for a Record type, typically a range of
standard sizes. Index it to select a row:

```firmament
Record Spec { width: Length }
Static outer: Spec = Spec { width: 10mm }
Model Plate {
  units: mm
  Record Spec { width: Length thickness: Length }
  Static Table choices: Spec {
    width: [30mm, 40mm]
    thickness: [6mm, 8mm]
  }
  Static selected: Spec = choices[1]
  Box stock { size: [selected.width, 20mm, selected.thickness] }
}
```

Rows are typed exactly like literal Records. Tolerances in Table cells and other
collection elements are not supported and reject.

## Scope

Records, Statics and Tables belong to the scope that declares them. A local
declaration shadows the same name in an enclosing scope, and sibling scopes
cannot see each other's names.

Record types are nominal. In the example above, the Model's local `Spec` is a
different type from the file-level `Spec`, even though it reuses the name.
`outer` keeps its own one-field type and does not acquire `thickness`. The Table
uses the local type.

Template defaults resolve where the Template is defined; explicit arguments
resolve where it is invoked. Unknown fields, inaccessible names, duplicate
declarations and cycles reject.

## Choices: `Options` and `match`

`Options` (also spelled `Enum`) declares a set of mutually exclusive cases.
`match` selects one value by case:

```firmament
Model ConfiguredPlate {
  units: mm
  Options SizeChoice { Compact Standard }
  Static size: SizeChoice = Compact
  Static width: Length = match size {
    Compact => 40mm
    Standard => 80mm
  }
  Box stock { size: [width, 20mm, 5mm] }
}
```

The rules:

- **Exhaustive.** Every case, or both `true` and `false` for a Bool, appears
  exactly once. Missing, duplicate and unknown cases reject, even ones that would
  not be selected. There is no default arm, no fallthrough, no guard and no
  payload.
- **Typed.** All arms have the same result type. `Length` and `Angle` cannot
  share a result, and neither can two Record types that merely have identical
  fields. Cases can be qualified (`SizeChoice.Compact`); a case of another Enum
  with the same name is not interchangeable.
- **Lazy.** Only the selected arm is evaluated, so an unselected expression does
  not execute and an unselected spatial value builds no geometry. Names and
  fields in unselected arms are still checked.
- **An expression.** `match` produces a value. It does not conditionally include
  Feature, Part, Mate or Assembly declarations.

A Boolean comparison can be the scrutinee:
`match diameter > 8mm { true => 6mm; false => 4mm }`. Arms may be on separate
lines or separated by semicolons. A selected Record keeps its type, and a
selected toleranced value keeps its tolerance.

`match` is admitted in Static initializers, Record fields, Template inputs,
defaults and bodies, Feature inputs, defaults and locals, and Concept spatial
values such as `Box3` bounds and Grid point sets.

`Options` means one choice among several. It does not mean a set of enabled
flags.

### Older numeric selectors

Existing source may select among collections by count:
`Pattern ... over Match count { 4 => bolts4; 6 => bolts6; 8 => bolts8 }`. This
form is kept for compatibility, checks every arm and rejects an unlisted count.
It is not general integer matching. Use `Options` for new choices and Tables for
standard-value matrices.

## Collections: `Set<T>` and arrays

A choice picks one value; a collection keeps all of them for repetition.

```text
Static mountPoints: Set<Point2> {
  left => Point2(-12mm, 0mm)
  right => Point2(12mm, 0mm)
}
```

Each Set entry has a unique, stable name, and source order is authoritative.
Equal values are allowed. `mountPoints.left` selects one entry. An empty Set
gives zero repetitions.

Arrays (`[a, b, c]`) are ordered and anonymous. Results generated from an array
are numbered by position; results generated from a Set are named after their
keys and keep those names when entries are inserted, removed or reordered.
[Patterns](reuse.md#pattern-finite-repetition) consume both.

docs/public/reference/language/domains-a.markdown:
# Domains and modules

Firmament covers several engineering domains with one syntax. Each domain has its
own compiler front end and its own rules about what is admitted. Sharing syntax
does not make every operation legal everywhere: a field or statement a domain
does not own is rejected there.

## Choosing a domain: `schema`

An optional `schema Name` header selects a front end explicitly. Write it once,
before any other directive or declaration, preferably on its own line. Comments
before or after it are fine. Names are case-sensitive. An unknown name, a second
or late header, or source that does not match the selected domain rejects, and
the compiler does not retry with another front end. A Template specialization
stays in the domain it was admitted to.

| Schema | Guide |
| --- | --- |
| `Mechanical` | [Geometry](../../firmament/geometry.md), [Revolve](../../firmament/revolve.md), [gears](../../firmament/gears.md). Revolve is an operation here, not a schema. |
| `WireForm` | [Formed wire](../../firmament/wire-form.md) |
| `Sweep` | [Circular-section sweeps](../../firmament/sweep.md) |
| `SectionChain` | [Framed section chains](../../firmament/section-chains.md) |
| `Piping` | [Ports, connections and routing](../../firmament/piping.md) |
| `Structural` | [Nodes, straight members and weldments](../../firmament/structural.md) |
| `Sculpting` | [Immutable body and surfacing states](../../firmament/sculpting.md) |
| `PlasticShell` | [Molded shell manufacturing intent](../../firmament/plastic-shell.md) |
| `Analysis` | [Linear-elastic analysis](../../firmament/fea.md) |
| `Garment` | [Panels and stitches](../../experimental/garments/garments.md) (experimental) |

Assembly, Scene, SheetMetal and Drawing are not schemas; each has its own entry
form, described in its guide. Piping uses its documented Model/PipingSystem form,
with `schema Piping` optional. Do not invent `schema Assembly`, and do not wrap
another domain's declarations in a Model.

| Task | Start here |
| --- | --- |
| Parts, ports, constraints, occurrences | [Assemblies](../../firmament/assemblies.md), [components and sites](../../firmament/assembly-components-and-sites.md) |
| Spatial layout and presentation | [Scenes](../../firmament/scenes.md) |
| Sheet parts, regions and bends | [Sheet metal](../../firmament/sheet-metal.md) |
| Engineering annotation | [PMI](../../firmament/pmi.md) |
| Body states and bounded surface edits | [Sculpting](../../firmament/sculpting.md) |
| Multi-file projects | [Project snapshots](../../firmament/project-snapshots.md), [Inventory](../../firmament/inventory.md) |

## Body states

### BodyState: keep an engineering body

`BodyState` can reference the Model's admitted engineering body. It does not
convert that geometry into the old rectangular housing prototype.

**Complete file:**

```firmament
Model Sleeve {
  units: mm
  Cylinder stock { radius: 6mm height: 17mm }
  BodyState base { input: stock }
  output: base
}
```

The ordinary engineering compiler admits `stock`, including its modifications
and explicit PMI. The state retains that exact product, semantic correspondence
where available, and its source recipe for replay. `input` must name an admitted
body or final Compose; it cannot select an unrelated Record, Profile guide or
an intermediate stage of the same construction. Use separate Parts for separate
products, as in ordinary mechanical authoring. Primitive, profile/Compose,
Gear, Sweep and Revolve products retain their existing engineering lowerers.
When adding a state output to a file with an explicit `schema Mechanical`,
select `schema Sculpting` for the state-owning document; an explicit conflicting
selector is still an error.

The older `BodyState base { size: [...] Hole ... }` form remains a housing
construction. Holes are optional. Its named crown and mounting regions belong
to that construction; they are not inferred on arbitrary engineering bodies.
The existing surface-edit materializers still have explicit topology/support
requirements. An unsupported edit or history combination rejects before it can
replace earlier geometry. See the [operation boundaries](../../firmament/sculpting.md).

### Exact face edits and mesh sculpting

`ReplaceRegion` grafts a bounded patch onto an engineering-source
BodyState. Inspect the state for current `FaceN` and `EdgeN` handles, then bind
every patch side explicitly. The supported case is an outward, non-rational
bicubic Bezier graph over a planar four-line face. It retains all topology,
edge curves, vertices and neighboring supports. A replaced face handle becomes
stale; its named SurfacePatch is the successor. Raw STEP PMI that lacks a complete
editable projection rejects before editing. See the complete
[exact-face example](../../../../fixtures/Regression/GenericSculpting/exact-face.firmament).
Imported engineering sources and edits to PMI/interface-bearing faces remain
outside this native adapter's qualified contract.

Use `MeshState` for explicit conversion to an editable subdivision control cage.
It produces a mesh artifact, not an exact BodyState. There is no automatic
mesh fallback when an exact edit fails.

**Complete file — convert a box, soften its creases and edit its cage:**

```firmament
Model CageSculpt {
  units: mm
  Box stock { size: [20mm, 16mm, 8mm] }
  BodyState exact { input: stock }
  MeshState cage {
    input: exact
    cage: Box
    segments: 1
    maximumDeviation: 0.01mm
  }
  MeshState smooth {
    input: cage
    Crease { edges: [All]; mode: Smooth }
  }
  MeshState refined { input: smooth; Subdivide { levels: 2 } }
  MeshState edited {
    input: refined
    preserve: [v1]
    Move { vertices: [v0]; offset: [0mm, 0mm, 1mm] }
  }
  output: edited
}
```

`cage: Box` requires a pure axis-aligned box, and starts with sharp stock edges.
`cage: Sphere` requires a pure exact spherical support; it creates a welded
cube-sphere quad cage. `segments` is 1..16 per cube side (default 1 for Box,
4 for Sphere). Required `maximumDeviation` bounds the finite conversion's
radial error for Sphere, including output quantization; the native Box cage
retains its exact boundary. The same budget limits 32-bit coordinate
quantization for every selected mesh successor. It does not constrain an
explicit Move/Scale to stay near the original body. A tighter
sphere budget may require more segments. This is not arbitrary BRep retopology
or a certificate for the infinite subdivision limit surface.

Each successor has exactly one operation:

| Operation | Fields | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Subdivide` | `levels: 1` | Finite Catmull-Clark refinement, 1..4 levels per operation |
| `Move` | `vertices: [v0]`, `offset: [0mm, 0mm, 1mm]` | Move selected current cage vertices in world space |
| `Scale` | `vertices: [All]`, `factor: [1.5, 1, 0.75]`, `origin: [0mm, 0mm, 0mm]` | Explicit positive scale about a required origin; factors are dimensionless |
| `Crease` | `edges: [All]`, `mode: Sharp` or `Smooth` | Mark or unmark current cage edges as sharp |

Use `inspect --json` for current vertex/edge identities; edge handles are
derived from their endpoint identities. `[All]` is an explicit whole-cage
selection. Existing vertex IDs survive refinement; new edge/face points have
parent-derived IDs. Old edge handles are replaced by their child edges.
Optional `preserve: [v1]` requires those input vertices to retain their exact
coordinates and identities in that successor. A conflict rejects atomically.
There are at most 64 mesh states/operations and 24,576 cage faces.

The [sphere example](../../../../fixtures/Regression/GenericSculpting/sphere-cage.firmament)
uses `Scale` to create an ellipsoid-like subdivision mesh. Its original sphere
remains an unchanged exact BodyState. Mesh states carry their source body,
conversion evidence, typed construction recipe and edit history. Finite meshes
are checked for enclosure, directed winding and local edit foldover. Global
self-intersection is **not certified**; unsupported requirements are errors.

Export a mesh output with `aetheris mesh part.firmament --format glb` or
`--format stl`, or `build --out artifacts/local/part.glb`. GLB is binary glTF 2.0.
Each output has a `.sculpt.json` sidecar with the cage and replayable construction.
STL does not embed those semantics, so retain its sidecar. GLB uses the existing
millimeter/Z-up to meter/Y-up projection and finite, flat-shaded triangles.
Both formats use 32-bit coordinates; export reports quantization and rejects
precision collapse. `validate` reports `MeshBuilt`, `SubdivisionMesh` and
`stepExportAvailable: false`. A normal STEP build of that output rejects;
select the retained exact state as `output` when STEP is required. The existing
STEP-based `view`/`verify` commands explicitly reject mesh-only outputs.

## Modules: `include` and `Inventory`

Use `include bolt: Part = Step("vendor/bolt");` for a short typed resource
reference, or `include "parts/bolt";` when shared declarations are convenient. For
larger compositions, give Part, Subassembly, Assembly and Scene dependencies typed
names in an Inventory Record:

```firmament
Inventory Record Components {
  bracket: Part = Firmament("parts/bracket").Bracket
  drive: Subassembly = Firmament("assemblies/drive").Drive
  bearing: Part = Step("vendor/bearing")
  gearbox: Assembly = Step("vendor/gearbox")
}
```

This fragment requires the named resources. Locators normally omit the extension;
ambiguous matches reject. Place `Components.bracket` through a Part occurrence,
`Components.drive` through an Assembly occurrence, or a Scene entry through a
Scene occurrence. The catalog makes definitions available; occurrences determine
quantity and placement. Part and Subassembly entries may reference typed Template exports; supply their
named arguments at the occurrence. Definition-private names remain in the defining
module. Assembly and Scene entries currently import concrete exports.

Inventory follows lexical scope and retains imported file identity. Existing
untyped `include` remains the concise declaration-composition form. A typed
include follows the same reference rules as an Inventory member. STEP Assembly
imports retain product hierarchy and transforms; no implicit flattening occurs.
Optional `metadata:` selects an ordinary typed Static Record. An optional generated
`firmament.lock.toml` pins dependencies; existing locks are enforced without
automatic refresh. `InlineStep { from: Components.housing }` binds one STEP Part
for local annotation or surgery, with a lock-supplied or explicit source pin.
Use `geometryOnly: true` explicitly when excluding imported PMI. See
[Inventory Records](../../firmament/inventory.md) for complete projects, source snapshots, STEP
boundaries and extension resolution.

Assembly occurrence trees use `<Assembly>` / `<Part>` tags as well as brace
bodies. Tree nesting does not create a Mate. Inclusion is owned by the consuming
project/domain; `include` is **not** a universal mechanical preprocessor.

Standalone part compilation rejects an unresolved include explicitly, even if
the named file exists. Use a documented Assembly/project loader to resolve file
dependencies before part compilation. The shipped `Use Profile.Modifications`
import retains its existing library owner. Other unconsumed directives reject.

docs/public/reference/language/profiles..title: Profiles and 2D construction
docs/public/reference/language/profiles..markdown:
# Profiles and 2D construction

Most parts start as a closed 2D boundary. The pattern is always the same:

1. declare **construction geometry** (guides) that creates no material;
2. trace guides into a **Profile**, closed loops with an inside;
3. give the Profile to a **material consumer** such as `Extrude`, `Compose`,
   `Revolve` or a sheet-metal `Base`.

There is no sketch solver. Positions and sizes are stated, so the boundary is
exactly what the numbers say.

Helios's [IntelliDraft workspace](../../firmament/sketcher.md) follows this same
construction → trace → material workflow. It writes named points, guides and
Path steps into ordinary Firmament source and uses the compiler to resolve them.

## One-line Profiles

A single closed shape can be a Profile directly:

```firmament
Model Plate {
  units: mm
  Profile outline = Rect2 { center: [0mm, 0mm]; size: [80mm, 50mm] }
  Extrude stock { profile: outline; from: 0mm; to: 2mm }
}
```

This uses the same fields and the same exact boundary as a named `Rect2`,
`Circle2`, `Slot2` or other closed shape. `Profile copy = outline` derives an
immutable copy of a named Profile or closed shape.

[Sheet metal](../../firmament/sheet-metal.md) consumes the same named Profiles
for its `Base` and `Cut` operations, within its own limits (a rectangular base,
line and arc cuts).

## Layouts and loops

Use the loop form when a Profile has inner loops, combines several guides, or
needs named edges:

For a shape-driven example, [this independently placed L plate](../../../../fixtures/Regression/IntelliDraft/independent-rectangles-l.firmament)
retains two `Rect2` declarations with their own centers and dimensions. Their
placement makes named corners available for tracing; it does not impose a
persistent relationship between the rectangles. A closed Profile still requires
the selected spans to meet.

For optional explicit dependencies, [this L plate](../../../../fixtures/Regression/IntelliDraft/rectangles-l.firmament)
retains two `Rect2` declarations: an envelope and an inset rectangle whose top
and right edges follow it through shared dimensions. The Profile traces selected
edge spans between their named corners. Changing the envelope or shared wall
input updates the construction and boundary together, without independently
moving six vertices. [Its revision](../../../../fixtures/Regression/IntelliDraft/rectangles-l-revised.firmament)
changes only driving dimensions.

```firmament
Model ProfilePlate {
  units: mm

  Concept Struct layout on XY {
    Rect2 boundary { center: [0mm, 0mm]; size: [30mm, 24mm] }
  }

  Profile outline using layout {
    Loop Outer {
      boundary.Bottom as south
      |> boundary.Right as east
      |> boundary.Top as north
      |> boundary.Left as west
      |> Close
    }
  }

  Extrude stock { profile: outline; from: 0mm; to: 12mm }
}
```

`Loop Outer` is the outside boundary; additional loops such as `Loop Inner` are
holes. [Lesson 2](../../learn/02-profiles.md) shows an outer
polygon with an inner circle.

### Tracing with `|>`

`|>` joins guide segments in source order:

- The first stage sets its own direction; each later stage orients itself to
  continue from the current endpoint. A gap, or a continuation that could go two
  ways, is an error.
- `Reverse` asks for the opposite direction, falling back to whichever direction
  connects after the first stage.
- `Close` checks that the loop closes. It never adds a missing segment.
- `as name` names the resulting edge. Edge names are unique across the whole
  Profile, not per loop; use `as` to tell apart edges that would otherwise share
  a name.
- `guide |> TraceLoop` copies a whole closed guide and fixes its winding for the
  loop it is in. It works for `Rect2`, `Square2`, `RoundedRect2`, `Polygon2`,
  `RegularPolygon2`, closed Paths, `Circle2` and `Ellipse2`. A full circle or
  ellipse stays one boundary segment named after the guide.

To trace only part of a guide, select endpoints by name:

```text
guide from startPoint to endPoint as selectedEdge
```

After the first stage, `guide to endPoint` starts from the previous endpoint.
Endpoints must be named points on that guide. Circular spans work the same way,
and `Reverse` takes the other way round.

`|>` is only for tracing. It is not a general map, filter or function
composition operator. Manual `Segment` declarations remain available for
low-level control.

## 2D shapes

| Shape | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `Point2` | `position` |
| `Line2` | named `from` and `to` points |
| `Arc2` | named `center`, `from` and `to` points; the counter-clockwise arc from `from` to `to`. `to` must lie on the circle through `from`; it is rejected otherwise |
| `CubicBezier2` | named endpoints plus `control1`, `control2` |
| `Rect2` | `center`, `size` (two full lengths) |
| `Square2` | `center`, `size` (one length) |
| `RoundedRect2` | `center`, `size`, `radius` |
| `SmoothRoundedRect2` | `center`, `size`, `cornerExtent`; polynomial corners, not circular fillets |
| `Circle2` | `center` and exactly one of `radius` or `diameter` |
| `Ellipse2` | `center`, `axisLengths` (two full lengths; `axes` also accepted) |
| `Slot2` | `center`, `length`, `width`; `length` is overall, including both round ends, and at least `width` |
| `Triangle2<Equilateral \| Isosceles \| Right \| Explicit>` | variant-specific dimensions |
| `Polygon2<Rhombus \| Parallelogram \| Trapezoid \| Explicit>` | variant-specific dimensions |
| `RegularPolygon2<N>` | regular polygon with a bounded vertex count |

`Point2`, `Line2`, `Arc2` and `CubicBezier2` are open guides; the rest are closed.
Named points on an `Arc2` split it into spans, as on a `Line2`.
Parametric shapes accept `rotation` in degrees.

`Polygon2<Explicit>` takes its corners inline,
`Polygon2 outline { points: [[0mm, 0mm], [40mm, 0mm], [0mm, 20mm]] }`, or from a
named point set with `vertices: points`. Coordinates may use Static arithmetic.
Both forms check winding, duplicate points, self-intersection and non-zero area.
Explicit triangles and polygons do not accept a rotation; rotate the points, or
place a derived Profile with `Curve2`.

Prefer the shape that says what you mean: a `Rect2` for a rectangle, a
`Triangle2` for a triangle, a named polygon variant before a list of points.
`Polygon2<Rhombus>`, for example, takes two full diagonals:

```text
Polygon2<Rhombus> diamond { center: [0mm, 0mm]; diagonals: [90mm, 64mm] }
```

There are no arbitrary 2D Boolean operations. Shape families and variant fields
are listed in full in [closed 2D boundaries](../../firmament/boundaries.md);
[equation curves](../../firmament/equation-curves.md) covers `Curve2` and
`Curve3`; [boundary edits](../../firmament/profile-boundary-edits.md) covers
named tabs and smooth replacements on an existing Profile.

## Planes

A layout's header picks its plane: `on XY` (the default), `on XZ` or `on YZ`.

| Layout | Local axes | Normal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `on XY` | world X, Y | +Z |
| `on XZ` | world X, Z | −Y |
| `on YZ` | world Y, Z | +X |

`Extrude` follows the layout's plane. `Compose` takes its frame from its Base
Profile and requires every Base/Add/Remove operand to share it. On a plane other
than XY, Compose currently rejects Boss, Pocket, Hole, Slot and EdgeFinish,
because their supports are defined in world XY.

The layout plane applies only to that layout's 2D guides. It does not move
unrelated 3D members, and it does not change any other consumer's support.

## Frames and selectors

`XY`, an axis such as `+Z`, a `Plane`, a `DatumFrame` and a published face are
different kinds of reference, and `on` means something different in each place it
appears: a layout plane, a hole's support face, a section frame or an assembly
attachment. Each consumer admits specific reference types. An unsupported
placement rejects; it is never replaced with XY.

Faces have three distinct naming schemes: native named faces, signed primitive
faces such as `face(+Z)`, and imported `#face` references from STEP. They are not
interchangeable. See [STEP import](../../firmament/step-import.md),
[datum seating](../../firmament/datum-seating.md) and
[Concept derivation](../../firmament/concept-derivation.md).

More construction forms: [geometry](../../firmament/geometry.md),
[spans](../../firmament/spans.md), [Revolve](../../firmament/revolve.md).
