reference through the owning AST scope, separately from material outputs. Do not
silently erase ordinary solids when a SurfaceCoil references them.

helios/ai-connections.md.title: Connect an AI collaborator
helios/ai-connections.md.markdown:
# Connect an AI collaborator

AI Author can use your installed Codex client, connect Claude Code or Antigravity native chat through MCP tools, or use an OpenAI, Anthropic or Google API key. Every path works on a separate candidate project, uses the Aetheris compiler to build it, and keeps recovery checkpoints in **Version Control**.

## Use your Codex subscription

1. Install the native Codex CLI and sign in with ChatGPT using `codex login`.
2. Run the [standalone Helios launcher](standalone.md). It opens your browser with a local authenticated session. Source-workspace development hosts use their normal sign-in flow instead.
3. In **AI Author**, select **Installed Codex · ChatGPT subscription**.
4. Expand **AI connection settings**, then select **Test connection**. Choose a model from the installed client's catalog.
5. Describe your change and select **Run agent**. Progress streams into the conversation. **Stop agent** cancels the candidate task.

The connection uses Codex's supported app-server interface. It starts a separate task; it does not attach to a conversation already open in the Codex desktop app. Codex retains ownership of its login and token renewal. Helios does not read or copy its credential files. An API-key account is refused in this mode, and a failed subscription request never switches to API billing.

The model catalog is not a guarantee of account entitlement. A completed task verifies access for that request; subscription quotas and provider policies still apply. This adapter uses experimental Codex dynamic tools, qualified on Windows with CLI `0.164.0-alpha.11.1`. Unsupported client/protocol combinations fail explicitly. Custom OpenAI provider definitions in the Codex profile are refused in subscription mode so a custom API route cannot change its billing behavior.

## Connect Claude Code, Claude Desktop Chat or Antigravity

Your existing desktop client keeps its chat, login, model selection and subscription. Helios supplies candidate editing and engineering tools. No provider credential is copied from the desktop client, and no model request is made by Leviathan in this mode.

1. In **AI Author → Connection**, choose **Claude Code · project workspace**, **Claude Desktop · local MCP**, or **Antigravity · native desktop chat** to match the client you are actually using.
2. Expand **AI connection settings** and select **Prepare desktop connection**. This creates a temporary, local MCP capability; it does not claim to have authenticated your provider account.
3. Select **Copy MCP configuration** and add the `helios` server in your native client, preserving other server entries. Configure the client before starting the task so setup time does not consume the task budget.
4. Check the connection line under the client choice. It reads **connected ✓** once your client has called the Helios server with this pairing.
5. Select **Start desktop task**. Typing the request in Helios is optional: you can leave the box empty and ask in your native chat instead. A recovery checkpoint is saved before candidate access is granted.
6. Ask your client to make the change. The first time, **Copy desktop task prompt** gives a sentence that points it at `task_context`; the agent then uses the Helios tools, builds, and calls `finish_task`.
7. Check the result in Helios. Under **After a successful build**, **Apply right away** (the default) applies the built candidate after saving a checkpoint, and **Undo AI changes** reverts it in one step while nothing else has changed. **Review the diff first** shows the source changes for you to apply or discard.

For **Claude Code**, add the copied entry to the selected workspace's `.mcp.json`. The entry uses `type: "http"`, `url`, and an Authorization header. Open or reload that workspace in Claude Code and enable the server there. This is the Code workspace connection; a browser-hosted Claude connector cannot reach a loopback URL on your computer. See [Claude Code MCP setup](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp).

For ordinary **Claude Desktop Chat**, a project `.mcp.json` is not loaded. Choose **Claude Desktop · local MCP** instead. Merge the generated `helios` entry into the Desktop local MCP configuration through **Settings → Developer → Edit Config** (or the local-server/Extensions section in newer layouts), preserving other entries. Fully restart Claude Desktop and enable the server in a new Chat through **+ → Connectors**. The generated entry launches the local .NET stdio bridge with a temporary Helios capability. This process runs on the desktop computer and forwards MCP calls to the same local tool endpoint; the model's Linux execution environment does not need a route to Windows localhost. See [Claude Desktop local MCP setup](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10949351-getting-started-with-local-mcp-servers-on-claude-desktop).

Do not add this loopback URL as a Claude **remote/cloud connector**: those requests originate from Anthropic's infrastructure. The local Desktop configuration is a different mechanism; availability in Cowork/VM sessions must not be inferred from Chat support. This local-host pass does not add a public tunnel or Cowork plugin. [Network requirements](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-get-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp)

For **Antigravity**, use its MCP settings. In Antigravity IDE, the route is **… → MCP Servers → Manage MCP Servers → View raw config**. Merge the copied `helios` entry into `mcpServers`, then refresh the server. Versions supporting workspace MCP configuration can load `.agents/mcp_config.json`. The generated entry uses `serverUrl` and an Authorization header. See [Antigravity MCP setup](https://www.antigravity.google/docs/mcp).

Antigravity's consumer-plan guidance excludes wrapping its headless CLI inside another application. This connection uses its supported native MCP client: you chat in Antigravity and it calls Helios tools. [Provider guidance](https://antigravity.google/docs/faq)

The pairing lasts up to eight hours, remains in local-host memory, and grants access only while a Helios task is active. It can be reused for later tasks in that browser session. After host restart or expiry, select **Prepare desktop connection** again and refresh the updated configuration in the native client. Treat the copied capability as a local credential; keep it out of source repositories, chat and exports.

**Stop agent** cancels the current task and removes candidate access. **Disconnect desktop** revokes the pairing. Cancelling an in-flight native tool request also rejects the current candidate. HTTP connections launch no native-client processes; your existing desktop applications remain open. Claude Desktop owns the small stdio bridge process: closing its stdin ends that process and disposes the HTTP transport. Stopping an individual task keeps that reusable MCP connection idle. Native-client filesystem and shell permissions remain controlled by that client; the Helios tool server supplies neither.

### What the agent sees

`task_context` returns plain JSON: the task typed in Helios (or a note that the request is in the native chat), the requirements, the project files with their hashes, how Helios will apply the result, the time budget and its end time, and the rules and workflow. Desktop tasks default to a 20-minute budget because the agent reasons between tool calls; when the budget runs out the candidate is discarded.

The tools are built to be read by an agent. `schema` lists every construct with a one-line buildable example; `describe_construct` gives one construct's fields. `edit_file` reports syntax and admission problems for the edited file straight away. `outline` lists declarations with their line numbers and field text. `build` returns a summary rather than viewport data: diagnostics, bounds, each body with its features (holes with their diameters), faces with surface type and diameter, and editable parameters. Use the occurrence and face ids from `build` in `measure`.

When a task has ended, the next tool call says why (finished, cancelled, time budget, page reloaded) and asks the user to start another task, so the agent does not guess.

An idle paired client can discover the tool schema but cannot read project source. `finish_task` requires a successful build of the current candidate; a subsequent source edit invalidates that admission. The final Helios build and source-revision check still run before application. The MCP server never exposes a direct apply-to-working-project tool.

## Configure API keys locally

In **AI connection settings**, select **Open configuration folder**. This creates a commented `helios.toml` template if there is no file. Edit it with your preferred text editor, select **Reload connections**, and select **Test connection** for the chosen provider.

```toml
defaultProvider = "openai"

[providers.openai]
apiKeyEnv = "OPENAI_API_KEY"

[providers.anthropic]
apiKeyEnv = "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"

[providers.gemini]
apiKeyEnv = "GEMINI_API_KEY"

[agents.codex]
executable = "codex"
```

Instead of `apiKeyEnv`, you can write `apiKey = "your actual key"` in the corresponding provider table. Use one field per provider. TOML keys are case-sensitive: `apiKey`, `apiKeyEnv`, `defaultProvider` and `executable`. Unknown fields, malformed TOML and conflicting key fields are errors. On Windows, use forward slashes or a single-quoted literal string for an absolute executable path; select the native `codex.exe`, not a `.cmd` wrapper.

The default location is the operating system's application-data directory under `Aetheris/Helios/helios.toml`. On Windows this is normally `%APPDATA%\Aetheris\Helios\helios.toml`. The UI displays the exact path. Treat the file as a local secret: it is plaintext if you put keys directly in it. Keep it outside design projects and restrict access to your operating-system user. Files created by the host use user-only permissions on Unix.

The local host reads keys; they are never returned to the browser, sent in chat, stored in checkpoints, or included in design exports. **Provider API key** mode uses separately billed API access. Testing an API connection requests the provider's model catalog without requesting inference; a completed task still needs to verify selected-model access and quota.

Explicit TOML provider settings take precedence over host environment credentials. An empty key or an unset variable named by `apiKeyEnv` leaves that provider unconfigured; it does not fall back. Providers omitted from TOML retain support for the host's existing environment credentials. `defaultProvider` selects the initial connection; it does not enable automatic provider fallback. `codex`, `claude-code`, `claude-desktop` and `antigravity` are also admitted defaults. Native-chat modes do not need an executable entry under `agents`.

## Review, apply and recover

All connection modes can read project documents, inspect compiler schemas, edit candidate source, build, measure and prepare review exports through the existing engineering tools. Installed Codex tasks do not inherit shell access or the user's MCP connectors into the candidate workspace. No agent tool directly applies changes to the working project.

Helios saves **Before AI task** before starting work. A changed candidate must build successfully before it can be applied. Choose **Review the diff first** to inspect the source diff before applying; after an automatic application, **Undo AI changes** restores the previous source while nothing else has changed, and the **Before AI task** checkpoint remains for later recovery. The host's transaction status states whether the working project was updated; the agent's final text can describe an earlier candidate state.

Cancelled, disconnected and failed tasks are not applied. Source changes made elsewhere invalidate the running task. Use **Version Control** to restore a checkpoint; restoration keeps the later checkpoints. Browser-local history is not a cloud backup.

## Local host setup for development

Until the Helios desktop launcher is packaged, start the local host from the sibling Leviathan checkout:

```powershell
$env:ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT = 'Development'
$env:HELIOS_LOCAL_AI = 'true'
$env:LEVIATHAN_DATA_DIR = Join-Path $PWD 'artifacts/local/helios-data'
dotnet run --project src/Leviathan.Server --no-launch-profile --urls http://127.0.0.1:5189
```

Then start Helios with `npm run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1`. Register or sign in to the local host using Helios's account screen; local AI currently retains the existing account and active Helios installation checks. It does not bypass cloud authorization.

`HELIOS_CONFIG_FILE` can select another absolute configuration path. `HELIOS_API_URL` changes the Vite development proxy target when the host uses another port. Local AI is opt-in and requires explicit loopback bindings. Host settings, executable launching and subscription connections are refused for non-loopback requests. Do not expose the development UI or local host through a public proxy. A hosted Helios deployment cannot read a visitor's local TOML or run their installed agent.

Related: [project and checkpoint workflow](helios-showcase.md), [export formats](exports.md), [Codex app-server documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server).

helios/branding.md.title: Aetheris Helios knot mark
helios/branding.md.markdown:
# Aetheris Helios knot mark

The logo is an Aetheris-authored torus-knot WireForm, exported as a static binary
glTF (`.glb`). Helios loads that mesh for the welcome-page and header marks. The
browser supplies lighting, a subtle glow and a slow rigid rotation; it does not
generate the knot geometry or run the CAD compiler for the logo.

The [Firmament source](../../fixtures/branding/aetheris-knot.firmament) defines a
single closed (3,5) torus knot with 42 mm major radius, 14 mm minor radius and
6 mm wire diameter. Its scale is arbitrary for this branding use. The
[appearance file](../../fixtures/branding/appearance.json) supplies the warm
yellow-gold metal finish. Studio reflections give the round tube broad highlights
and shaded sides. The source is independent of the original reference image's
authoring code.

To regenerate with a built sibling Aetheris checkout:

```powershell
npm run branding:export
```

`AETHERIS_CLI` can point to another built `aetheris.dll`. The command validates
and inspects the source, exports through `asm export-glb`, then publishes
`public/branding/aetheris-knot.glb` and its source/asset hash receipt. Diagnostic
outputs go under ignored `artifacts/local/branding/`.

The mark makes one turn in roughly 100 seconds. Reduced-motion preferences keep
it still, and hidden or offscreen marks stop animating. If WebGL or the asset is
unavailable, the boxed H remains usable. The product name stays accessible as
ordinary text; the model is decorative.

helios/exports.md.title: Export a model
helios/exports.md.markdown:
# Export a model

Build your model, open **Export**, tick the formats you need, then choose
**Download**. One format downloads directly; several formats download together in
one ZIP. Files use the project root's name, including when a component source file
is open in the editor. The command palette's **Export model…** opens the same picker.

| Format | Part | Assembly | Scene |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| STEP AP242 | Yes | Yes | No |
| glTF / GLB | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| OpenUSD / USDA | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| STL | Qualified closed mesh | No | No |
| OBJ | Supported SurfaceMeshIR geometry | No | No |
| PDF, SVG, PPTX drawing | Supported dimensioned part families | No | No |

Unavailable formats remain visible with an explanation. A supported format can
still reject particular geometry; the compiler's message appears in Problems and
Output. If any selected export fails, no partial ZIP downloads. Uncheck that format
to download the others.

STEP contains the compiled exact engineering geometry and supported semantic PMI.
GLB and USDA contain static presentation geometry at the authored assembly pose,
with hierarchy and supported materials/cameras. They do not export the animation
currently playing, the viewport camera, Concept guides, edge overlays, or selection
highlights. GLB includes the existing millimetre/Z-up to metre/Y-up conversion;
USDA declares its units and axis. STL and OBJ use millimetres; STL has no unit field.

For parts, GLB also carries supported datum/diameter PMI: exact nominal and
upper/lower allowances in `asset.extras.pmi`, associated STEP face references,
and separate font-outline/leader and gold surface-marker primitives. Body mesh buffers remain
unchanged. The metadata schema is `aetheris/pmi-display/1`; values and annotation
coordinates use millimetres before the common GLB axis/unit conversion. This is
presentation metadata, not an AP242 semantic extension. Unsupported callout
kinds or unresolved associations reject annotated GLB export explicitly.
Datum attachments use a small patch inside the selected plane. Diameter attachments
highlight the associated cylindrical wall and physical rim wires, with a leader
ending on the wall rather than inside the solid or at a rim corner. Surface-normal
stems identify the attachments. The default body look is lightly translucent when
PMI is present; explicitly authored appearances remain unchanged. Gold markers do
not intercept face/edge selection and do not alter the STEP or body mesh.
Callout geometry currently uses a static XY plane; orbit to read it, or use the
viewport legend. It is not a camera-facing text system or a production drawing.
USDA, STL and OBJ do not carry PMI.

**Import STEP** opens a supported canonical single part as immutable geometry
with a Firmament annotation layer. Pick a planar face to add a datum, or a
cylindrical face to enter a nominal and explicit upper/lower diameter allowances.
The viewport displays supported callouts and an annotation legend. **Save
workspace** retains STEP text and source in `.helios.zip`; **Open file** reopens
it. Local checkpoints retain assets too. Cloud single-source saving refuses
multi-file workspaces. Arbitrary vendor files, imported assemblies and existing
semantic-PMI layers in an imported STEP are not qualified in this first slice;
they are not silently reconstructed or stripped. Reopen the original workspace
to continue annotation work.

For parts modeled in SolidWorks, the [SolidWorks export add-in](solidworks.md)
uses its ordinary AP214 exporter and the existing Aetheris canonicalization path,
retains the original file, and opens a hash-pinned local annotation workspace.
The add-in validates each part; this does not qualify arbitrary vendor geometry
or existing vendor PMI for direct browser import.

Automatic drawings currently cover rectangular plate/box stock with disjoint
circular Z-through holes. Other shapes fail with a precise drawing diagnostic.
The picker does not bypass this check or substitute reference-only sheets. Drawing
formats share the existing dimension plan and preserve supported AP242 PMI; missing
stock/position/angle tolerances, material and signoffs remain visibly unspecified.
A downloaded drawing is not manufacturing approval. To author those requirements,
use the [Aetheris drawing workflow](../../../Aetheris/docs/public/drawings.md).

If you edited the source, Export first rebuilds the project. A failed build prevents
exporting the retained last-good geometry as if it were the current source. Editing
while files are being prepared also discards that export; build and export again.

Exports run locally through `@aetheris/cad` in the browser's Aetheris worker. No
upload or server conversion is required. DXF and standalone JSON glTF are not
exposed; GLB is the supported glTF 2.0 download.

helios/graph-modeling.md.title: Make a part through the graph
helios/graph-modeling.md.markdown:
# Make a part through the graph

Use the graph to create a block, drill holes, finish edges and export exact
geometry without writing Firmament. No AI connection is needed.

Drag a card by its header to arrange the graph. Positions stay in the open workspace
when you select cards, edit fields, rebuild, or switch views. This changes the graph
layout only; it does not move a physical part or reorder source declarations.
**Auto arrange** restores the automatic layout for the current graph view.
Manual positions reset when the workspace is closed or the page is refreshed.

The **Parts** graph's links display source dependencies. Cards have no draggable
wire ports: use their fields and **+ Add** to author bodies and features. The
**Assembly** graph retains frame-to-frame dragging to create a mate, with the
mate type chosen before applying the compiler-checked edit.

Assembly ports represent named **mate frames**. Drag from the first, fixed frame
to the second, moving frame, then choose a mate type in **Create mate**. The dialog
shows both frame references; dropping on a part card lets you choose its moving
frame. **Preview → Apply** writes the compiler-checked Firmament `Interface<…>`
and mate definition. These connections have physical assembly meaning. Firmament
source remains authoritative for the graph, fields and resulting placement.

For a custom outline, use [IntelliDraft](intellidraft.md): named points and
guides or distance-driven Paths, then Trace and Extrude. **Sketch** retains the
closed-shape dimension workspace for rectangles, circles and slots.

1. Choose **New part**. In **Choose base shape**, keep **Box**, enter Size X = 60,
   Y = 40 and Z = 12 mm, then **Preview → Apply**. The block is centred in X/Y;
   its bottom is at Z = 0.
2. Select the **Body** card. Click **Add hole…** beside its values. Leave **On**
   at +Z for the top face. Set Center X = 8, Y = 4 mm, Diameter = 8 mm, and
   **End → Through all**. **Preview** displays the candidate. **Apply** commits it.
3. Click the hole's row in the Modify card to edit it. Change X, Y and diameter,
   then click **Apply changes** once. **Discard edits** resets unapplied values.
   Changing focus between fields does not rebuild the part.
4. Click **Chamfer…** or **Fillet…**. Keep the top face and Boundary target;
   enter a distance or radius such as 0.5 mm. **Preview → Apply**.

   A Box also supports a whole-face rim finish on the bottom or any side: change
   **Face** before Preview. Rim previews draw the candidate's BRep boundaries
   as gold polylines over the current solid. The solid, source and export remain
   unchanged until **Apply**; **Cancel** removes the gold guides. Interfering or
   unsupported combinations report a compiler diagnostic instead of a preview.
5. Use **Export → STEP AP242 → Download selected format**. **Save source**
   downloads the editable design. Save before closing or refreshing a local tab.

**Counterbored hole…**, **Countersunk hole…** and **Blind hole…** use the same
placement workflow. A blind hole has a **Blind depth** input. In the End control,
you can switch between through and blind termination. **Other expression…**
retains access to parameter references and other compiler-admitted expressions.

Center X/Y are measured in the support face's local frame, from its authored
origin; they are not screen coordinates. **Use picked face** copies a retained,
source-addressable support from the viewport. Unsupported or unmapped faces are
not substituted with another face. **Field help** explains the compiler's fields.

Use **Pocket…** for a finite recess; **+ Add** opens the full catalog. A part has
one material body. Choosing another base replaces that base and checks its
existing downstream features. Use an Assembly for separate parts.

## Drafts, failures and history

A placement preview does not change working source. **Cancel** leaves the
accepted design intact. Editing an existing node and choosing **Apply changes**
changes source and builds it. If that build fails, the last good geometry stays
visible and is marked out of date. The inspector reports the diagnostic and
offers **Revert to last good**. This also resets the displayed fields.

Toolbar **Undo/Redo** reverses complete source transactions and rebuilds. Escape
discards the focused field's pending text; it does not commit it on blur.
During a build or graph refresh, edit controls are temporarily disabled so that
another operation cannot target an older source revision. Apply or discard
unapplied field edits before switching selections.

Unapplied graph fields keep Source, Parameters and other editing operations
unavailable until **Apply changes** or **Discard edits**. Selecting another card
or navigating to its source keeps the current field draft in place. Saving is
also unavailable while these edits are pending, so a download cannot silently
omit the values still shown in the inspector.

The compiler admits supported feature combinations; the graph does not broaden
kernel capabilities. Angular mold Draft is currently a legacy V1 operation and
is not exposed as a V2 graph feature. A saved or failed editing draft is a
different concept. Arbitrary-body fillets and every face/feature combination
are not supported. A rejected preview reports the actual failure.

See [exports](exports.md), [standalone setup](standalone.md) and the
[Firmament language reference](https://github.com/yuechen-li-dev/Aetheris/blob/master/docs/public/reference/language/README.md).

helios/helios-showcase.md.title: Aetheris Helios workspace
helios/helios-showcase.md.markdown:
# Aetheris Helios workspace

The front page is an object catalog: natural Inter lettering, monochrome wireframe
cards on warm paper and short model names. **New part** opens a base-shape chooser with a box starter;
**New assembly** opens an editable two-component starter. Both are browser-local
workspaces with the existing build, source-download and STEP-export paths.
Search or filter, then click a card to open its intact source project. New browsers use
the white **Apollonia** theme; **Dark** switches to the green-and-gold **Bronze Age**
palette. The choice follows you into the editor and is remembered across reloads.

The **Aetheris Helios** hero uses the gold knot mark and Inter lettering. A short statement rolls
up every five seconds, with one line visible at a time. Hover, keyboard focus or
the pause control stops it; reduced-motion preferences keep the first line static.

ATLAS's card uses an explicitly recorded bent-arm presentation pose, evaluated by
Aetheris's assembly kinematics. Opening the canonical example retains its authored
zero pose. The card texture is a subtle presentation overlay; SVG geometry remains
the native topology projection.

Open the root page to browse local examples. No account or backend is required for the showcase. Community discovery and saved account projects remain at `/discover` and `/projects`.

The gallery has independently scrolling **Basic** and **Advanced** rows. Basic contains **Simple bracket** and **Paperclip**; Advanced contains all five original showcase projects. Use a row's arrows, swipe/trackpad, or focus the row and press Left/Right or Home/End. Search matches model details and group names across all rows.

**+ New group** lets you name a personal row and choose its examples. **Edit group** changes its name or membership, or removes it with an Undo option. Groups are saved in this browser and shared between the welcome gallery and the workspace's Examples picker. They organize references to shipped examples; they do not duplicate source or sync to an account.

1. Open **Simple bracket** or **Paperclip** for a small first model, or choose an Advanced project.
2. Use **Graph** to select a body or feature and edit its dimensions, then **Apply changes**. **Source** opens Firmament in Monaco; use **Build** or **Ctrl+Enter** after source edits. See [Make a part through the graph](graph-modeling.md) for a complete no-code block-to-hole workflow.
3. Drag the viewport to orbit, Shift-drag to pan, and scroll to zoom. **F** fits the model. Camera presets and authored Scene cameras are available in the viewport.
4. Use **Files** to browse separate project documents and the compiled hierarchy. **Inspector** shows selected semantic and occurrence data. Clicking a diagnostic navigates to its source when a location is available.
5. Download the active source with **Save source** or **Ctrl+S**. Local documents live only in the current browser session. Multi-file local editing does not add multi-file cloud persistence.

Build always targets the project root, including edits in supporting files. Switching files does not build or discard edits. A failed build retains the last valid geometry and labels it as out of date. Problems show the compiler's actual diagnostic codes and explanations.

### Modeling through the graph

Select a card or one of its rows to open **Selection** below or beside the graph.
Box **Size** has X/Y/Z inputs. Simple `Point2` and `Point3` fields, including hole
**Center**, have coordinate inputs with their authored units. A coordinate supplied
by a named parameter remains a parameter link. More complex expressions remain
text fields; the graph does not turn relationships into fixed numbers.

Use **+ Add** to search bodies, features and contextual construction actions.
New features open a pending placement panel. Choose the host and support, then
set dimensions and Center X/Y. **Use picked face** copies an actual compiler-owned
selector from the viewport. Unmapped display faces cannot be used as source
references. Retained top/bottom faces of qualified plain shaft-hole box stock
are mapped; other construction families can still have unmapped faces.

**Preview** compiles the complete candidate without changing working source.
The viewport labels the preview explicitly; exports are disabled until you
**Apply** or **Cancel**. Apply commits one undoable source transaction. A refused
preview reports the compiler diagnostic and leaves the accepted model intact.
Existing node fields collect edits until **Apply changes**; coordinate components
and dimensions build together. **Discard edits** resets pending values. A refused
applied draft retains the last valid geometry and offers **Revert to last good**.

Select a body for **Replace base…** or **Pocket…**. Replacing a base retains its
name and downstream references, and checks whether those features still work.
Changing shape uses the catalog defaults shown in the panel. Pockets accept an
existing Profile or a new circle/rectangle, and finite depth. Qualified plain
Box or Extrude stock is converted to equivalent Compose stock; unsupported
fields or body combinations are refused rather than discarded.

Select a field-based Hole in Modify for **Pattern…**. Grid counts include the
original seed; row/column keys identify additional occurrences. Select a Profile
for **Extrude…**: this edits the extrusion end while retaining its authored start.
The compiler remains the authority on which combinations can build.

The grid creation action is one Pattern workflow. Existing Function-driven
patterns retain their authored layout and recipe. Navigate **Concept Struct →
Points → Series** to edit literal bounds or the position expression; select a
**Function** card to edit its **Value** expression. These rebuild normally.
Generated features remain read-only projections. There is not yet one inspector
joining the Pattern, layout, law inputs and generated keys.

A current compiler binding gap affects checked Static count/spacing inputs in
part Series, even though assembly Series admits them. **Make count a parameter**
can therefore create a rejected draft there; **Revert to last good** or Undo
recovers it. This is a defect being tracked, not a requirement to freeze design
parameters into literal coordinates.

**New assembly** publishes Bottom/Top frames on its two components. Use **+ Mate**
or drag between published frame ports, then choose fixed and moving frames and
preview the relationship. Apply replaces the moving component's absolute
Placement in the same transaction. **Edit mate…** retargets its endpoints while
retaining the authored contract and options. **Place component…** provides X/Y/Z
translation and one-axis rotation for literal Origin-to-Parent placements.
Named-frame placements, expressions and general matrices remain source-driven;
mate-driven components direct you to their relationship instead.

The **⇡** beside a numeric dimension makes it a named parameter. Change shared
dimensions in **Parameters**. **Delete** asks before removing a declaration.
Toolbar **Undo/Redo**, **Ctrl+Z**, **Ctrl+Shift+Z** and **Ctrl+Y** use the same source
history as Monaco; graph transactions undo in one step and rebuild. In text
fields, normal text editing shortcuts retain their ordinary behavior.
Use **Version Control → Save checkpoint** before a group of edits; **Restore**
keeps a checkpoint of the state being replaced. Checkpoints live in this browser.

For a profile-based part, choose **Sketch**. If the current solid has no editable
Profile, **New sketch part** starts a separate rectangle-and-extrusion document;
keep the current work with Save source or a checkpoint first. In Sketch, edit
Width/Height or drag their handles. **Circular profile opening** can follow a named
rectangle corner or midpoint using inward offsets. **Done** returns to the graph.
Source remains available for compiler features beyond these qualified UI actions.

The **Export** picker offers the formats admitted by the compiled model, including
STEP AP242, GLB and USDA. Scene has no STEP product export. See
[export formats and limits](exports.md), including supported datum/diameter PMI
labels and tolerance metadata in GLB. **Import STEP** opens the supported
canonical single-part annotation workflow; **Open file** also reopens portable
`.helios.zip` workspaces containing source and immutable STEP assets.

Drag pane separators or focus them and use arrow keys. The utility dock and bottom panel can collapse. **Ctrl+Shift+P** opens the command palette, which includes formatting and existing source-authoring actions. The terminal is available only on the local Vite development host, and starts when its tab is opened.

Inter is bundled locally and used throughout the workspace, source editor and terminal. **Wrap** above the source editor, or **Alt+Z** while editing, toggles word wrap. That preference is remembered in this browser. Long unwrapped lines scroll horizontally; the vertical scrollbar has its own opaque gutter.

**AI Author** is separate from **Version Control**. Provider configuration is required
for AI authoring; ordinary graph editing, builds, checkpoints and local exports do
not require an AI provider. Spatial examples demonstrate static authoring and
interchange, not factory automation or manufacturing simulation.


A separate Function parameter-shadowing defect can admit incorrect equation
results when a module Static has the same name as a Function parameter. This
needs compiler binding repair before broader equation-pattern editing is exposed;
successful validation alone does not rule out this known counterexample.


### Source-preserving Patterns

Use **Patterns…** in the graph construction menu to reopen a finite Pattern,
its layout, shared law inputs and recipe. New applications can use an existing
keyed collection, equation Series or named stations. Preview builds the complete
candidate project; Apply commits one undoable transaction. Evaluated keys and
expansion associations are read-only. The gold Point2 plot is explicitly local
layout space; it does not guess the recipe's support frame.

Use **Grid seed hole…** for the separate rectangular Hole helper (counts include
the seed). Legacy radial/linear forms remain supported by their domain compiler;
the finite-layout panel explains when it has no visual adapter. Imported laws
remain in their source file; open that file to edit them.

helios/intellidraft.md.title: IntelliDraft
helios/intellidraft.md.markdown:
# IntelliDraft

IntelliDraft draws rectangles, circles, ellipses, slots and rounded rectangles as retained construction shapes, then traces a material Profile from their boundaries. A rectangle retains its exact size, right angles and parallel opposite sides. Each shape has its own placement. Temporary alignment guides help you position shapes without creating persistent relationships or a constraint solver.

Open **IntelliDraft** above the viewport. It edits an existing profile-based part when available; **New profile part** starts a separate draft. Otherwise it starts a new construction layout. The current part stays unchanged until **Build and use part** succeeds.

## Shape list and drawing tools

The sidebar has a searchable, independently scrollable **Shapes** list. Select a row to inspect that shape, even when shapes overlap on the canvas. The list remains available while tracing.

Each row's checkmark controls **construction visibility in this workspace**. Uncheck it to hide the shape and exclude it from picking and alignment targets; check it to show it again. **Show all** restores the construction. This is display suppression, not deletion or a conditional build: source, existing traced Profiles and exported geometry stay unchanged. Selecting a hidden row does not reveal it. Visibility resets when the IntelliDraft workspace closes.

Use **Draw rectangle**, **Draw ellipse**, **Draw slot**, or **Draw rounded rectangle**, then drag between two corners. **Draw circle** takes two clicks: center, then a point that sets the radius. **Draw arc** (in the Circle type menu, or **A**) takes three clicks: center, arc start, arc end. Arcs run counter-clockwise from start to end; the end stays on the selected radius. Enter exact shape dimensions in the inspector afterward, or fill the creation fields and choose **Add shape** (**Add Rectangle** for a rectangle).

While drawing or moving a shape, the canvas shows a temporary preview. Finishing
the gesture submits one edit to the compiler; it does not rebuild for every mouse
movement. **Esc** cancels a drag. Middle-button dragging pans the canvas.

| Tool | Retained type | Exact inputs |
|---|---|---|
| Rectangle | `Rect2` | Width, height, center |
| Circle | `Circle2` | Radius, center |
| Ellipse | `Ellipse2` | Two full axis lengths, center |
| Slot | `Slot2` | Overall length including both round ends, width, rotation, center |
| Rounded rectangle | `RoundedRect2` | Width, height, corner radius, center |

A circle's radius is the distance from its first click to its second, including a horizontal or vertical radius. A slot's longer dragged extent becomes its overall length; a vertically drawn slot keeps that orientation. A rounded rectangle starts with a radius one eighth of the smaller extent; edit it through **Radius**. Invalid slot dimensions or an oversized corner radius are rejected by the compiler.

In **Draw**, choose **Select** (**V**) and drag a shape's body or a line, arc, or axis directly. Lines and arcs translate their defining named points together in one undoable edit; shared points remain shared. Expression-driven placements retain their expressions. **Trace** and **Extrude** lock construction movement and dimensions. Selecting a row in those stages does not unlock it: return to **Draw** to edit. Escape cancels a pending center/radius/arc gesture; changing tools also discards its preview.

### Select and move a group

Choose **Group select** (**G**). Drag a box that fully encloses the elements to
select, click their sidebar rows, or use **Select all construction**. **Shift-click**
adds or removes an element; holding Shift while boxing adds the enclosed elements.
**Clear group selection** empties the selection. Infinite axes can be selected
through their rows. Hidden construction is excluded from Select all and boxing.

Drag a selected element to move the selection together, or enter exact **Move X/Y**
distances and choose **Move selection**. This is one translation and one Undo step:
shared named points and shared placement parameters move once. It creates no
persistent group or relationship in Firmament. A shared driving parameter also
affects its other dependants. Elements must belong to one layout.
A driven placement, conflicting shared parameter, or invalid resulting Profile
refuses the complete move and preserves the preceding source. Group movement is
available in **Draw**; return there from Trace or Extrude to change construction.

### Inspect a guide

Select a line, arc, named circle or axis in **Draw** to open its **Guide inspector**.
Lines expose Start/End X/Y, axes expose Origin X/Y, and arcs and circles expose
Center X/Y and Radius. **Apply guide dimensions** submits one source transaction;
**Discard guide edits** restores the current values. Apply or discard before
changing tools or building. Undo and Redo refresh the displayed coordinates.

Changing an arc's radius keeps its center, endpoint angles and sweep fixed. A
center change translates it; both operations keep it circular. Shared endpoints
remain shared, so a connected line can change when the arc radius changes. The
compiler refuses an invalid result. Guides with driven or unsupported inputs show
read-only guidance to edit their defining source inputs.

In **Trace**, select the construction shape. **Use whole shape outline** traces a complete circle, ellipse, slot or rounded rectangle. Rectangles also offer named landmark spans as described below. Existing **Manual guide trace** exposes the compiler's named boundary guides for more detailed selection; curved span trimming uses its existing named-point controls rather than inventing intersection points.

## Draw, dimension, place, repeat, trace

The complete reference program is Aetheris's `fixtures/Regression/IntelliDraft/independent-rectangles-l.firmament`.

1. Name the layout `layout`, choose **XY**, then **Add Layout**.
2. Name the first rectangle `outer`. Drag between two corners on the canvas to draw it. Enter exact **Width = 60 mm**, **Height = 40 mm**, then **Apply shape dimensions**. **Placement** lets you enter an exact center; use **Center X/Y = 0 mm** for this example. Alternatively, fill these values before choosing **Add Rectangle**.
3. Choose **Draw rectangle**, name it `notch`, and draw the second rectangle. Set its exact **Width = 52 mm**, **Height = 32 mm**, then apply.
4. Drag the second rectangle until its top and right edges align with the first. Pink guides indicate nearby edge or center alignment. Release to store its placement: **Center X/Y = 4 mm** in this example. You can verify or enter these values under **Placement**.

The placement is a number, not a relationship. Moving or resizing `outer` later does not pull `notch` along. The rectangles retain their own shape properties; the source does not acquire a hidden mate or an expression linking the two shapes.

**Hold Alt while dragging** to bypass alignment. **Escape** cancels the active gesture without closing the workspace or changing source. Pointer cancellation also abandons the preview. Drawing corners and unsnapped dragging use 0.1 mm authoring increments; an alignment uses the projected target position exactly. This increment is not a declared manufacturing tolerance. Explicit numeric fields can use finer precision.

**Fit construction**, **+ / −**, and middle-button dragging navigate the canvas. Click a shape card to inspect its dimensions. Overlapping shapes can be selected through their cards; dragging the visible body uses the topmost shape under the pointer.

Thin centerlines mark the drawing axes, with a small origin mark and positive
direction arrows. Their labels follow the layout plane (for example, X/Z), and
their weight and label size stay constant while zooming. They are reference
graphics and do not create construction geometry.

5. Choose **Trace**. Select a **Trace shape**, then click these spans in boundary order:

| Shape | Selected span |
|---|---|
| outer | Entire bottom edge |
| outer | Right edge below the notch's bottom-right corner |
| notch | Bottom edge |
| notch | Left edge |
| outer | Top edge left of the notch's top-left corner |
| outer | Entire left edge |

Named corners supply the endpoints. You do not author six points or six Line2 declarations. Connected spans follow the preceding span; selected pieces stay dark while the gold construction remains visible. **Available boundary spans** offers the same choices as accessible buttons.

6. Choose **Trace Profile**, leave **Extrusion depth = 6 mm**, then **Extrude Profile** and **Build and use part**.

The L occupies X=-30–30 mm, Y=-20–20 mm and Z=0–6 mm, with nominal volume 4,416 mm³. For a single rectangle, **Use whole rectangle outline** replaces span-by-span selection.

## Exact inputs and transactions

Drawing and dragging preview locally, then submit one compiler-owned source transaction on release. Dimension fields require **Apply** or **Discard** before switching editors, tools or building. Independent dimensions remain writable; expression-driven dimensions show their authored expressions and remain read-only. Dragging never replaces an explicit expression with a number.

**Undo** and **Redo** navigate staged source transactions. **Cancel** discards the staged draft. Save source or create a checkpoint before closing or refreshing a local browser tab. A complete candidate must pass normal engineering build admission before replacing the current document.

After extruding, **Extrude** keeps the current **Extrusion end height** available,
including when reopening an existing part. It is measured along the layout normal
from the same origin as the displayed start height. Choose **Update extrusion**
to apply the new end height, or **Discard extrusion edits** to restore it.
Unapplied height changes disable building and stage changes. Expression-driven
end heights remain read-only; edit their driving parameter or source instead.
Update stages the construction change; **Build and use part** performs the full
solid check. A failed solid build keeps the draft open for correction.

A traced Profile must remain closed and valid. A move that breaks an existing Profile is refused with the compiler's diagnostic and leaves the preceding candidate intact; another shape is never moved to repair it. Correct the placement or use Trace to select a different valid boundary. **Close** verifies closure and never invents a missing segment.

## Explicit dependencies are optional

Under **Advanced: explicit expression relationship**, **Add related rectangle** intentionally creates a dimension-driven top-right inset with a shared wall or separate insets. This is an explicit source expression workflow, separate from independent placement. Its values remain editable through their driving inputs. Ordinary dragging and alignment never select this behavior implicitly.

Existing references `rectangles-l.firmament` and `rectangles-l-revised.firmament` demonstrate those optional explicit dependencies.

## Advanced construction and limits

The drawing palette creates retained closed shapes plus Line2, Arc2 and Axis2 construction guides. Shapes whose compiler-projected center controls are independently writable can be moved; positions driven by expressions retain their inputs. Guide drags require literal positions for all defining points (or an axis origin); the compiler still rejects moves that break an arc or an existing traced Profile. **Advanced: points, lines and Paths** retains named Point2/Line2/Circle2 guides and ordered line/arc Path steps. Legacy named-circle spans use named endpoints. Paths use distances, radii and signed turns; **Close Path with line** explicitly adds a closing line. Existing slot and rounded-rectangle dimensions and circular profile openings remain available through **Sketch**.

Layouts support XY, XZ and YZ; UI-created Paths use XY. Alignment considers shapes in the same layout, using compiler-projected bounds. It is temporary positioning assistance, not general geometric inference. Trace uses existing named landmarks. Arbitrary intersection creation, new inner-loop assembly, arbitrary trim/extend and freeform curve editing are not implemented.

The canvas samples compiler-resolved curves for display only. Geometry, admissibility and source provenance remain compiler-owned. Included/generated geometry does not become writable by flattening its expansion.

Related: [graph modeling](graph-modeling.md), [exports](exports.md).

helios/learning.md.title: Learn Firmament in Helios
helios/learning.md.markdown:
# Learn Firmament in Helios

Build a part while you learn. Open **Learn** in the header, or press **F1**, to browse this manual, the full Firmament language reference, and six guided lessons. Documentation is bundled with Helios and remains available without a documentation server.

## Your first part

1. Open [A first part](../../docs/public/learn/01-first-part.md) and choose **Practice in new tab**. Your current workspace stays open.
2. Helios opens the complete plate example in the Source editor and builds it with Aetheris. The **Tutorial** panel stays beside the viewport.
3. Drag in the viewport to orbit. Scroll to zoom. Press **F** outside the editor to fit the part, or use **Fit** above the viewport.
4. Change `diameter: 8mm` to `diameter: 12mm`. Press **Ctrl+Enter** (or **Cmd+Enter**) to build. Live red underlines check the source; a successful Build updates the geometry.
5. Use **Save source** to keep your work. Use **Export** to download the formats available for that model, including exact STEP AP242 and GLB where supported.

The guided checklist records your own progress on this device. Its build step is enabled only when the current source has a successful build. Other steps are self-checks: inspect the model and make the suggested edit before marking them complete. You can reset a lesson's checklist without changing its source.

## Six lessons

The [Firmament course](../../docs/public/learn/README.md) progresses from stock and holes through profiles, manufacturing features, reuse, PMI and checks, and assemblies with explicit interfaces. Each new practice workspace starts from the complete canonical example. Save your edited source before closing or reloading a practice tab; the checklist and the source are saved separately. Examples and reference pages follow Aetheris's current public manual.

The lessons also show CLI commands for validation, measurement and inspection. Run those commands in an installed Aetheris CLI. In Helios, use live diagnostics and **Build** for the editor loop. Code blocks labeled `sh` contain shell commands; blocks labeled `firmament` contain model source.

## Finding an answer

Search titles and page contents from **Learn**. Search terms are combined, so `hole counterbore` narrows the results. The contents rail jumps to headings within a page. Internal documentation links stay in the manual; source examples open in a source viewer where you can copy or download them. Examples that need companion files or imported geometry should be opened as a complete project, not pasted as isolated fragments.

Start with the [language reference](../../docs/public/reference/language/README.md) for syntax and fields, [modeling guides](../../docs/public/README.md#guides) for a particular feature, and [known issues](../../docs/public/reference/known-issues.md) for current boundaries. Experimental pages are marked as experimental. The compiler is the authority when it rejects a combination.

## Working in the editor

| Action | Shortcut |
|---|---|
| Learn and reference | F1 |
| Command palette | Ctrl+Shift+P / Cmd+Shift+P |
| Build | Ctrl+Enter / Cmd+Enter |
| Save | Ctrl+S / Cmd+S |
| Completion | Ctrl+Space |
| Format document | Shift+Alt+F |
| Next diagnostic | F8 |
| Go to definition | F12 |

Source is the model's authority. The graph is a structured editing view of that source, with explicit ports and Mates. See [graph modeling](graph-modeling.md), [IntelliDraft](intellidraft.md), [STEP and SolidWorks import](solidworks.md), and [export formats](exports.md) for the other Helios workflows.

helios/solidworks.md.title: SolidWorks → Aetheris Helios
helios/solidworks.md.markdown:
# SolidWorks → Aetheris Helios

Model a single solid part in SolidWorks, then use **Export to Aetheris Helios**
to open a local annotation workspace. The command uses the ordinary AP214
exporter. It does not call SolidWorks MBD, reconstruct feature history, or read
native files with a separate parser.

## Build and install

On Windows, install SolidWorks, the .NET SDK and .NET Framework 4.8 targeting
pack, and build the sibling Aetheris CLI. Start the local Helios application.
From this repository:

```powershell
./scripts/Build-SolidWorks.ps1 -HeliosUrl http://127.0.0.1:4173
```

The script locates the running SolidWorks installation's interop assemblies.
Alternatively pass `-SolidWorksInteropDir` pointing at its `api/redist` folder.
Use `-OutputDirectory` to stage an update in a separate directory when a running
SolidWorks session retains the previous managed DLL.
Use `-AetherisCli` to select an Aetheris executable or DLL. DLL execution needs
the corresponding .NET runtime. Output is under
`artifacts/local/solidworks/addin/`; keep that directory in place after registration.

1. As the normal SolidWorks user, run
   `./artifacts/local/solidworks/addin/Helios.SolidWorks.Cli.exe --register`.
2. Once, in an administrator PowerShell, run that executable with
   `--register-machine`. This installs this add-in's managed COM entries under
   `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Classes` and its discovery entry under
   `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\SolidWorks\Addins`. It changes only Helios'
   CLSID/ProgID and discovery entries.
3. As the normal user, run the executable with `--load`. The **Aetheris Helios**
   command tab/menu contains **Export to Aetheris Helios**. Loading at Windows
   or SolidWorks startup is not configured.

The loader checks the actual connected add-in object; a zero `LoadAddIn` status
alone does not establish success. Full machine COM registration allowed loading
in the already-running SolidWorks session without a restart.
`addin.log` beside the DLL records construction, connection and connection errors.
Use `--registration-status` without administrator privileges to inspect the
machine discovery/COM entries and registered DLL paths. Builds before 0.1.7
installed only machine discovery; rerun the administrator step with a current
build to install the missing managed COM entry.

`helios-solidworks.json` beside the DLL contains `HeliosUrl`, `AetherisCli`, and
`ExportDirectory`. The default export directory is Documents/Aetheris Helios/Exports.
The Helios URL must be an HTTP origin at `127.0.0.1` with the port of your local
Helios application. Remote handoff targets are rejected. Start Helios before exporting.

Unload with `--unload` before updating the add-in. SolidWorks may retain managed
assemblies until it exits; save your work and restart SolidWorks before replacing
a loaded build. To uninstall, run `--unregister-machine` as administrator and
`--unregister` as the normal user. These remove only this add-in's registration.

## Export and annotate

Finish any sketch. The command requires exactly
one solid body. It exports the complete active configuration, restores the
previous selection and STEP export settings, and asks Aetheris to import and canonicalize the
geometry. Unsupported geometry is refused with the original AP214 retained for
inspection. No file is overwritten: each export gets its own directory.

The generated `.helios.zip` contains the untouched AP214, Aetheris's canonical
STEP, and a Firmament annotation root pinned to that canonical asset's SHA-256.
A two-minute, one-use loopback transfer opens it in Helios. The transfer accepts
only the configured Helios origin and an unpredictable capability URL; it closes
after delivery or timeout. There is no installed transfer service. If the browser
handoff fails, use **Open file** in Helios to open the saved workspace.

Pick a planar face and add a datum. Pick a cylindrical face to add a nominal
diameter and explicit upper/lower allowances. These requirements become part of
the Firmament layer; geometry stays unchanged. Choose **Export → STEP AP242**
and/or **GLB** to retain supported engineering semantics and 3D callouts. **Save
workspace** retains the original assets and annotations for reopening.
See [export formats and limits](exports.md).

Re-exporting after a SolidWorks geometry change creates a new workspace. Existing
face attachments are not guessed onto a new snapshot. Imported-geometry repair,
general dimension/GD&T authoring, assemblies and automatic PMI extraction from
SolidWorks are outside this initial command's scope. Supported geometry is
determined by Aetheris admission, not by the presence of a STEP file extension.

## Local tools for agents

The same executable provides a stdio MCP interface. It attaches to a running
SolidWorks session through its ordinary COM API. It also works without the
button's administrator registration. Example client configuration:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "solidworks-local": {
      "command": "C:\\path\\to\\Helios.SolidWorks.Cli.exe",
      "args": ["--stdio"]
    }
  }
}
```

| Tool | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `solidworks_inspect` | Active part/configuration, features, linear dimensions and volume |
| `solidworks_create_part` | New rectangle, circle or annulus sketch with a blind extrusion |
| `solidworks_set_dimension` | Edit an existing linear dimension and rebuild the current configuration |
| `solidworks_rebuild` | Rebuild without saving the native document |
| `solidworks_export` | Export the inspected part; optionally open local Helios |

Dimension edits require the document token and expected previous value returned
by inspection. A stale document/configuration or value is refused. A failed
rebuild attempts to restore the previous dimension and reports the failure.
The tools do not save over native documents, run arbitrary code, execute shell
commands, or offer a network command endpoint. Creation leaves a separate new
document open and preserves existing documents.

For command-line clients, `--call request.json` accepts the same operations:

```json
{"operation":"create_part","profile":"annulus","outerDiameterMm":40,"innerDiameterMm":10,"depthMm":8}
```

For interchange diagnostics, `--verify-step part.step` imports a STEP into a
separate temporary SolidWorks document, reports its solid count and volume, and
closes that test document without saving. It refuses a file already open by path.

The integration has no model-upload or telemetry path. Geometry conversion runs
locally. MCP results are supplied to the agent client you configure; a cloud AI
client may transmit those results according to its own settings. SolidWorks'
own cloud-connected behavior is independent of this add-in.

helios/standalone.md.title: Run Helios on your computer
helios/standalone.md.markdown:
# Run Helios on your computer

The standalone preview combines Helios, its CAD browser runtime, and a local
Leviathan host. It opens your installed browser instead of installing another
Chromium runtime. No developer tools or cloud account are needed to model parts.

1. Download the archive for your platform from
   [Helios releases](https://github.com/yuechen-li-dev/HeliosCAD/releases).
2. Extract the whole archive. Run **Helios.exe** on Windows or `./Helios` from
   a terminal on Linux/macOS. Keep the companion files beside the launcher.
3. Choose **New part**, **New assembly**, or a gallery example. Use the graph or
   Firmament source, then **Build**. Open existing source/workspaces or supported
   STEP parts with **Open file**.
   For a first part, follow [Make a part through the graph](graph-modeling.md).
4. Use **Export** for the formats available on that model. **Save source**
   downloads source or a portable workspace. **My projects** stores projects in
   this computer's local database. Saved projects currently support one source
   document; use **Save workspace** for projects with includes or STEP assets.
5. Save your work, then choose **Quit Helios**, close the launcher window, or
   press Ctrl+C. Closing a browser tab alone leaves the host running. Starting
   the launcher again opens the existing local host instead of duplicating it.
   Quit the old host before starting an updated bundle; otherwise you reconnect
   to the version that is already running.

The host uses `http://127.0.0.1:4180` and is loopback-only. A launch capability
opens your local identity; there is no registration step. Keep this port stable:
browser checkpoints belong to that origin and browser profile. **Version
Control** checkpoints survive host restarts but are lost if browser site data is
cleared. Download source and maintain backups; checkpoints are not cloud saves.

The launcher prints its local data directory. Windows normally uses
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Aetheris\Helios`; macOS uses
`~/Library/Application Support/Aetheris/Helios`; Linux uses
`$XDG_DATA_HOME/Aetheris/Helios` or `~/.local/share/Aetheris/Helios`.
These follow [.NET's platform application-data locations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/compatibility/core-libraries/8.0/getfolderpath-unix).
The database, object storage,
identity keys, and `logs/helios.log` live there, outside the extracted package.
Updating the bundle does not erase them.

## Optional AI

Modeling works without AI. The local profile also enables **AI Author** with
installed native agent subscriptions or local provider keys in `helios.toml`.
Use **AI connection settings → Open configuration folder** to find that file.
See [AI connections](ai-connections.md) for the separate Codex, Claude Code,
Claude Desktop Chat, Antigravity and provider API setup paths. Helios does not
install those clients, sign in to them, or certify their account entitlements.

## Preview limits

The package is unsigned and has no installer or automatic updater. SmartScreen
or Gatekeeper may prompt. A modern Chrome/Edge browser is the primary browser
qualification target. There is no embedded native window, bundled browser, or
development terminal in this preview.

If port 4180 is occupied, Helios stops with a diagnostic instead of moving your
browser history to another origin. You can explicitly run `Helios --port 4183`
and keep that port for subsequent launches. `--data-dir <directory>` chooses a
different local data directory. `--no-browser` supports automated qualification;
an unauthenticated tab does not gain API access by visiting localhost.

The local server is not a LAN service. Keep the printed launch capability and
local data private; do not expose or proxy the host publicly. Provider requests
send the candidate project context to your chosen provider/native agent only
when you start an AI task. Local saved projects do not synchronize with a hosted
Helios account. Check the package README and release notes for platform-specific
qualification and limitations.
